stem: A development team uses AWS CodePipeline to deploy a microservices application to Amazon ECS. The team wants to implement a blue/green deployment strategy that automatically rolls back if the new version's error rate exceeds 5% during a 10-minute evaluation period. Which configuration achieves this requirement?

options.text: Configure CodePipeline to deploy a new ECS service behind a separate target group. Use an Application Load Balancer listener rule with weighted routing and a Step Functions workflow that monitors CloudWatch error metrics and shifts DNS weights.

Configure CodePipeline with an ECS rolling update deployment action. Create a CloudWatch composite alarm combining 5xx error rate and latency metrics, then use an EventBridge rule to trigger a Lambda function that calls the ECS UpdateService API to revert.

Configure CodePipeline with a CodeDeploy EC2 in-place deployment action. Attach a CloudWatch alarm on the Application Load Balancer TargetResponseTime metric and enable CodeDeploy automatic rollback on alarm state to revert to the previous task definition.

Configure CodePipeline with a CodeDeploy ECS blue/green deployment action. Set up a CloudWatch alarm monitoring HTTP 5xx error rate with a 5% threshold and attach the alarm to CodeDeploy's automatic rollback configuration for deployment monitoring.

explanation: CodeDeploy natively supports ECS blue/green deployments with CloudWatch alarm-based automatic rollback. Option B uses ECS rolling updates, which don't support blue/green deployment. Option C targets EC2 in-place deployments, not ECS. Option D requires custom orchestration and DNS-based shifting instead of using CodeDeploy's built-in capability.

stem: A company manages infrastructure across 15 AWS accounts using AWS CloudFormation. Engineers occasionally make manual console changes that cause stack drift. The company wants to detect drift automatically and alert the team, while still allowing emergency changes with proper documentation. Which approach BEST addresses this?

options.text: Use CloudTrail to log all API calls and create EventBridge rules that match resource modification events. Compare events against CloudFormation change sets using a Lambda function and notify via SNS when unmanaged changes occur.

Enable AWS Config rules to detect CloudFormation stack drift on a schedule. Use an SNS topic to notify the team when drift is detected, and require engineers to tag emergency changes with a change request ID for audit tracking.

Schedule a Lambda function to call the CloudFormation DetectStackDrift API for all stacks hourly. Publish drift results to an SNS topic, and implement an SCP that denies all resource modifications except through CloudFormation service principal.

Deploy AWS Config with the cloudformation-stack-drift-detection-check managed rule across all accounts via AWS Organizations. Send non-compliant findings to a centralized SNS topic and use SCP exemption with a condition key for emergency roles.

explanation: AWS Config's managed rule cloudformation-stack-drift-detection-check provides native multi-account drift detection via Organizations. Combined with SCP exemptions for emergency roles, this balances drift prevention with emergency access. Option A detects drift but lacks the multi-account organizational deployment. Option B's hard SCP deny blocks emergency changes entirely. Option D requires complex custom logic and doesn't detect drift directly.

stem: A company runs a critical application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer across two Availability Zones. The application connects to an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster. During a recent AZ failure, the application experienced 15 minutes of downtime because unhealthy instances were not replaced quickly enough. Which solution minimizes downtime during an AZ failure?

options.text: Configure the Auto Scaling group with a shorter health check grace period of 60 seconds and set the default instance warmup to 120 seconds. Enable capacity rebalancing and set the minimum healthy percentage to 100% in the deployment configuration.

Create a cross-Region read replica of the Aurora cluster in a secondary Region. Configure Route 53 health checks on the ALB endpoint and set up an active-passive failover routing policy with a TTL of 60 seconds for the DNS record.

Configure the Auto Scaling group to use three Availability Zones with capacity distributed evenly. Enable ELB health checks with a 30-second interval and set the unhealthy threshold to 2, so failed instances are replaced within approximately 90 seconds.

Deploy the application using an ECS Fargate service across two Availability Zones with a minimum healthy percent of 100. Configure the ALB health check with a 10-second interval and deregistration delay of 30 seconds on the target group.

explanation: Spreading across three AZs ensures that when one AZ fails, two-thirds of capacity remains available. ELB health checks with a short interval and low unhealthy threshold enable rapid detection and replacement. Option A adjusts timing but doesn't add AZ redundancy. Option C adds cross-Region failover, which is over-engineered for an AZ failure scenario. Option D migrates to Fargate, which doesn't address the core issue of AZ distribution for EC2 workloads.

stem: A company needs to aggregate logs from 200 microservices running on Amazon ECS Fargate across three AWS Regions into a centralized logging solution. The solution must support near-real-time search, retain logs for 90 days, and archive logs older than 90 days to reduce costs. Which architecture meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure each ECS task with the awslogs log driver to send logs to CloudWatch Logs. Create Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams with a Lambda transformation to forward logs to an S3 bucket, then use Amazon Athena for ad-hoc querying.

Configure each ECS task with a FireLens log driver using a Fluent Bit sidecar to send logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs in each Region. Create cross-account CloudWatch subscriptions to stream all logs to a central account's CloudWatch log group.

Configure each ECS task with a FireLens log driver to send logs directly to a centralized Amazon OpenSearch Service domain. Set up an Index State Management policy to transition indices older than 90 days to UltraWarm storage and delete after 365 days.

Configure each ECS task with a FireLens log driver to send logs to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams in each Region. Use Kinesis Data Firehose to deliver logs to a centralized S3 bucket and query using Amazon Redshift Spectrum with materialized views.

explanation: Amazon OpenSearch Service with FireLens provides near-real-time search capability, and Index State Management policies handle automated lifecycle management including transitioning to cheaper UltraWarm storage after 90 days. Option A centralizes in CloudWatch but doesn't efficiently support full-text search across 200 services. Option C uses S3+Athena which doesn't provide near-real-time search. Option D adds unnecessary complexity with Redshift Spectrum, which is optimized for structured data analytics rather than log search.

stem: A company's production Amazon RDS Multi-AZ PostgreSQL database experienced a failover event that caused a brief application outage. The operations team was not notified until users reported the issue 30 minutes later. The team needs an automated notification system that alerts on-call engineers within 1 minute of any RDS failover event. Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Enable Amazon RDS Enhanced Monitoring with a 1-second granularity. Create a CloudWatch alarm on the CPUUtilization metric with a 60-second evaluation period and configure the alarm to send notifications to an SNS topic subscribed by the on-call team.

Create a CloudWatch Logs metric filter on the RDS PostgreSQL error log for failover-related keywords. Configure a CloudWatch alarm on the custom metric with a 1-minute evaluation period and send alarm state changes to an SNS topic.

Enable RDS Performance Insights for the database instance. Create a CloudWatch alarm on the db.SessionsActive performance counter and set a threshold anomaly detection band to trigger an SNS notification when connection patterns change.

Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to match RDS DB instance events with the detail-type of 'RDS DB Instance Event' and event ID for multi-AZ failover. Set the target as an SNS topic with the on-call team's email and SMS subscriptions.

explanation: Amazon EventBridge natively receives RDS events including multi-AZ failover notifications in near real-time. A rule matching the specific failover event type provides the fastest and most reliable alerting. Option A monitors CPU, which doesn't directly detect failover events. Option C monitors session activity, which is an indirect indicator of failover. Option D relies on log parsing which adds latency and may miss events if log keywords don't match exactly.

stem: A company must ensure that all Amazon S3 buckets across 50 AWS accounts enforce encryption at rest using AWS KMS customer-managed keys and block public access. Non-compliant buckets must be automatically remediated within 1 hour. Which solution provides continuous compliance enforcement?

options.text: Configure AWS CloudTrail to log all S3 API calls across all accounts. Create EventBridge rules in each account to match CreateBucket and PutBucketEncryption events and trigger a Lambda function that applies the required encryption and access settings.

Deploy Amazon Macie across all accounts using AWS Organizations delegated administrator. Configure Macie to scan buckets for encryption settings and use EventBridge rules to trigger Lambda remediation functions for non-compliant buckets.

Deploy AWS Config rules s3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled and s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited across all accounts using AWS Organizations. Attach auto-remediation actions using Systems Manager Automation documents to enforce encryption and block public access.

Create an SCP in AWS Organizations that denies s3:CreateBucket unless the request includes SSE-KMS encryption and BlockPublicAccess parameters. Deploy a Lambda function on a 1-hour schedule to scan existing buckets and apply missing configurations.

explanation: AWS Config rules provide continuous compliance evaluation with built-in managed rules for S3 encryption and public access. Auto-remediation via SSM Automation documents can automatically fix non-compliant resources. Option B prevents new non-compliant buckets but requires custom Lambda for existing ones, combining two separate mechanisms. Option C uses Macie, which is designed for data discovery not compliance enforcement. Option D only catches specific API events and misses buckets modified through other means.

stem: A team uses AWS CodeBuild to run unit tests and build Docker images for 30 microservices. Build times average 12 minutes, and the team wants to reduce them to under 5 minutes. Each microservice has its own buildspec.yml and Dockerfile. The Docker images range from 500MB to 2GB. Which optimization strategy is MOST effective?

options.text: Migrate from CodeBuild to Amazon ECS tasks with Kaniko for building Docker images. Store base images in Amazon ECR with immutable tags and configure ECS tasks to pull base images from a VPC endpoint to reduce network transfer time.

Create a single monorepo CodeBuild project that builds all 30 microservices in sequence. Use CodeBuild batch builds with the build graph strategy to identify dependencies between services and skip unchanged services using git diff checks.

Enable CodeBuild local caching with Docker layer cache mode and configure a custom cache S3 bucket. Refactor each Dockerfile to use multi-stage builds with dependency installation layers ordered before source code copy for optimal layer reuse.

Upgrade all CodeBuild projects to use compute type BUILD_GENERAL1_2XLARGE with 145 GB memory and 72 vCPUs. Enable privileged mode for Docker builds and configure concurrent build limits to allow all 30 services to build simultaneously.

explanation: Docker layer caching in CodeBuild combined with properly ordered Dockerfile layers provides the most significant build time reduction. Multi-stage builds with dependency layers before source copy means only changed layers rebuild. Option B increases compute but doesn't address the core issue of rebuilding unchanged Docker layers. Option C adds migration complexity without fundamentally solving the caching issue. Option D introduces a monorepo approach that doesn't reduce individual build times and adds sequential overhead.

stem: A company is migrating from manually provisioned infrastructure to AWS CloudFormation. The team needs to import 50 existing EC2 instances, their associated security groups, and EBS volumes into CloudFormation management without downtime. Which TWO steps are required to accomplish this?

options.text: After importing resources, run a CloudFormation drift detection operation on the stack to identify any configuration differences between the template definitions and the actual resource configurations, then update the template to match actual state.

Write a CloudFormation template that defines each existing resource with a DeletionPolicy of Retain and matching configuration. Use the CloudFormation import operation to associate each existing resource with its template definition by providing resource identifiers.

Run CloudFormation drift detection on the existing resources to generate a baseline template. Export the drift results as a CloudFormation template using the console's export feature and create a new stack from the exported template.

Use the AWS CloudFormation CLI create-stack command with the --import-resources flag and provide a JSON mapping file that lists each existing resource's physical ID alongside its desired logical ID in the new stack template.

explanation: Resource import requires defining resources in a template with DeletionPolicy Retain and using the import operation with resource identifiers (A). After import, drift detection verifies the template matches actual resource state (D). Option B uses a non-existent --import-resources flag; import is done through the console or create-change-set with import type. Option C describes a feature that doesn't exist; drift detection doesn't export templates.

stem: A company operates a stateful application on EC2 instances that process financial transactions. Each transaction takes up to 30 seconds to complete and must not be interrupted. The Auto Scaling group needs to scale in during off-peak hours. How should the team configure the Auto Scaling group to prevent transaction loss during scale-in events?

options.text: Configure the Auto Scaling group with a default cooldown period of 300 seconds between scaling activities. Set the health check grace period to 120 seconds and enable instance protection on all instances that are actively processing transactions.

Enable Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks for the autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING event. Configure the application to complete in-flight transactions when it receives the lifecycle notification and send a CONTINUE signal via the CompleteLifecycleAction API.

Set the Auto Scaling group's termination policy to OldestInstance and configure a deregistration delay of 120 seconds on the target group. Enable connection draining on the Application Load Balancer with a timeout matching the longest transaction duration.

Configure the Auto Scaling group to use a scheduled scaling policy that reduces capacity only during a maintenance window. Send an SNS notification 5 minutes before the scheduled action and have engineers manually verify no transactions are in progress.

explanation: Lifecycle hooks pause the instance termination process, giving the application time to complete in-flight transactions before the instance is terminated. The application can signal completion via the CompleteLifecycleAction API. Option B's cooldown and instance protection don't gracefully drain in-flight work during scale-in. Option C's deregistration delay prevents new connections but doesn't signal the application to complete work. Option D requires manual intervention and doesn't automate the transaction protection.

stem: A company's application generates custom business metrics that must be monitored with sub-second granularity. The operations team needs to create dashboards showing the 99th percentile of order processing latency and trigger alarms when the p99 exceeds 500ms for 3 consecutive 10-second periods. Which approach supports this requirement?

options.text: Use the CloudWatch PutMetricData API to publish individual metric values with StorageResolution set to 1 (high resolution). Create a CloudWatch alarm using the ExtendedStatistic p99 with a 10-second period and set datapoints to alarm at 3 out of 3.

Use the CloudWatch embedded metric format in application logs sent via the CloudWatch Logs agent. Configure the metric filter to extract latency values and create a dashboard widget displaying the p99 statistic with a 1-minute refresh interval.

Use Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus to ingest custom metrics via the remote write endpoint. Create recording rules to compute the 99th percentile histogram over 10-second windows and configure Alertmanager rules for threshold-based alerting.

Use the CloudWatch PutMetricData API with the StatisticValues parameter to publish aggregated statistics every 10 seconds. Create a CloudWatch alarm on the Average statistic with a 10-second period and 3 evaluation periods with a 500ms threshold.

explanation: High-resolution CloudWatch metrics (StorageResolution=1) support 1-second granularity. Publishing individual data points allows CloudWatch to compute percentile statistics like p99, and alarms can evaluate at 10-second periods. Option A uses StatisticValues which pre-aggregates data and doesn't support percentile calculations. Option C uses embedded metric format which defaults to 1-minute resolution and doesn't support sub-second granularity. Option D uses Prometheus which works but adds unnecessary service complexity when CloudWatch natively supports this.

stem: An e-commerce application experiences intermittent 504 Gateway Timeout errors during peak traffic periods. The application runs on ECS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer, with an Aurora PostgreSQL database backend. CloudWatch metrics show normal CPU and memory utilization on ECS tasks. Which investigation approach will MOST likely identify the root cause?

options.text: Enable ALB access logs and analyze the target_processing_time field to determine if backend tasks are slow to respond. Check the Aurora DatabaseConnections metric and compare against the max_connections parameter to identify connection pool exhaustion.

Configure CloudWatch Container Insights for the ECS cluster to collect per-task CPU and memory metrics at 1-minute granularity. Create a CloudWatch dashboard correlating task-level resource utilization with the ALB HTTP 504 count metric over time.

Enable AWS X-Ray tracing on the ECS tasks and ALB to generate a service map showing latency distribution across components. Review the X-Ray analytics console to identify latency outliers correlated with specific API endpoints or downstream dependencies.

Enable VPC Flow Logs for the subnets hosting the ECS tasks and Aurora cluster. Analyze flow logs in CloudWatch Logs Insights to identify dropped packets or connection resets between the application tasks and the database endpoints.

explanation: 504 errors from an ALB typically indicate the target didn't respond within the idle timeout. ALB access logs' target_processing_time identifies slow backends, and checking Aurora connection limits reveals if the database is rejecting connections. Option B provides distributed tracing but requires instrumentation and is better for latency analysis than timeout debugging. Option C shows normal metrics per the scenario; container-level metrics won't reveal new information. Option D analyzes network-level flow data, which rarely reveals application-level timeout causes.

stem: A company needs to rotate database credentials for 50 Amazon RDS instances automatically every 30 days. Applications retrieve credentials at startup and cache them in memory. The solution must ensure applications can still connect during and immediately after rotation without restarts. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Store credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store SecureString parameters with a Lambda function on a 30-day EventBridge schedule. Update each parameter with new credentials and configure applications to poll Parameter Store every 5 minutes for changes.

Store credentials in AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation enabled using a Lambda rotation function. Configure the rotation to use the alternating users strategy with a 30-day rotation schedule and update applications to call GetSecretValue before each connection.

Store credentials in AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation enabled using a single-user rotation strategy. Configure the rotation Lambda in the same VPC as the RDS instances and update applications to retrieve credentials once at startup with a 30-day TTL cache.

Store credentials in HashiCorp Vault running on ECS Fargate with a dynamic secrets engine for RDS PostgreSQL. Configure Vault to generate short-lived credentials with a 30-day maximum TTL and integrate applications using the Vault Agent sidecar pattern.

explanation: Secrets Manager's alternating users strategy maintains two sets of credentials, ensuring the previous credentials remain valid while new ones are created. Applications calling GetSecretValue before each connection always get valid credentials. Option B uses Parameter Store which lacks native rotation support and requires custom implementation. Option C's single-user strategy briefly invalidates the current password during rotation, causing connection failures for cached credentials. Option D adds significant infrastructure complexity with HashiCorp Vault when Secrets Manager provides native RDS integration.

stem: A team manages 20 AWS Lambda functions deployed via AWS SAM. Each function requires environment-specific configuration for dev, staging, and production stages. The team wants to use a single SAM template across all environments and promote the exact same artifact through stages without rebuilding. Which deployment strategy achieves this?

options.text: Use SAM template parameters with environment-specific parameter override files stored in S3. Configure CodePipeline to build once in the source stage and use CloudFormation deploy actions with ParameterOverrides referencing environment-specific JSON files from S3.

Create separate SAM template files for each environment with hardcoded configuration values. Use CodePipeline with separate source actions for each template and deploy each environment using its own CloudFormation deploy action with the respective template.

Store environment configurations in AWS AppConfig feature flags for each Lambda function. Deploy the same SAM template to all stages and configure each Lambda function to retrieve its configuration from AppConfig at invocation time using the AppConfig Lambda extension.

Use SAM nested stacks with a parent template that accepts an Environment parameter. Create child stacks for each Lambda function group and use CloudFormation Mappings to select the correct configuration values based on the Environment parameter value.

explanation: Using parameter override files allows a single SAM template and build artifact to be promoted across environments, with only configuration values changing per stage. This follows the build-once-deploy-many pattern. Option A requires separate templates per environment, violating the single-template requirement. Option C externalizes configuration but doesn't address artifact promotion through CodePipeline stages. Option D still uses a single template but nested stacks add complexity without solving the artifact promotion requirement better than parameter overrides.

stem: A company uses AWS CDK with TypeScript to define infrastructure. The team wants to enforce that all S3 buckets created through CDK have versioning enabled, encryption with KMS CMKs, and access logging configured. The enforcement must happen before deployment and prevent non-compliant stacks from being synthesized. Which approach provides this pre-deployment enforcement?

options.text: Create a custom CDK L3 construct called SecureBucket that wraps the S3 Bucket construct with mandatory versioning, KMS encryption, and access logging. Publish the construct to an internal CodeArtifact repository and prohibit direct S3 Bucket usage.

Write custom AWS Config rules using Lambda functions that evaluate S3 bucket configurations. Deploy the Config rules before the CDK stack and configure CloudFormation stack policies to prevent updates that would create non-compliant S3 resources.

Implement a custom CloudFormation Guard rule set that validates the synthesized CloudFormation template. Integrate cfn-guard as a CodeBuild step in the CI/CD pipeline to validate templates and fail the build if S3 bucket rules are violated.

Create CDK Aspects that visit all S3 Bucket constructs in the construct tree during synthesis. Check for versioning, KMS encryption, and access logging properties, and call Annotations.of(node).addError() for non-compliant buckets to fail synthesis.

explanation: CDK Aspects provide a native mechanism to traverse the construct tree during synthesis and validate resource configurations before any deployment occurs. Adding errors through Annotations fails the synthesis. Option B uses AWS Config which only evaluates after deployment, not before. Option C validates post-synthesis templates in CI/CD but not during synthesis itself. Option D provides a compliant construct but cannot prevent engineers from using the standard S3 Bucket construct directly.

stem: A company operates a multi-Region active-active application using Amazon DynamoDB global tables. During a simulated Region failover test, the team discovered that some writes were lost because both Regions accepted conflicting updates to the same item simultaneously. Which strategy prevents data loss from conflicting writes in a multi-Region active-active configuration?

options.text: Switch from active-active to active-passive configuration using Route 53 health checks for Region failover. Configure DynamoDB global tables to replicate from the primary Region only and use a Lambda function to redirect writes to the active Region endpoint.

Implement application-level conflict resolution by adding a vector clock attribute to each item. Use DynamoDB conditional expressions with attribute_exists and version checks to detect conflicts and route resolution to a designated primary Region for arbitration.

Enable DynamoDB Streams on the global table and configure a Lambda function to detect conflicting writes by comparing version attributes. Implement a custom last-writer-wins resolution strategy using conditional writes with a monotonically increasing version number.

Configure DynamoDB global tables with the last-writer-wins reconciliation default behavior and add a timestamp attribute updated by the application. Accept DynamoDB's built-in conflict resolution and design the application to tolerate eventual consistency across Regions.

explanation: DynamoDB global tables use last-writer-wins reconciliation based on timestamps by default. The correct approach is to design the application to work with this behavior and tolerate eventual consistency. Option A adds custom conflict detection but DynamoDB global tables already handle replication and conflict resolution automatically. Option B implements vector clocks which add complexity and don't integrate with DynamoDB's native replication mechanism. Option D eliminates the active-active benefit, which is counter to the stated architecture requirement.

stem: A company wants to implement centralized logging for applications running across 10 AWS accounts. Logs must be stored in a central account's S3 bucket with cross-account access, encrypted using a KMS key from the central account, and retained for 7 years for compliance. Which TWO configurations are required?

options.text: Create a KMS key in the central account with a key policy that grants kms:GenerateDataKey and kms:Decrypt permissions to the CloudWatch Logs service principal from each source account, enabling cross-account log encryption at the destination.

Configure S3 Object Lock in Governance mode on the central logging bucket with a retention period of 7 years. Enable S3 Versioning and create lifecycle rules to transition logs to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 90 days for cost optimization.

Configure CloudWatch Logs subscription filters in each source account to stream logs to a Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream in the central account. Set the Firehose destination to the S3 bucket with SSE-KMS encryption using the central account's KMS key.

Deploy a CloudWatch Logs destination in the central account with a resource policy allowing source accounts to put subscription filters. Configure the destination to forward logs to a Kinesis Data Stream that feeds into a Firehose delivery stream writing to S3.

explanation: Kinesis Data Firehose delivery streams in the central account can receive logs from cross-account subscription filters and write them encrypted to S3 (B). S3 Object Lock with the 7-year retention ensures compliance retention and Glacier Deep Archive reduces long-term storage costs (D). Option A incorrectly grants permissions to CloudWatch Logs service principal instead of the Firehose service role. Option C adds an unnecessary Kinesis Data Stream intermediary when Firehose can directly receive subscription filter data.

stem: A company's Auto Scaling group launches EC2 instances that take 5 minutes to fully bootstrap using a UserData script. During a traffic spike, new instances were added to the load balancer before bootstrapping completed, causing HTTP 503 errors. How should the team prevent instances from receiving traffic before they are ready?

options.text: Set the Auto Scaling group health check type to ELB and increase the health check grace period to 600 seconds. Configure the ALB deregistration delay to 300 seconds and enable slow start mode on the target group with a 300-second duration.

Add an Auto Scaling lifecycle hook for EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING that pauses the instance in Pending:Wait state. Have the UserData script send a CONTINUE signal via the CompleteLifecycleAction API only after bootstrapping finishes successfully.

Create a CloudWatch alarm that monitors the custom health check metric published by each instance during bootstrapping. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the alarm as a scaling trigger and only register instances with the target group when the alarm is in OK state.

Configure the ALB target group health check with a path that returns HTTP 200 only after bootstrapping completes. Set the health check interval to 10 seconds, the healthy threshold to 3, and the unhealthy threshold to 2 to allow time for initialization.

explanation: Lifecycle hooks in Pending:Wait state prevent the instance from being registered with the load balancer until the application signals it's ready. The UserData script calls CompleteLifecycleAction after bootstrapping. Option A improves health check detection but the instance still receives some traffic before being marked unhealthy. Option B's grace period delays detection of unhealthy instances but doesn't prevent initial traffic routing. Option D requires custom metric infrastructure and doesn't natively integrate with ALB registration.

stem: A company deploys containerized applications on Amazon EKS and needs to prevent pods from running as root, ensure all container images come from a trusted ECR registry, and enforce resource limits on every pod. Which solution provides automated enforcement of these policies at admission time?

options.text: Enable Pod Security Standards in the EKS cluster at the Restricted level. Configure namespace labels to enforce the restricted profile and create custom ValidatingWebhookConfigurations to check for ECR registry sources and resource limit requirements.

Configure Amazon Inspector to scan EKS workloads continuously for security findings. Create EventBridge rules that trigger a Lambda function to delete non-compliant pods and send notifications to the security team via SNS when policy violations are detected.

Deploy AWS Config rules for EKS clusters that evaluate pod security configurations against CIS benchmarks. Configure auto-remediation using SSM Automation documents that patch non-compliant pod specifications and restart affected deployments automatically.

Install OPA Gatekeeper on the EKS cluster and define ConstraintTemplates that enforce non-root security context, restrict image sources to the trusted ECR registry, and require resource limits. Apply Constraints to target all namespaces except kube-system.

explanation: OPA Gatekeeper acts as a Kubernetes admission controller that evaluates pod specifications against defined policies before admission. ConstraintTemplates can enforce all three requirements at admission time. Option B uses Inspector for detection but deleting pods post-creation doesn't prevent admission. Option C provides Pod Security Standards for security context but requires additional webhooks for image registry and resource limits, making it a partial solution. Option D uses AWS Config which evaluates after deployment, not at admission time.

stem: A company has a monorepo containing 10 microservices in a single AWS CodeCommit repository. Each microservice has its own directory with source code and buildspec.yml. The team wants CodePipeline to build and deploy only the microservices that have changed in each commit, not all 10 every time. Which solution achieves selective builds?

options.text: Configure an EventBridge rule to trigger a Lambda function on CodeCommit repository state change events. Have the Lambda function parse the commit diff and start individual CodePipeline executions by calling the StartPipelineExecution API for affected services.

Create a single CodePipeline with a CodeBuild batch build using the build-matrix strategy. Define each microservice as a separate build environment in the batch configuration and use the buildspec to check for changes before executing each build.

Create a single CodePipeline with a CodeCommit source action. Add a CodeBuild project that runs a git diff script to identify changed directories, then dynamically triggers individual CodeBuild projects for each changed microservice using the AWS SDK.

Create 10 separate CodePipeline pipelines, each with a CodeCommit source action filtered by file path using the CloudWatch Events trigger configuration. Set each pipeline's event filter to match changes only in its corresponding microservice directory.

explanation: CodePipeline supports file path-based triggers through EventBridge event filtering on CodeCommit events. Each pipeline only starts when files in its specific directory change. Option A requires custom orchestration logic in CodeBuild to manage selective builds. Option C uses batch builds but doesn't natively support file-path-based selective execution. Option D adds custom Lambda logic when native file path filtering is available through EventBridge rules.

stem: A company uses Terraform to manage AWS infrastructure across multiple teams. They need to ensure that the Terraform state file is stored securely with encryption, supports locking to prevent concurrent modifications, and maintains a history of state changes for audit purposes. Which configuration meets ALL requirements?

options.text: Store the Terraform state in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as a SecureString parameter with KMS encryption. Implement locking using a DynamoDB table with conditional writes and version the state by creating timestamped parameter copies before each update.

Configure the Terraform backend to use an S3 bucket with SSE-S3 encryption and MFA Delete enabled for state protection. Use an SQS FIFO queue as a custom locking mechanism via a wrapper script and enable CloudTrail S3 data events for state change auditing.

Configure the Terraform backend to use Terraform Cloud with remote state storage and built-in locking. Enable state versioning in Terraform Cloud's workspace settings and configure SAML SSO integration with the company's identity provider for access control.

Configure the Terraform backend to use an S3 bucket with SSE-KMS encryption and versioning enabled for state history. Add a DynamoDB table for state locking with a LockID partition key and enable S3 access logging to an audit bucket for access tracking.

explanation: S3 backend with SSE-KMS provides encryption, versioning provides state history for auditing, and DynamoDB provides native state locking support. This is the recommended Terraform backend configuration for AWS. Option B uses SSE-S3 instead of KMS and an SQS-based custom locking mechanism that isn't natively supported. Option C uses Parameter Store which has size limitations and doesn't natively serve as a Terraform backend. Option D uses Terraform Cloud, which works but introduces an external dependency when the question implies AWS-native storage.

stem: A company runs a batch processing system on Amazon EC2 Spot Instances that processes jobs from an SQS queue. Each job takes between 10 and 45 minutes to complete. When Spot Instances are interrupted, in-progress jobs are lost and must be reprocessed. Which solution ensures jobs are not lost during Spot interruptions?

options.text: Configure the application to check the EC2 instance metadata endpoint for Spot interruption notices every 5 seconds. When a notice is received, save the job's progress to an S3 checkpoint file and return the message to the SQS queue by resetting its visibility timeout.

Deploy the batch processing on AWS Fargate Spot tasks instead of EC2 Spot Instances. Configure the ECS service to automatically restart interrupted tasks and set the SQS queue visibility timeout to match the maximum job processing duration of 45 minutes.

Use an Auto Scaling group with mixed instance types and a capacity-optimized Spot allocation strategy. Configure the SQS queue visibility timeout to 60 minutes and enable dead-letter queue redrive with a maximum receive count of 3 for failed jobs.

Switch from Spot Instances to On-Demand Instances in a Reserved capacity pool to eliminate interruptions entirely. Configure Auto Scaling scheduled actions to scale capacity based on the expected queue depth during peak processing hours.

explanation: EC2 Spot interruption notices provide a 2-minute warning. Checking metadata every 5 seconds, saving progress to S3, and returning the SQS message ensures no work is lost. Option B reduces interruption probability but doesn't handle the case when interruption occurs with an in-progress job. Option C uses Fargate Spot which also has interruptions and doesn't solve the fundamental problem of in-flight job loss. Option D eliminates Spot cost savings, which contradicts the use case for batch processing.

stem: A company uses AWS X-Ray to trace requests through a distributed microservices architecture. The team notices that some traces are incomplete, missing segments from downstream services. All services are instrumented with the X-Ray SDK and run on ECS Fargate. Which configuration issue is MOST likely causing incomplete traces?

options.text: The downstream services are not propagating the X-Amzn-Trace-Id header in their HTTP responses to upstream callers. Update the application code to extract the trace header from incoming requests and include it in all outbound HTTP client requests.

The X-Ray sampling rules are configured with a low fixed rate that drops segments from high-throughput downstream services. Update the centralized sampling rules in the X-Ray console to increase the reservoir size and fixed rate for downstream services.

The X-Ray daemon sidecar container is not configured in the ECS task definitions for downstream services. Add an aws-xray-daemon container to each task definition and configure the application containers to send trace data to the daemon on UDP port 2000.

The ECS task execution role lacks the xray:PutTraceSegments and xray:PutTelemetryRecords permissions. Update the task execution role's IAM policy to include these X-Ray API actions with a resource scope of the account's trace group ARN.

explanation: On ECS Fargate, the X-Ray daemon must run as a sidecar container in each task definition since there's no host-level daemon. Without the daemon sidecar, downstream services cannot send trace segments to X-Ray. Option A incorrectly references the task execution role; X-Ray permissions should be on the task role, and this would cause all segments to fail, not just some. Option C describes header propagation which the X-Ray SDK handles automatically. Option D would cause random sampling gaps, not consistently missing downstream segments.

stem: A company detected unauthorized API calls in AWS CloudTrail logs that created IAM users with administrative privileges. The security team needs to immediately contain the incident and determine the scope of the breach. Which sequence of actions should the team take FIRST?

options.text: Isolate the affected account by removing it from the AWS Organization and applying an SCP that denies all actions. Launch a forensic EC2 instance in a separate account to analyze CloudTrail logs stored in the centralized logging S3 bucket for the past 30 days.

Delete the unauthorized IAM users and their access keys immediately. Rotate all IAM user passwords and access keys across the account. Enable MFA on the root account and all IAM users, then review CloudTrail logs for the past 90 days to assess impact.

Enable AWS Security Hub with the Foundational Security Best Practices standard to identify all compromised resources. Run an Amazon Inspector assessment on all EC2 instances in the account and generate an automated remediation plan using Systems Manager OpsCenter.

Attach a deny-all IAM policy to the unauthorized IAM users to disable their access without deleting evidence. Revoke all active sessions for the compromised principal using an inline policy with a NotBefore condition, then analyze CloudTrail logs for full scope.

explanation: Attaching deny-all policies preserves the unauthorized users as evidence while immediately containing access. Revoking active sessions prevents continued use of existing credentials. Analyzing CloudTrail provides scope. Option A deletes users which destroys forensic evidence. Option C removes the account from the Organization which is overly disruptive and may break cross-account dependencies. Option D focuses on detection and assessment tools rather than immediate containment actions.

stem: A company is implementing a CI/CD pipeline for container deployments to Amazon ECS. The security team requires that container images are scanned for vulnerabilities before deployment and that images with critical or high severity vulnerabilities are blocked from being deployed. Which TWO actions should be implemented?

options.text: Create an EventBridge rule that matches ECR image scan completion events with findings of CRITICAL or HIGH severity. Configure the rule target as a Lambda function that updates the ECR repository policy to deny pulls for the specific image tag.

Configure an ECR lifecycle policy that automatically deletes images older than 30 days. Enable ECR image tag immutability to prevent overwriting scanned images and configure the ECS task definition to always pull the latest tagged image version.

Add a CodeBuild stage in the pipeline that runs Trivy container scanning against the built image. Parse the scan output JSON for critical and high findings, and exit with a non-zero code to fail the pipeline stage if any are found.

Enable Amazon ECR image scanning with enhanced scanning powered by Amazon Inspector. Configure scan-on-push to automatically scan images when they are pushed to the repository and generate findings with severity classifications for each vulnerability.

explanation: ECR enhanced scanning with Inspector provides comprehensive vulnerability detection on push (A). An EventBridge rule that blocks pulls for images with critical/high findings prevents deployment of vulnerable images (C). Option B adds a third-party tool when native ECR scanning is available, and it only blocks in the pipeline, not from direct pulls. Option D manages image lifecycle and immutability but doesn't scan for vulnerabilities or block vulnerable images from deployment.

stem: A company uses AWS CodeDeploy to perform rolling deployments to a fleet of 100 EC2 instances. During a recent deployment, a bug in the application caused errors that were only detected after 60% of the fleet was updated. The team wants to minimize the blast radius of future faulty deployments. Which deployment configuration achieves this?

options.text: Configure CodeDeploy with AllAtOnce deployment and add a manual approval step in CodePipeline between the staging and production deploy actions. Require two team leads to approve the deployment after reviewing staging test results before proceeding to production.

Configure a CodeDeploy deployment group with a canary deployment configuration that deploys to 5% of instances first and waits 15 minutes. Attach a CloudWatch alarm on HTTP 5xx count and enable automatic rollback before proceeding to the remaining 95% of instances.

Configure CodeDeploy with a OneAtATime deployment configuration to minimize blast radius by updating one instance at a time. Enable automatic rollback on deployment failure and set the minimum healthy hosts to 99% to maintain service availability throughout the deployment.

Configure a CodeDeploy deployment group with a linear deployment configuration that deploys to 10% of instances every 5 minutes. Add a CloudWatch alarm monitoring the application error rate and configure automatic rollback on alarm to revert all updated instances.

explanation: Canary deployment deploys to a small percentage first, allowing validation before proceeding to the full fleet. With a CloudWatch alarm, faulty deployments are caught when only 5% of instances are affected. Option A uses linear which continuously deploys without a validation pause, potentially affecting multiple batches before the alarm triggers. Option C uses AllAtOnce which provides no blast radius control and relies on staging detection. Option D's OneAtATime is slow but doesn't provide a dedicated validation period between a small canary group and the rest.

stem: A company needs to deploy identical infrastructure stacks across 20 AWS accounts and 4 Regions using AWS CloudFormation. The stacks include VPCs, security groups, and IAM roles. Some resources like IAM roles must only be created once per account regardless of Region. Which approach handles this multi-account, multi-Region deployment efficiently?

options.text: Write a single CloudFormation template with conditions using AWS::Region pseudo-parameter to conditionally create IAM roles only in us-east-1. Deploy the template as a StackSet across all 20 accounts and 4 Regions, relying on conditions to skip IAM creation in other Regions.

Create a CodePipeline that iterates through each account and Region combination. Use CloudFormation deploy actions with separate templates for regional and global resources, and implement a Lambda function to track which accounts have already received global resources.

Use Terraform with a multi-provider configuration referencing all 20 accounts using assumed roles. Define modules for regional and global resources with conditional deployment logic based on the provider's Region, storing state in a centralized S3 backend.

Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions through AWS Organizations. Create two StackSets: one for Region-specific resources deployed to all 4 Regions, and one for global IAM resources deployed to only one Region per account using Region filters.

explanation: CloudFormation StackSets with Organizations integration natively handles multi-account deployment. Splitting into two StackSets separates Region-specific resources from global resources like IAM roles, with Region filters controlling where each deploys. Option B's conditional approach works but creates empty stacks in non-primary Regions and doesn't cleanly separate concerns. Option C requires complex custom orchestration logic. Option D uses Terraform which works but the question context implies CloudFormation-based solution and StackSets are purpose-built for this.

stem: A company's web application uses Amazon ElastiCache for Redis as a session store. When the primary Redis node fails, the application loses all user sessions, forcing users to re-authenticate. Which ElastiCache configuration ensures sessions are preserved during a primary node failure?

options.text: Deploy ElastiCache Memcached with a multi-node cluster across multiple Availability Zones. Configure automatic discovery enabled and client-side consistent hashing to distribute session data evenly and survive individual node failures without data loss.

Deploy ElastiCache Redis in cluster mode disabled with Multi-AZ enabled and automatic failover. Configure at least one read replica in a different AZ that automatically promotes to primary during failure, preserving the existing data through asynchronous replication.

Deploy ElastiCache Redis in cluster mode enabled with multiple shards across Availability Zones. Configure each shard with two replicas and enable in-transit encryption with AUTH token authentication to secure session data during inter-node replication.

Deploy ElastiCache Redis with daily automated backups retained for 7 days. Configure a Lambda function triggered by ElastiCache SNS failover notifications to restore the most recent backup to a new Redis cluster and update the application endpoint.

explanation: Redis with Multi-AZ and automatic failover promotes a replica to primary during failure, preserving session data through replication. Option B's cluster mode with sharding is more complex than needed for session storage and doesn't specifically address failover better than Multi-AZ. Option C uses Memcached which doesn't support replication; if a node fails, its data is lost. Option D restores from backups which causes data loss between the last backup and the failure event, and introduces significant delay.

stem: A company needs to create a CloudWatch dashboard that displays the total number of API Gateway requests across 50 REST APIs, broken down by HTTP status code categories (2xx, 4xx, 5xx). The dashboard should update every 1 minute and support drill-down into individual APIs. Which approach creates this dashboard efficiently?

options.text: Create CloudWatch metric math expressions that use SEARCH to query all API Gateway Count metrics grouped by ApiName and StatusCode dimensions. Use METRICS function to aggregate status code categories and display results in a stacked area chart widget.

Configure API Gateway access logging to CloudWatch Logs for all 50 APIs. Create CloudWatch Logs Insights queries that parse status codes and aggregate by API name, then add the query results as a dashboard widget with a 1-minute auto-refresh interval.

Enable detailed CloudWatch metrics for each API Gateway stage. Create individual CloudWatch metric widgets for each of the 50 APIs showing 4xxError and 5xxError metrics, then use a CloudWatch dashboard text widget to display the calculated totals.

Create a Lambda function on a 1-minute schedule that calls the CloudWatch GetMetricData API for all 50 APIs. Aggregate the results by status code category and publish custom metrics using PutMetricData, then build dashboard widgets from the custom metrics.

explanation: CloudWatch metric math SEARCH expressions dynamically query metrics across multiple resources, and METRICS function enables aggregation by status code categories. This automatically includes new APIs without dashboard updates. Option B uses Logs Insights which adds latency and doesn't integrate as smoothly with dashboards for real-time metrics. Option C requires a custom Lambda function when native metric math provides the same capability. Option D creates individual widgets per API, making the dashboard unmanageable at 50 APIs.

stem: A company's application on EC2 runs behind a Network Load Balancer and experiences periodic connection timeouts. The operations team suspects the issue is related to EC2 instance networking but cannot reproduce it consistently. Which approach provides the MOST detailed network-level troubleshooting data?

options.text: Enable VPC Flow Logs on the ENIs attached to the affected EC2 instances with maximum aggregation interval of 1 minute. Publish logs to CloudWatch Logs and create a Logs Insights query that filters for REJECT actions and correlates timestamps with timeout reports.

Enable Traffic Mirroring on the ENIs of the affected EC2 instances with a filter for TCP traffic on the application port. Send mirrored traffic to a monitoring EC2 instance running tcpdump to capture full packet headers and analyze TCP retransmissions and resets.

Install the CloudWatch agent on the affected EC2 instances configured to collect netstat and ss output as custom metrics. Publish TCP connection state counts including ESTABLISHED, TIME_WAIT, and CLOSE_WAIT every 10 seconds to identify connection leaks.

Configure CloudWatch network performance metrics for the EC2 instances including NetworkPacketsIn, NetworkPacketsOut, and NetworkPacketsDropped. Create a CloudWatch alarm on the PacketsDropped metric and correlate spikes with the NLB HealthyHostCount metric changes.

explanation: Traffic Mirroring captures actual packet data, providing full TCP handshake analysis including retransmissions, resets, and window scaling issues that cause connection timeouts. Option A shows flow-level accept/reject data but lacks packet-level detail like TCP flags and retransmissions. Option C provides aggregate network metrics but not granular connection-level diagnostics. Option D monitors connection states which is useful but doesn't capture the network-level events causing timeouts.

stem: A company needs to enforce that all EC2 instances launched in production accounts use only approved AMIs from a central shared services account. Instances launched from non-approved AMIs must be automatically terminated. Which approach provides this enforcement?

options.text: Configure Amazon Inspector to continuously assess EC2 instances against a custom assessment template. Create an EventBridge rule matching Inspector findings for non-approved AMIs and target a Step Functions state machine that terminates instances after confirmation.

Create an AWS Config rule using the approved-amis-by-id managed rule with the list of approved AMI IDs. Configure auto-remediation with an SSM Automation document that terminates EC2 instances launched from non-approved AMIs and sends an SNS notification.

Deploy a Service Control Policy in AWS Organizations that uses a condition key to restrict ec2:RunInstances to only the approved AMI ARNs. Configure the SCP at the production organizational unit level and exempt the shared services account from the policy.

Create an IAM policy in each production account that denies ec2:RunInstances unless the imageId condition matches the approved AMI list. Attach the policy to all IAM roles and users in the production accounts and update the AMI list monthly in each account.

explanation: AWS Config's approved-amis-by-id rule continuously evaluates running instances against approved AMIs, and SSM Automation auto-remediation terminates non-compliant instances. Option B prevents launching from non-approved AMIs but doesn't detect or terminate already-running instances launched before the SCP was applied. Option C requires maintaining IAM policies across all accounts and roles which is operationally burdensome. Option D uses Inspector which doesn't have a native AMI approval assessment template.

stem: A development team needs to implement database schema migrations as part of their CI/CD pipeline deploying to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. The migrations must run automatically during deployment, support rollback on failure, and not block application deployments for more than 30 seconds. Which approach meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a Lambda function deployed in the Aurora VPC subnet that executes Liquibase migrations using a custom runtime. Invoke the function as a CodePipeline Lambda action before the ECS deploy stage with a 30-second timeout and automatic rollback on failure.

Use an RDS Data API endpoint to execute migration SQL scripts directly from a CodePipeline Lambda invoke action. Store migration scripts in an S3 bucket versioned by deployment and configure the Lambda to execute statements sequentially using the Data API batch endpoint.

Add a CodeBuild stage before the application deployment that connects to Aurora through a VPC-configured build environment and runs Flyway migrations. Configure Flyway with outOfOrder set to false and enable baseline-on-migrate for the initial deployment run.

Configure the application container to run database migrations on startup before accepting traffic. Use an ECS container dependency with a migration sidecar container that runs Flyway and reports success via a health check endpoint that the main container waits for.

explanation: CodeBuild in a VPC can connect directly to Aurora and run Flyway migrations as a pipeline stage. If migration fails, the pipeline stops before application deployment. Option B's 30-second Lambda timeout is too short for complex migrations and Lambda has a maximum 15-minute timeout, not 30 seconds. Option C uses Data API which has statement size limits and doesn't support all PostgreSQL migration features. Option D ties migrations to application startup which can cause deployment timeouts and doesn't separate migration from application lifecycle.

stem: A company uses AWS Systems Manager to manage configuration across 500 EC2 instances. The team needs to deploy a new version of a configuration file to all instances in a controlled manner: 10% first, verify for 10 minutes, then the remaining 90%. If any instance reports failure during the rollout, the deployment must stop. Which SSM feature achieves this?

options.text: Create an SSM Distributor package containing the configuration file with an install script. Use SSM State Manager to create an association targeting all instances with the distributor package, setting the schedule to apply the configuration with a rate expression.

Configure AWS AppConfig with a deployment strategy that deploys to 10% of instances with a 10-minute bake time before proceeding to the remaining 90%. Create a configuration profile backed by an S3 object and integrate the application with the AppConfig agent.

Create an SSM State Manager association with a rate control configuration set to 10% concurrency and 1 error threshold. Apply the association to all 500 instances with an AWS-RunDocument command document that deploys the configuration file to each target instance.

Use SSM Run Command with a custom command document that copies the configuration file from S3. Configure the command with MaxConcurrency at 10% and MaxErrors at 0, and use a maintenance window with a two-phase execution schedule for the canary and full rollout.

explanation: AWS AppConfig provides native canary deployment strategies with configurable bake times and automatic rollback on errors, exactly matching the 10%/90% rollout with monitoring. Option A uses State Manager which applies configurations but doesn't support canary-then-full rollout with a bake period between phases. Option B's Run Command with MaxConcurrency controls speed but doesn't implement a two-phase canary strategy with validation pause. Option C uses Distributor for package distribution but doesn't support phased rollout with bake times.

stem: A company's application uses Amazon SQS standard queues for asynchronous processing. During a recent incident, a poison message caused the consumer Lambda function to repeatedly fail and retry, blocking other messages in the queue. Which solution prevents a single poison message from blocking queue processing?

options.text: Switch from SQS standard queue to an SQS FIFO queue with content-based deduplication enabled. Configure the FIFO queue's deduplication scope to messageGroup and set the visibility timeout to 30 seconds to ensure messages are reprocessed by other consumer instances.

Implement exponential backoff in the Lambda function code using a try-catch block around message processing. Store the retry count in a DynamoDB table keyed by message ID, and manually delete the message from the queue after the maximum retry count is exceeded.

Configure the Lambda event source mapping with a maximum retry attempts setting of 2 and a maximum batching window of 5 seconds. Enable bisect-on-function-error to split failed batches and send failed records to a configured on-failure destination SQS queue.

Configure the SQS queue with a redrive policy that moves messages to a dead-letter queue after 3 receive attempts. Set the main queue's visibility timeout to 6 times the Lambda function timeout and create a CloudWatch alarm on the DLQ ApproximateNumberOfMessages metric.

explanation: A dead-letter queue with a redrive policy automatically moves messages that exceed the maxReceiveCount to a separate queue, preventing poison messages from blocking processing. Option B's bisect-on-function-error and on-failure destinations apply to Kinesis and DynamoDB Streams event sources, not SQS. Option C requires custom retry logic and DynamoDB state management, adding complexity when native DLQ handling exists. Option D switches to FIFO queues which doesn't solve the poison message problem and adds ordering constraints.

stem: A company runs a serverless application using API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB. The operations team needs end-to-end visibility into request latency, error rates by endpoint, and DynamoDB throttling events. Which TWO services should be configured together to provide comprehensive observability?

options.text: Deploy Amazon Managed Grafana with the CloudWatch data source plugin configured for the production account. Create Grafana dashboards displaying API Gateway latency percentiles, Lambda concurrent execution metrics, and DynamoDB ConsumedReadCapacityUnits over time.

Enable AWS X-Ray active tracing on API Gateway and Lambda functions. Instrument the Lambda function code with the X-Ray SDK to create subsegments for DynamoDB calls and enable the X-Ray service map to visualize latency distribution across all components.

Enable Amazon CloudWatch ServiceLens to aggregate metrics, logs, and traces into a unified observability view. Configure ServiceLens resource health monitoring for the Lambda functions and DynamoDB tables to correlate performance anomalies across the application stack.

Configure API Gateway access logging with detailed request and response fields sent to CloudWatch Logs. Create CloudWatch Logs Insights queries to compute p50 and p99 latency by endpoint, error rates by HTTP status code, and correlation with DynamoDB throttle events.

explanation: X-Ray provides distributed tracing with service maps showing latency across API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB (A). CloudWatch Logs with API Gateway access logging and Logs Insights queries provide detailed per-endpoint analytics and error rate tracking (C). Option B describes ServiceLens which depends on X-Ray traces and CloudWatch data but doesn't configure the underlying data collection. Option D provides visualization but Grafana alone doesn't collect observability data without the underlying metrics and traces being configured first.

stem: A company needs to automatically remediate security group rules that allow unrestricted SSH access (0.0.0.0/0 on port 22) within 5 minutes of creation. The remediation must work across all AWS accounts in the organization and log all remediation actions for audit. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy the AWS Config managed rule restricted-ssh across all accounts using a conformance pack via AWS Organizations. Configure auto-remediation with the AWS-DisablePublicAccessForSecurityGroup SSM Automation document and log remediation actions to a centralized CloudTrail trail.

Enable AWS Security Hub across all accounts with the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard. Configure custom actions for non-compliant security group findings and create an EventBridge rule that triggers automated remediation through a cross-account Lambda function.

Deploy Amazon GuardDuty across all accounts using a delegated administrator. Configure GuardDuty to detect unrestricted security group changes as a custom threat intelligence indicator and use a Step Functions workflow to revoke the offending rules and notify the team.

Create an EventBridge rule in each account that matches AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress API calls from CloudTrail. Target a Lambda function that checks if the rule allows 0.0.0.0/0 on port 22 and calls RevokeSecurityGroupIngress, then publishes audit events to a central SNS topic.

explanation: AWS Config's restricted-ssh managed rule detects unrestricted SSH rules, and deploying via Organizations conformance pack provides multi-account coverage. Auto-remediation with SSM Automation removes the offending rules within the Config evaluation cycle. Option B requires deploying EventBridge rules and Lambda functions individually in each account. Option C detects via Security Hub but requires additional custom actions and cross-account Lambda setup for remediation. Option D uses GuardDuty which doesn't natively detect security group misconfigurations.

stem: A company needs to implement least-privilege access for its CI/CD pipeline that deploys CloudFormation stacks. The pipeline runs in a tools account and deploys to staging and production accounts using cross-account IAM roles. How should the cross-account deployment roles be configured to follow least privilege?

options.text: Create IAM roles in staging and production accounts with CloudFormation service-linked role permissions. Configure the roles with a permissions boundary that limits the maximum permissions to the specific services used in the CloudFormation templates.

Create IAM roles in staging and production accounts with inline policies that allow only the specific CloudFormation, EC2, S3, and IAM actions required by the stacks. Configure trust policies that allow only the tools account's pipeline role ARN with an external ID condition.

Create a single IAM role in the tools account with cross-account resource policies on each target account's CloudFormation stacks. Grant cloudformation:* and iam:PassRole permissions scoped to the specific stack ARNs in each target account using resource-based conditions.

Create IAM roles in staging and production accounts with the AdministratorAccess managed policy attached. Configure trust policies that allow the tools account's root principal and add an IP address condition restricting access to the tools account's NAT Gateway Elastic IPs.

explanation: Inline policies with specific actions and trust policies restricted to the pipeline role ARN with external ID provide least privilege. Option B uses AdministratorAccess which violates least privilege, and IP conditions on IAM trust policies don't effectively restrict cross-account access. Option C tries to use resource-based policies on CloudFormation, which don't support cross-account access the same way. Option D's service-linked roles are managed by AWS and can't be customized for pipeline-specific permissions.

stem: A team uses AWS CodePipeline with a GitHub source action. They want to require that all pull requests pass automated tests in CodeBuild before merging, and that only merged code from the main branch triggers production deployments. Which configuration implements this workflow?

options.text: Configure a CodePipeline triggered by GitHub webhook events on the main branch for production deployments. Separately, create a CodeBuild project triggered by GitHub pull request webhook events to run tests and report status checks back to the GitHub pull request.

Configure CodePipeline with two source actions: one for pull requests that triggers a CodeBuild test stage, and one for main branch pushes that triggers the full deployment pipeline. Use a CodePipeline manual approval action between the test and deploy stages.

Configure CodePipeline with a GitHub source action on all branches. Add a CodeBuild stage that checks the branch name from the CODEBUILD_WEBHOOK_HEAD_REF environment variable and conditionally executes tests for PRs or deployment for the main branch pushes.

Configure CodePipeline with a GitHub source action using GitHub Actions as the CI provider. Create a GitHub Actions workflow that runs tests on pull requests and triggers the CodePipeline execution via AWS CLI only when tests pass on the main branch.

explanation: Separate CodeBuild projects triggered by PR webhooks handle pre-merge testing, while CodePipeline triggered by main branch changes handles production deployment. This separates concerns cleanly. Option B's dual source actions in a single pipeline don't work as described since CodePipeline triggers on any source change. Option C uses branch checking in CodeBuild which is fragile and doesn't properly integrate with GitHub PR status checks. Option D introduces GitHub Actions as an external dependency when AWS-native services handle the workflow.

stem: A company uses AWS CloudFormation to deploy a VPC with public and private subnets, NAT gateways, and route tables. The template frequently fails during updates because of dependency issues between route table associations and NAT gateway replacements. Which CloudFormation feature resolves the dependency ordering problem?

options.text: Use CloudFormation resource import to manage existing VPC resources instead of updating them in place. Create a change set preview before each update to identify potential dependency conflicts and manually reorder resource operations in the change set execution.

Refactor the template to use CloudFormation nested stacks, separating the VPC, subnet, NAT gateway, and route table resources into individual child stacks. Use stack outputs and cross-stack references with Fn::ImportValue to establish explicit dependency chains.

Add UpdateReplacePolicy and DeletionPolicy attributes set to Retain on NAT gateway and route table resources. Use Fn::GetAtt instead of Ref to reference NAT gateway attributes in route table entries, ensuring CloudFormation infers the correct dependency graph.

Add explicit DependsOn attributes to route table association resources referencing the NAT gateway resources. Define a CreationPolicy on the NAT gateway with a ResourceSignal timeout of 10 minutes to ensure the NAT gateway is fully available before route creation.

explanation: Explicit DependsOn attributes establish the correct resource creation and update order. CreationPolicy with ResourceSignal ensures the NAT gateway is operational before dependent routes are configured. Option B's resource import doesn't address dependency ordering during updates. Option C's nested stacks add complexity but cross-stack references still face the same dependency issues. Option D's Retain policies prevent cleanup but don't resolve the ordering problem, and Fn::GetAtt vs Ref doesn't change dependency inference for this scenario.

stem: A company operates an event-driven architecture where an API Gateway receives orders, publishes them to an SNS topic, and multiple SQS queues subscribe for different processing pipelines. During a traffic spike, some orders were lost because the SQS queues reached their maximum message size. Which design change prevents order loss during traffic spikes?

options.text: Add Amazon Kinesis Data Streams between the API Gateway and SNS topic to buffer incoming orders. Configure the Kinesis stream with on-demand capacity mode and set the retention period to 7 days to handle sustained traffic spikes without losing messages.

Replace the SNS-to-SQS fan-out with Amazon EventBridge as the central event bus. Configure EventBridge rules to route orders to target SQS queues and enable EventBridge's built-in dead-letter queue for failed deliveries with automatic retry for up to 24 hours.

Increase the SQS queue maximum message retention period to 14 days and enable long polling with a 20-second wait time. Configure the consumer Lambda functions with reserved concurrency matching the expected peak throughput to process messages faster during spikes.

Configure the SNS topic with a delivery retry policy that includes exponential backoff with a maximum of 100 retries over 24 hours. Enable server-side encryption on the SNS topic and SQS queues, and set the SQS queue visibility timeout to 5 minutes.

explanation: Kinesis Data Streams with on-demand capacity mode provides elastic buffering that absorbs traffic spikes. The 7-day retention ensures orders persist even if downstream processing is slow. Option A switches to EventBridge but doesn't fundamentally solve the throughput issue if queues are overwhelmed. Option C increases retention but doesn't address the root cause of queues being overwhelmed during ingestion. Option D improves delivery retry but doesn't add buffering capacity to handle the spike volume.

stem: A company wants to detect anomalous behavior in its AWS account, such as unusual API call patterns, unexpected resource provisioning, or access from unfamiliar IP addresses. The detection must be automated and require minimal configuration. Which service provides this capability with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Deploy CloudWatch Anomaly Detection on key CloudTrail metrics including API call counts by service, error rates, and unique source IP addresses. Create CloudWatch alarms that trigger when metrics deviate from the anomaly detection band by more than 2 standard deviations.

Create a Kinesis Data Analytics application that processes CloudTrail events in real-time using SQL queries. Implement sliding window aggregations to detect unusual API call volumes and source IP patterns, and send alerts through an SNS topic when anomalies are detected.

Configure Amazon Detective to automatically investigate security findings from CloudTrail and VPC Flow Logs. Use Detective's behavioral graph to identify anomalous patterns and create custom detection rules based on historical baseline analysis of account activity.

Enable Amazon GuardDuty in all accounts and Regions. GuardDuty uses machine learning to analyze CloudTrail management events, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs to detect threats and anomalies, providing findings with severity levels and recommended remediation actions.

explanation: GuardDuty is a fully managed threat detection service that uses ML to analyze CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs with no infrastructure management required. It automatically detects anomalous behavior with minimal configuration. Option B is for investigation of existing findings, not detection. Option C requires manual metric selection and alarm configuration for each anomaly type. Option D requires building and maintaining a custom real-time analytics application.

stem: A company uses AWS Systems Manager Incident Manager to handle production incidents. The team needs to ensure that when a critical CloudWatch alarm triggers, an incident is automatically created, the on-call engineer is paged, a response plan is activated, and all actions are documented in a timeline. Which configuration achieves this?

options.text: Configure the CloudWatch alarm to send notifications to an SNS topic subscribed by PagerDuty. Create a PagerDuty webhook integration that calls the Incident Manager CreateTimelineEvent API to log the alarm trigger and initiate the escalation process.

Configure AWS Chatbot integration with Incident Manager and the team's Slack workspace. Set up a CloudWatch alarm that sends notifications to the Chatbot SNS topic, and configure Chatbot to create incidents when team members react to the alarm notification in Slack.

Create an EventBridge rule matching CloudWatch alarm state changes. Target a Step Functions state machine that creates an Incident Manager incident via the StartIncident API, sends page notifications through SNS, and logs timeline events at each workflow step.

Create an Incident Manager response plan that defines the escalation path, runbook, and engagement contacts. Configure the CloudWatch alarm to trigger the response plan via an EventBridge rule target, automatically creating an incident and paging the on-call rotation.

explanation: Incident Manager response plans define the complete incident workflow including contacts, runbooks, and escalation. CloudWatch alarms can directly trigger response plans via EventBridge, automating incident creation and paging. Option B introduces PagerDuty as an unnecessary intermediary and requires custom API integration. Option C builds custom orchestration with Step Functions when Incident Manager natively handles the workflow. Option D requires manual Slack interaction, which doesn't meet the automatic requirement.

stem: A company needs to ensure that all data in transit between microservices running on Amazon ECS Fargate is encrypted using mutual TLS (mTLS). The services communicate over HTTP and the team wants to avoid modifying application code. Which solution implements mTLS without code changes?

options.text: Deploy AWS App Mesh with virtual services and virtual nodes for each microservice. Configure the App Mesh TLS policy to enforce mTLS using certificates from AWS Certificate Manager Private CA, with Envoy sidecar proxies handling the TLS termination transparently.

Install and configure Istio service mesh on the ECS cluster using the Istio ECS integration. Enable strict mTLS peer authentication policies across all namespaces and configure Istio's Citadel component to automatically provision and rotate certificates for each service.

Deploy Amazon API Gateway as an internal REST API between each microservice pair. Enable mutual TLS on the API Gateway custom domain name with a truststore in S3 and configure each service to communicate through its dedicated API Gateway endpoint.

Configure an Application Load Balancer with mutual TLS authentication enabled on each listener. Import client certificates into ACM and configure the ALB to validate client certificates against a trust store containing the CA certificate chain for each microservice.

explanation: AWS App Mesh provides a managed service mesh with Envoy sidecar proxies that handle mTLS transparently without application code changes. ACM Private CA integration provides automated certificate management. Option B uses ALB mTLS but requires routing all inter-service traffic through ALBs which adds latency and doesn't scale for service-to-service communication.
