Deploy Aurora Global Database with a secondary cluster in the DR Region. Configure ElastiCache Global Datastore for cross-Region replication. Use CloudFormation StackSets to deploy the ECS infrastructure in the DR Region and automate failover with Route 53 health checks.

Deploy an active-active architecture with Aurora Multi-Master across both Regions. Configure ElastiCache with client-side data sharding across both Regions and deploy identical ECS services in both Regions behind a Global Accelerator for automatic traffic routing.

Configure Aurora cross-Region read replicas and take automated snapshots every 5 minutes using AWS Backup. Deploy a standby ElastiCache cluster in the DR Region with daily snapshot restores and maintain a cold ECS task definition ready to deploy on failover initiation.

explanation: Aurora Global Database provides sub-second replication (well within 5-minute RPO). ElastiCache Global Datastore replicates cache data cross-Region. Pre-deployed ECS infrastructure via StackSets enables 30-minute RTO. Route 53 automates DNS failover. Option B's 5-minute backup snapshots may miss the RPO boundary and cold ECS deployment exceeds the RTO. Option C uses custom MySQL replication and custom cache replication which adds operational complexity. Option D's Aurora Multi-Master doesn't support cross-Region multi-master configurations.

stem: A company's application team reports that their Lambda function's cold starts are causing SLA violations. The team needs to establish a baseline for cold start frequency and duration, and set up alerting when cold starts exceed acceptable levels. Which monitoring approach provides cold start-specific metrics and alerting?

options.text: Enable Lambda Insights by adding the Lambda Insights extension layer to the function. Lambda Insights reports init_duration metrics separately, allowing baseline establishment through the multi-function dashboard and alarm creation on the init duration percentile statistics.

Configure AWS X-Ray tracing on the Lambda function and analyze the Initialization subsegment duration. Create an X-Ray group filtering for traces containing Initialization subsegments and set up a CloudWatch alarm on the X-Ray group's fault rate metric.

Create a CloudWatch Logs metric filter on the Lambda function's log group matching the 'Init Duration' field in REPORT log lines. Extract the init duration value as a custom metric with dimensions for function name and version, and create alarms on the metric's p99 statistic.

Enable CloudWatch Application Signals for the Lambda function to track cold start metrics as part of SLO monitoring. Configure an availability SLO that accounts for cold start latency and set up error budget burn rate alerts when cold starts cause SLA violations.

explanation: Lambda Insights provides dedicated init_duration metrics with percentile statistics, enabling precise cold start monitoring and alerting. The multi-function dashboard shows cold start trends for baselining. Option A uses custom metric filters which require manual configuration and maintenance. Option C provides trace-level cold start data but doesn't aggregate into metrics suitable for continuous monitoring and alerting. Option D's Application Signals tracks overall SLO but doesn't provide granular cold start-specific metrics.

stem: A company deployed a new version of their ECS service that introduced a subtle memory leak. The service runs correctly for 2-3 hours before containers start getting OOMKilled. The development team needs the containers to be automatically replaced when they approach the memory limit, while also preserving diagnostic data for debugging. Which approach provides both automatic recovery and diagnostics?

options.text: Configure a CloudWatch alarm on the ECS service's MemoryUtilization metric with a threshold at 85%. Set the alarm action to trigger an ECS service update that forces a new deployment, replacing all tasks. Configure CloudWatch Container Insights to capture per-container memory trends.

Configure ECS Exec on the service to enable remote debugging. When containers approach the memory limit, have the on-call team use ECS Exec to trigger a heap dump and manually stop the task. Set up a CloudWatch alarm on MemoryUtilization to alert the team before OOMKill.

Configure the ECS task definition with a container health check that monitors memory usage via a custom health check script. When memory exceeds 80% of the limit, the health check fails, ECS replaces the task, and CloudWatch Container Insights captures memory metrics for analysis.

Deploy a sidecar container that monitors the application container's memory usage via the Docker stats API. When memory exceeds 80%, the sidecar writes a heap dump to an EFS mount, then calls the ECS StopTask API to trigger task replacement by the ECS scheduler.

explanation: ECS container health checks with custom scripts detect high memory usage before OOMKill. Failed health checks trigger automatic task replacement by ECS. Container Insights preserves memory utilization history for debugging. Option B triggers a full service redeployment which is disruptive when only individual containers need replacement. Option C adds sidecar complexity and doesn't capture heap dumps natively in Fargate (Docker stats API isn't accessible). Option D requires manual intervention which doesn't provide automatic recovery.

stem: A company needs to ensure that all VPC security groups in their production accounts do not allow inbound traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 on any port except port 443. Non-compliant security groups must be automatically remediated within 10 minutes of detection. Which solution provides real-time detection and auto-remediation?

options.text: Create an SCP in AWS Organizations that denies AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress for rules with CidrIp 0.0.0.0/0 unless the FromPort and ToPort are both 443. Apply the SCP to the production organizational unit to prevent non-compliant security group rules from being created.

Deploy the AWS Config managed rule vpc-sg-open-only-to-authorized-ports with the authorized port set to 443. Configure auto-remediation with the AWS-RevokeSecurityGroupIngress SSM Automation document and set the remediation retry to automatic with a 5-minute timeout.

Enable Amazon GuardDuty to detect security groups with unrestricted access. Configure an EventBridge rule matching GuardDuty findings of type Recon:EC2/PortProbeUnprotectedPort and trigger a Lambda function that revokes the offending security group rules automatically.

Create an EventBridge rule matching AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress CloudTrail events. Target a Lambda function that evaluates the new rule and calls RevokeSecurityGroupIngress for rules allowing 0.0.0.0/0 on any port other than 443, executing within seconds of the API call.

explanation: EventBridge rules matching CloudTrail API events provide near-real-time detection (within seconds) of security group changes. The Lambda function immediately evaluates and revokes non-compliant rules. Option B uses AWS Config which evaluates periodically, potentially exceeding the 10-minute remediation window. Option C prevents creation but doesn't remediate existing non-compliant rules. Option D uses GuardDuty which detects actual port probing activity, not security group configuration violations.

stem: A company has a mobile application backend with APIs deployed on API Gateway and Lambda. The team wants to implement A/B testing of new API features by routing a percentage of mobile app traffic to a new API version while the rest continues using the stable version. Which approach enables API-level A/B testing?

options.text: Create a new API Gateway stage for the new version and configure the mobile application to randomly select between stage URLs based on a client-side percentage. Collect response metrics from both stages using API Gateway access logging and compare performance in CloudWatch.

Use AWS AppConfig feature flags in the Lambda function to control feature availability. Deploy a single Lambda version that checks AppConfig at invocation time and executes the new or old code path based on the feature flag's percentage rollout configuration.

Deploy the new Lambda function version and create an API Gateway canary deployment on the production stage. Configure the canary to route the specified percentage of traffic to the new version, with API Gateway handling the traffic split transparently to the mobile application.

Configure Amazon CloudFront in front of API Gateway with a Lambda@Edge function that inspects request headers. Route a percentage of requests to the new API Gateway stage based on a hashed user ID value, maintaining consistent routing for the same user across requests.

explanation: API Gateway canary deployments provide native traffic splitting between the current and canary deployment on the same stage. The mobile app doesn't need modification and API Gateway handles routing transparently. Option A requires mobile app changes for client-side routing. Option C adds CloudFront and Lambda@Edge complexity for what API Gateway provides natively. Option D uses feature flags in code which doesn't provide separate API versions with independent monitoring.

stem: A company uses Terraform and wants to prevent accidental destruction of critical production resources like RDS databases and S3 buckets. Developers should not be able to run terraform destroy on these resources, even if they modify the Terraform configuration. Which Terraform feature prevents accidental resource destruction?

options.text: Implement a Terraform wrapper script in the CI/CD pipeline that parses the terraform plan output for resource deletions. The script rejects plans containing destroy actions for resources tagged as critical and only allows terraform apply when no critical deletions are detected.

Add lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true } to critical resource blocks in the Terraform configuration. This meta-argument causes Terraform to reject any plan that would result in destroying the resource, including plan changes that require replacement and explicit destroy commands.

Configure the Terraform backend with a state lock using DynamoDB and restrict IAM permissions for the terraform destroy command. Create an IAM policy that denies the dynamodb:DeleteItem action on the state lock table, preventing the state from being modified for deletions.

Use Terraform workspaces to separate production resources from other environments. Configure workspace-specific variable files that set a custom 'protected' variable and add conditional logic in the configuration that prevents destruction when the protected variable is true.

explanation: The prevent_destroy lifecycle meta-argument is a Terraform-native feature that causes Terraform to reject any plan that would destroy the resource, providing a direct protection mechanism. Option B restricts state locking but doesn't specifically prevent resource destruction. Option C uses workspace variables which are a workaround rather than a built-in protection feature. Option D adds CI/CD pipeline checks but can be bypassed by running Terraform locally.

stem: A company runs AWS Lambda functions that are invoked by API Gateway. During traffic spikes, some requests receive HTTP 429 throttling responses because the Lambda function hits its concurrent execution limit. The company wants to handle traffic spikes gracefully without returning errors to users. Which approach absorbs traffic spikes?

options.text: Configure an SQS queue between API Gateway and Lambda using API Gateway service integration. API Gateway sends requests to SQS which buffers them, and Lambda processes the queue asynchronously. Return an immediate 202 Accepted response with a request tracking ID.

Configure Lambda function aliases with weighted routing between the primary function and an overflow function in a secondary Region. When the primary function's ConcurrentExecutions metric exceeds 80% of the limit, Route 53 shifts overflow traffic to the secondary Region.

Configure API Gateway with a usage plan that has a high burst limit and steady-state rate limit. Enable API Gateway response caching with a 60-second TTL for GET requests and configure a custom 429 response template that returns cached data instead of an error.

Increase the Lambda function's reserved concurrency to the maximum account limit and enable provisioned concurrency for the expected peak traffic baseline. Configure API Gateway throttling at a rate matching the provisioned concurrency to prevent overflow beyond Lambda capacity.

explanation: SQS buffering between API Gateway and Lambda absorbs traffic spikes by queuing requests. The 202 Accepted response provides immediate feedback while Lambda processes the queue at its available concurrency. Option A caches responses but only works for identical GET requests. Option C increases concurrency limits but still has a ceiling and provisioned concurrency is expensive. Option D adds cross-Region complexity and Route 53 DNS changes are too slow for real-time traffic management.

stem: A company operates an AWS environment with 100 EC2 instances running Windows Server. The operations team needs to collect Windows Event Logs (Application, Security, System) and IIS access logs from all instances and make them searchable in a centralized logging system. Which approach collects and centralizes Windows logs efficiently?

options.text: Install the CloudWatch agent on all Windows instances configured to collect Windows Event Logs by channel name and IIS log files by path. Configure the agent to publish logs to CloudWatch Logs log groups organized by instance and log type for centralized search via Logs Insights.

Install the Kinesis Data Firehose agent on all Windows instances to stream IIS access logs to a Firehose delivery stream. Configure the Windows Event Forwarding (WEF) feature to centralize event logs to a collector instance that forwards to CloudWatch Logs using the agent.

Configure SSM State Manager to run a PowerShell script that exports Windows Event Logs to CSV files on a 5-minute schedule. Upload the CSV files to an S3 bucket using the AWS CLI and use Amazon Athena to query the exported log data with SQL for centralized analysis.

Deploy a Fluentd agent on each Windows instance configured to tail Windows Event Logs and IIS log files. Route the logs to Amazon OpenSearch Service through a Kinesis Data Stream buffer and use OpenSearch Dashboards for centralized search and visualization.

explanation: The CloudWatch agent natively supports Windows Event Log collection by channel name and file-based log collection for IIS logs. CloudWatch Logs Insights provides centralized search. Option B uses scripts and CSV export which is fragile and has latency. Option C requires multiple tools (Firehose agent for files, WEF for events) which adds complexity. Option D uses Fluentd which has limited Windows support compared to the native CloudWatch agent.

stem: A company needs to create a comprehensive incident management workflow that includes automated detection, notification, escalation, and post-incident analysis. The workflow must integrate with their existing PagerDuty setup for on-call management. Which TWO AWS services form the foundation of this incident management workflow?

options.text: Use Amazon EventBridge to route CloudWatch alarm state changes to incident management targets. Create EventBridge rules matching critical alarms and configure PagerDuty as an API destination target for automated incident creation with event details passed as the request payload.

Use Amazon DevOps Guru for automated anomaly detection across AWS resources using machine learning. Configure DevOps Guru to detect operational anomalies and generate insights that trigger EventBridge rules, routing anomaly notifications to PagerDuty for on-call incident management.

Use AWS Systems Manager Incident Manager to define response plans with escalation contacts and runbooks. Configure PagerDuty integration through the Incident Manager engagement settings and automate incident creation from CloudWatch alarms via EventBridge rules targeting response plans.

Use AWS Systems Manager OpsCenter to create OpsItems from CloudWatch alarms and operational events. Configure OpsCenter to aggregate related findings and integrate with PagerDuty using a Lambda function that creates PagerDuty incidents when high-severity OpsItems are created.

explanation: Incident Manager provides structured incident response with escalation, runbooks, and PagerDuty integration (A). DevOps Guru detects operational anomalies using ML, complementing CloudWatch alarms with proactive detection (D). Option B routes events to PagerDuty but lacks the incident lifecycle management that Incident Manager provides. Option C uses OpsCenter which is an operational item tracker, not a full incident management workflow system.

stem: A company needs to implement a zero-trust network architecture for their VPC-based application. All traffic between services must be authenticated and authorized, even within the same VPC. Which AWS service enables zero-trust networking for VPC workloads?

options.text: Deploy Amazon VPC Lattice to create a service network connecting all application services. Configure Lattice auth policies that authenticate service-to-service communication using IAM SigV4 and define authorization rules that specify which services can communicate with each other.

Deploy AWS Verified Access to provide zero-trust access to application endpoints. Configure Verified Access policies that evaluate device posture and identity provider context before granting access, replacing traditional VPN-based and network-perimeter-based access controls.

Deploy AWS Network Firewall in each VPC subnet to inspect all intra-VPC traffic. Create stateful rule groups that match service-to-service communication patterns and implement deep packet inspection with TLS decryption to verify application-layer authentication tokens.

Configure VPC security groups with strict ingress rules that reference specific security group IDs for each allowed service-to-service communication path. Enable VPC Flow Logs with enriched metadata including security group information to audit all intra-VPC traffic flows.

explanation: VPC Lattice provides service-to-service networking with built-in IAM SigV4 authentication and authorization policies. It implements zero-trust at the service networking layer with fine-grained access controls. Option A's Verified Access is designed for user-to-application access (replacing VPN), not service-to-service communication. Option C's Network Firewall operates at the network layer and doesn't provide service identity-based authentication. Option D uses security groups which provide network-level access control but not authentication or identity-based authorization.

stem: A company uses AWS CodePipeline to deploy infrastructure changes using CloudFormation. Before deploying to production, the team wants to automatically test the infrastructure changes by deploying to a temporary test stack, running integration tests against it, and then deleting the test stack. Which pipeline design implements this test-in-production pattern?

options.text: Create a parallel CodePipeline that deploys to a permanent test environment. Run integration tests in the parallel pipeline and configure the production pipeline with a manual approval that references the test pipeline's execution results before allowing production deployment.

Add three sequential actions in a test stage: a CloudFormation CREATE_UPDATE action to deploy the test stack, a CodeBuild action to run integration tests against the test stack endpoints, and a CloudFormation DELETE_ONLY action to tear down the test stack after tests complete.

Use AWS Step Functions to orchestrate the test workflow: create stack, wait for completion, run tests, evaluate results, and delete stack. Invoke the Step Functions execution from a CodePipeline Lambda action and poll for the execution result before proceeding.

Add a CodeBuild action in the pipeline that uses the AWS CLI to create a test CloudFormation stack, runs integration tests, and deletes the stack in a single build phase. Use buildspec environment variables to pass the stack endpoint to the test scripts.

explanation: CodePipeline natively supports CloudFormation actions for stack creation, testing via CodeBuild, and stack deletion in sequential actions within a stage. This provides clean lifecycle management of the test stack. Option B uses a permanent test environment which is not the ephemeral test-and-destroy pattern requested. Option C puts all logic in one CodeBuild which is harder to debug and doesn't leverage CodePipeline's native CloudFormation integration. Option D adds Step Functions complexity when CodePipeline actions handle the workflow natively.

stem: A company's CloudFormation template needs to conditionally create resources based on the target environment. In production, the template should create a Multi-AZ RDS instance with 500 GB storage, while in development it should create a single-AZ db.t3.micro instance with 20 GB storage. Which CloudFormation feature handles this conditional resource configuration?

options.text: Define a CloudFormation Condition named IsProduction using Fn::Equals to check the Environment parameter. Use Fn::If in resource properties to select between production values (Multi-AZ, 500GB) and development values (single-AZ, 20GB) based on the condition evaluation.

Use CloudFormation nested stacks with environment-specific child templates. Create a parent template that accepts an Environment parameter and uses Fn::If to select which nested stack template URL to deploy, choosing between production and development child stacks.

Create separate CloudFormation templates for production and development environments. Maintain each template independently with environment-specific resource configurations and use CodePipeline to select the appropriate template based on the deployment target environment.

Define a template parameter named Environment with AllowedValues of 'prod' and 'dev'. Create CloudFormation Mappings that map each environment to the appropriate instance class, storage, and Multi-AZ settings. Reference the mappings in resource properties using Fn::FindInMap.

explanation: CloudFormation Conditions with Fn::If allow conditional property values within a single template. The IsProduction condition evaluates the Environment parameter and Fn::If selects the appropriate values for each resource property. Option A uses Mappings which work for simple lookups but don't handle boolean properties like Multi-AZ as cleanly as Conditions. Option B duplicates templates which violates DRY principles and increases maintenance burden. Option D adds nested stack complexity when Conditions handle the requirement in a single template.

stem: A company's Lambda function processes events from multiple SQS queues with different priority levels. High-priority events must be processed before low-priority events, but currently all queues are processed with equal concurrency. Which approach implements priority-based queue processing?

options.text: Implement a Step Functions workflow that polls both SQS queues. The workflow checks the high-priority queue first; if messages exist, it invokes the processing Lambda. Only when the high-priority queue is empty does it process messages from the low-priority queue in each iteration.

Create separate Lambda functions for each priority queue. Configure the high-priority function with a higher reserved concurrency allocation and the low-priority function with a lower reserved concurrency. When the high-priority queue is empty, unreserved concurrency serves low-priority.

Consolidate all events into a single SQS FIFO queue with message group IDs based on priority level. Configure a single Lambda consumer that processes messages in FIFO order with high-priority group IDs processed first using message group-level parallelism settings.

Configure the Lambda event source mapping for the high-priority queue with a higher batch size and shorter maximum batching window. Set reserved concurrency for the high-priority queue's Lambda function at 80% of total concurrency, leaving 20% for low-priority processing.

explanation: Separate Lambda functions with different reserved concurrency allocations ensure high-priority queue processing has dedicated capacity. When the high-priority queue is empty, its concurrency is available for other functions. Option A uses a single function which doesn't guarantee priority ordering. Option C's FIFO queue doesn't support priority ordering within message groups. Option D uses Step Functions polling which adds latency and doesn't scale as efficiently as native SQS-Lambda event source mappings.

stem: A company wants to implement proactive monitoring that detects operational issues before they impact users. The team needs automated anomaly detection that learns from historical patterns and alerts when metrics behave unexpectedly, without requiring manual threshold configuration for each metric. Which approach provides automated anomaly detection?

options.text: Enable Amazon DevOps Guru for the AWS account and select the CloudFormation stacks to monitor. DevOps Guru uses ML to analyze CloudWatch metrics, CloudTrail events, and operational data to detect anomalies and generate actionable insights with recommended remediation steps.

Configure CloudWatch Anomaly Detection on individual metrics by selecting metrics in the CloudWatch console and enabling anomaly detection. CloudWatch builds a model from 2 weeks of historical data and creates an anomaly detection band that adapts to daily and weekly patterns.

Create a SageMaker training job that builds a Random Cut Forest anomaly detection model from historical CloudWatch metric data. Deploy the model as a SageMaker endpoint and invoke it from a Lambda function on a 1-minute schedule to evaluate current metric values against the model.

Deploy Amazon Lookout for Metrics to monitor CloudWatch metrics for anomalies. Configure data sources pointing to CloudWatch metric streams and define measures and dimensions for the metrics to monitor. Lookout uses ML to detect anomalies and sends alerts via SNS.

explanation: DevOps Guru provides fully automated ML-based anomaly detection across all resources in monitored CloudFormation stacks. It learns from historical patterns without manual metric selection or threshold configuration, and provides actionable insights. Option B requires manually enabling anomaly detection on each metric individually. Option C uses Lookout for Metrics which requires configuring specific metrics and dimensions. Option D builds custom ML infrastructure for what DevOps Guru provides as a managed service.

stem: A company needs to implement automated capacity management for their DynamoDB tables. When a table approaches its provisioned capacity limit, the system should proactively scale up before throttling occurs. The current Auto Scaling is reactive and scale-up takes too long during sudden traffic increases. Which solution provides proactive capacity management?

options.text: Implement scheduled scaling using Application Auto Scaling scheduled actions for DynamoDB. Define scaling schedules based on known traffic patterns (business hours, batch processing windows) and configure the scheduled actions to pre-scale capacity 15 minutes before expected peaks.

Switch DynamoDB tables to on-demand capacity mode which eliminates the need for capacity planning entirely. On-demand mode scales instantly to accommodate any traffic level without provisioning and charges per request, removing the risk of throttling during traffic spikes.

Configure DynamoDB Auto Scaling with a lower target utilization of 50% instead of the default 70%. This triggers scaling at a lower threshold, providing more headroom before capacity is exhausted. Set the minimum and maximum capacity units to accommodate expected traffic ranges.

Create CloudWatch alarms on DynamoDB ConsumedReadCapacityUnits and ConsumedWriteCapacityUnits metrics using anomaly detection. When consumption anomalously increases, trigger a Lambda function that calls the UpdateTable API to increase provisioned capacity before throttling starts.

explanation: DynamoDB on-demand mode eliminates capacity planning entirely by instantly scaling to handle any traffic level. There's no provisioned capacity to manage or throttle against. Option A reduces the utilization target but still requires time for Auto Scaling to respond. Option B adds custom scaling logic that may be too slow during rapid traffic increases. Option D uses scheduled scaling which only works for predictable traffic patterns and doesn't handle unexpected spikes.

stem: A company operates a multi-account environment and needs to prevent any account from launching EC2 instances without an instance profile attached. Instances without instance profiles pose a security risk because they cannot assume IAM roles for AWS API access and may lead to developers hardcoding credentials. Which approach enforces this?

options.text: Deploy an AWS Config rule that evaluates whether EC2 instances have an associated instance profile. Configure auto-remediation with an SSM Automation document that stops instances without instance profiles and sends an SNS notification to the instance owner for remediation.

Create a CloudFormation hook that validates EC2 instance resources include an IamInstanceProfile property before allowing stack operations. Register the hook as a pre-create and pre-update hook type targeting AWS::EC2::Instance resources across all accounts via StackSets.

Create an SCP in AWS Organizations that denies ec2:RunInstances unless the ec2:InstanceProfile condition key has a non-empty value. Apply the SCP to all member accounts in the organization, preventing the launch of EC2 instances without an attached instance profile.

Configure an EventBridge rule matching RunInstances CloudTrail events where the instance profile is empty. Target a Lambda function that immediately terminates the instance and sends a notification to the team explaining the instance profile requirement and how to re-launch correctly.

explanation: SCPs enforce the instance profile requirement at the organization level, preventing instance launches without a profile before the instance is created. Option B detects after launch and stops instances, causing disruption. Option C uses CloudFormation hooks which only cover CloudFormation-created instances, missing console and CLI launches. Option D terminates instances after launch which is disruptive and reactive.

stem: A company uses AWS CodePipeline with multiple stages including source, build, test, staging deploy, manual approval, and production deploy. Pipeline executions sometimes pile up, with multiple changes queued for approval. The team wants to ensure that only the latest approved change deploys to production, skipping intermediate changes. Which pipeline behavior configuration achieves this?

options.text: Add an EventBridge rule that detects when multiple pipeline executions are in the approval stage. Target a Lambda function that cancels all but the most recent execution using the StopPipelineExecution API, ensuring only the latest change awaits approval.

Enable CodePipeline's pipeline-level concurrency setting to allow only one execution at a time. Configure the pipeline type as V2 with a queued execution mode that processes changes in order, ensuring each change completes before the next one starts its execution.

Configure the CodePipeline execution mode to SUPERSEDED. When a newer pipeline execution enters a stage, it supersedes older executions waiting in that stage. This ensures only the latest change proceeds through approval and deployment to production.

Configure the CodePipeline with a Lambda invoke action before the approval stage that checks for newer pending executions. If a newer execution exists, the Lambda function calls StopPipelineExecution for the current execution, allowing only the latest to proceed to approval.

explanation: CodePipeline's SUPERSEDED execution mode automatically replaces older executions in a stage when a newer one arrives. This native behavior ensures only the latest change proceeds without custom logic. Option B adds custom Lambda logic for what the pipeline handles natively. Option C's queued mode processes all changes sequentially rather than skipping intermediate ones. Option D adds external monitoring when the native superseded mode handles this directly.

stem: A company manages VPC networking infrastructure using Terraform. The networking team needs to provide VPC, subnet, and security group IDs to application teams who manage their own Terraform configurations in separate state files. How should the networking team share infrastructure references with application teams?

options.text: Define Terraform outputs in the networking module for VPC ID, subnet IDs, and security group IDs. Configure the networking state in an S3 backend with read-only access for application teams. Application teams use terraform_remote_state data source to read the networking outputs.

Store the VPC, subnet, and security group IDs in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store after the networking Terraform apply completes. Application teams use the aws_ssm_parameter data source in their Terraform configurations to retrieve the values from Parameter Store.

Tag all networking resources with standardized tags including environment and tier information. Application teams use aws_vpc, aws_subnet, and aws_security_group data sources with tag-based filters to look up the networking resources in their Terraform configurations.

Create a shared Terraform module that encapsulates the networking resources and is referenced by both the networking and application teams. Configure the module with a shared DynamoDB table that stores the resource IDs as outputs for cross-team consumption.

explanation: Terraform remote state data source is the native mechanism for sharing outputs between separate Terraform configurations. S3 backend with read-only access ensures application teams can reference outputs without modifying the networking state. Option B adds Parameter Store as an intermediary when Terraform remote state handles this natively. Option C uses data source lookups which are fragile and depend on consistent tagging. Option D shares modules which couples configurations rather than sharing outputs.

stem: A company runs an API that writes to Amazon DynamoDB. The API receives 50,000 writes per second during peak hours. Write operations occasionally fail with ConditionalCheckFailedException because multiple requests try to update the same item simultaneously. Which approach handles concurrent write conflicts efficiently?

options.text: Implement a distributed locking mechanism using ElastiCache for Redis with the SETNX command. Before each DynamoDB write, acquire a Redis lock on the item's key, perform the update, and release the lock. Configure lock TTL to prevent deadlocks from failed releases.

Implement optimistic locking using a version attribute in each DynamoDB item. Use conditional expressions that check the version number before updating, and retry the write with the latest version if a ConditionalCheckFailedException occurs, using exponential backoff with jitter.

Use DynamoDB transactions with TransactWriteItems to group related write operations atomically. Configure the transaction to include a condition check on the item's current state before applying the update, ensuring serializable isolation for all concurrent write operations.

Switch from DynamoDB to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with row-level locking. Configure Aurora with a connection pool using RDS Proxy and use SELECT FOR UPDATE to lock rows during read-modify-write operations, preventing concurrent update conflicts at the database level.

explanation: Optimistic locking with version attributes and conditional expressions is the DynamoDB best practice for handling concurrent writes. Retries with exponential backoff handle conflicts efficiently at scale. Option B migrates to a relational database which changes the architecture fundamentally and adds complexity. Option C adds Redis as a distributed lock which introduces a dependency and potential bottleneck at 50,000 WPS. Option D uses transactions which are more expensive (2x WCU) and add latency, overkill for simple concurrent update handling.

stem: A company needs to implement real-time application error tracking for their Node.js application running on ECS. The team wants to group similar errors together, track error frequency trends, and get notified when a new error type appears for the first time. Which approach provides these error tracking capabilities?

options.text: Configure the Node.js application to log errors in structured JSON format with stack traces to CloudWatch Logs. Create CloudWatch Logs metric filters matching error patterns and use CloudWatch anomaly detection on the error count metric to detect new error types.

Enable AWS X-Ray tracing and configure the Node.js application to capture exceptions as X-Ray fault annotations. Use X-Ray error groups to aggregate similar exceptions by error message and stack trace, and create CloudWatch alarms on X-Ray ErrorRate metrics for new error detection.

Configure CloudWatch Application Signals for the ECS service to automatically capture and group application errors. Application Signals tracks error rates by operation, detects new error patterns through its anomaly detection, and integrates with SLO monitoring for threshold-based alerts.

Instrument the application with the CloudWatch RUM (Real User Monitoring) SDK to capture client-side JavaScript errors. Configure RUM to group errors by error message and stack trace and send alerts when new error patterns are detected in the RUM dashboard.

explanation: CloudWatch Application Signals automatically captures application errors, groups them by operation, and provides anomaly detection for error rate changes. It detects new error patterns without manual metric filter configuration. Option A requires manual metric filter creation for each error pattern. Option B uses X-Ray which provides trace-level error data but doesn't natively group and track error types. Option C uses RUM which is for client-side browser monitoring, not server-side Node.js error tracking.

stem: A company's CloudFormation stack update failed and rolled back, but the rollback also failed, leaving the stack in UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED state. The team cannot update or delete the stack. Which approach recovers the stack from this state?

options.text: Delete the CloudFormation stack using the --retain-resources flag to preserve all underlying AWS resources. Recreate the stack with a corrected template that imports the existing resources using the resource import feature, re-establishing CloudFormation management.

Contact AWS Support to manually reset the stack state from UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED to UPDATE_COMPLETE. AWS Support has the ability to modify stack metadata directly in the CloudFormation service backend, allowing subsequent updates to proceed normally.

Use the CloudFormation ContinueUpdateRollback API with the ResourcesToSkip parameter to skip the resources causing the rollback failure. This allows CloudFormation to complete the rollback by ignoring problematic resources, returning the stack to UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE state.

Manually fix the underlying resource configuration that caused the rollback failure (such as restoring a deleted resource or correcting permissions). Then call the ContinueUpdateRollback API without skipping resources to allow CloudFormation to complete the rollback normally.

explanation: ContinueUpdateRollback with ResourcesToSkip allows CloudFormation to skip problematic resources and complete the rollback, recovering the stack. After recovery, the skipped resources can be addressed in a subsequent update. Option B deletes and recreates the stack which risks data loss and is more disruptive. Option C describes a manual AWS Support intervention that isn't the standard recovery process. Option D may work if the root cause is fixable, but skipping resources is faster and more reliable for immediate recovery.

stem: A company needs to implement a solution that scans all new AMIs for vulnerabilities and security misconfigurations before they are shared with development teams. Only AMIs that pass the security scan should be added to the approved AMI list. Which service automates the AMI security scanning pipeline?

options.text: Configure Amazon Inspector to scan EC2 instances launched from new AMIs automatically. Create an EventBridge rule matching Inspector scan completion events and trigger a Lambda function that evaluates findings and adds the AMI to an SSM Parameter Store approved list if it passes.

Create a CodePipeline that launches an EC2 instance from the new AMI, installs the Amazon Inspector agent, runs an assessment template, and evaluates findings. If no critical vulnerabilities are found, the pipeline shares the AMI using the ModifyImageAttribute API.

Use EC2 Image Builder with test components that run Amazon Inspector scans against the built AMI. Configure the pipeline to evaluate Inspector findings and only distribute the AMI to target accounts if no critical or high severity vulnerabilities are found in the scan results.

Deploy AWS Security Hub with automated security checks for EC2 AMIs. Configure Security Hub to evaluate AMI configurations against CIS benchmarks and the AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standard, flagging non-compliant AMIs for review before distribution.

explanation: EC2 Image Builder natively integrates with Amazon Inspector for vulnerability scanning as part of the image build pipeline. Test components evaluate scan results and conditionally distribute AMIs only if they pass security checks. Option B builds a custom pipeline when Image Builder provides this workflow natively. Option C scans instances after launch rather than scanning AMIs in a pipeline. Option D uses Security Hub which evaluates deployed resources, not AMI build artifacts.

stem: A company is implementing a CI/CD pipeline for a serverless application using AWS SAM and CodePipeline. The pipeline needs to deploy to three environments (dev, staging, production) with automated testing between each environment and manual approval before production. Which TWO pipeline configurations are needed?

options.text: Create separate CodePipeline pipelines for each environment triggered by different CodeCommit branches. The dev pipeline triggers on feature branches, staging on the develop branch, and production on the main branch, with each pipeline independently building and deploying.

Add a manual approval action between the TestStaging and DeployProduction stages. Configure the approval action with an SNS topic notification to the release manager, a review URL pointing to the staging endpoint, and a 24-hour timeout for approval expiration.

Configure CodePipeline with sequential stages: Source, Build (sam build and sam package), DeployDev (CloudFormation deploy with dev parameters), TestDev (CodeBuild integration tests), DeployStaging (CloudFormation deploy with staging parameters), and TestStaging (CodeBuild tests).

Configure each CloudFormation deploy action with the CHANGE_SET_REPLACE action mode instead of CREATE_UPDATE. This creates change sets that must be reviewed and executed separately, adding an implicit approval step before each environment deployment.

explanation: Sequential stages with environment-specific deployments and test stages between each provide automated testing across environments (A). Manual approval before production deployment ensures human oversight with configurable notification and timeout (B). Option C uses separate pipelines per branch which doesn't promote the same artifact through environments. Option D's change set review adds friction for dev and staging where automated deployment is desired.

stem: A company uses AWS CloudFormation with a template that creates an S3 bucket with a specific bucket name. When the team tries to update the stack to change a bucket property that requires replacement (like enabling bucket versioning on an existing bucket with a fixed name), the update fails because CloudFormation tries to create a new bucket with the same name. How should the team handle this?

options.text: Add an UpdateReplacePolicy of Retain to the S3 bucket resource. Update the stack to remove the bucket from the template (CloudFormation releases it without deleting), then re-import the bucket under a new logical ID with the updated configuration properties.

Configure the CloudFormation stack with a stack policy that prevents the S3 bucket resource from being replaced. The stack policy blocks replacement-type updates, and the team can then modify the template to use update-compatible property changes that don't require replacement.

Remove the explicit bucket name from the CloudFormation template and let CloudFormation auto-generate a unique name. This allows CloudFormation to create a new bucket during replacement without naming conflicts, though the bucket name will change with each replacement.

Manually enable versioning on the S3 bucket using the AWS CLI outside of CloudFormation. Run CloudFormation drift detection to confirm the configuration change, then update the CloudFormation template to match the current bucket state and update the stack to sync.

explanation: Manually enabling versioning outside CloudFormation avoids the replacement issue since versioning can be enabled without recreating the bucket. Updating the template to match and running drift detection ensures CloudFormation stays in sync. Option A changes the bucket name which breaks existing references to the bucket. Option B is complex and requires import/export operations. Option D blocks the update entirely without resolving the underlying configuration change.

stem: A company uses Amazon CloudFront to serve a single-page application (SPA) hosted on S3. When CloudFront returns a cached response during an S3 outage, users see stale content. After the outage, some users continue seeing stale content due to long cache TTLs. Which configuration provides the best balance of performance and freshness?

options.text: Configure CloudFront with a 24-hour TTL for all objects and implement cache invalidation through the CloudFront CreateInvalidation API after each S3 deployment. Create a CodePipeline post-deployment step that invalidates /* to clear all cached content globally.

Configure CloudFront with a TTL of 0 seconds for all objects to ensure every request goes to the S3 origin. Enable CloudFront origin shield to reduce the number of requests to S3 and configure S3 Transfer Acceleration for faster origin response times on cache misses.

Configure CloudFront with a cache policy that uses Cache-Control headers set by the S3 origin. Set HTML files to max-age=0, s-maxage=3600 with stale-while-revalidate=86400, and set static assets with content hashing in filenames to max-age=31536000 for immutable caching.

Configure CloudFront with a cache policy that uses query string-based cache busting. Append a version parameter to all asset URLs in the SPA and update the parameter with each deployment, forcing CloudFront to fetch new versions from S3 while keeping old versions cached.

explanation: Content-hash-based immutable caching for static assets provides optimal caching while ensuring freshness. HTML files with short s-maxage and stale-while-revalidate serve cached content during outages while revalidating in the background during normal operation. Option B's TTL of 0 eliminates caching benefits entirely. Option C's wildcard invalidation takes time to propagate globally and costs per invalidation path. Option D uses query string versioning which creates duplicate cached objects and doesn't handle HTML freshness.

stem: A company runs 50 AWS accounts and needs to detect when any account creates AWS resources that generate unexpected costs, such as large EC2 instances, provisioned IOPS EBS volumes, or NAT Gateways in unused Regions. The detection must happen within 1 hour of resource creation. Which approach provides near-real-time cost risk detection?

options.text: Configure AWS Cost Explorer with hourly granularity reports for each account. Schedule a Lambda function to query Cost Explorer hourly, compare current spending against the previous day's baseline, and send alerts when any account's hourly cost exceeds 150% of the baseline.

Deploy AWS Budgets with daily cost budgets for each account and service. Configure budget alerts at 50%, 80%, and 100% of the daily budget with SNS notifications to the FinOps team. Budget forecasts project whether monthly spending will exceed the planned budget.

Create EventBridge rules in each account matching CloudTrail events for RunInstances, CreateVolume, and CreateNatGateway. Target a centralized Lambda function that evaluates the resource configuration against a cost policy (instance type, volume type, Region) and alerts on violations.

Configure AWS Cost Anomaly Detection with individual monitors for each account. Set alert thresholds at $10 per day per service and configure SNS notifications to the FinOps team. Cost Anomaly Detection evaluates spending patterns and alerts on unexpected cost increases.

explanation: EventBridge rules matching CloudTrail resource creation events provide near-real-time detection (within minutes) of costly resource creation. Lambda evaluation against cost policies alerts before costs accumulate. Option A's Cost Anomaly Detection has a delay of several hours before detecting spending changes. Option C's Budgets alert on accumulated spending, not individual resource creation events. Option D's hourly Cost Explorer queries have a lag of up to 24 hours for data availability.

stem: A company uses Amazon EKS with Cluster Autoscaler. During a sudden traffic spike, the autoscaler needed to add nodes, but it took 5 minutes for new nodes to become ready and pods to be scheduled. This delay caused request failures. Which approach reduces the time to scale the EKS cluster?

options.text: Implement Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) with custom metrics to scale pod replicas before cluster-level scaling is needed. Configure the HPA to scale based on request queue depth with a target of 10 requests per pod, adding pods before existing node capacity is exhausted.

Configure the EKS managed node group with a warm pool of pre-initialized EC2 instances in stopped state. When the autoscaler triggers scale-up, warm pool instances start in 30-60 seconds instead of the 5-minute cold start for new instance provisioning and initialization.

Replace Cluster Autoscaler with Karpenter for node provisioning. Karpenter provisions right-sized nodes directly from EC2 without waiting for Auto Scaling group scale-up. Configure Karpenter provisioners with multiple instance types and zones for fastest availability.

Increase the Cluster Autoscaler's scan interval from the default 10 seconds to 5 seconds and set the scale-up delay to 0 seconds. Configure the autoscaler to expand by 2 nodes at a time instead of 1 to provide more capacity per scaling event for faster pod scheduling.

explanation: Karpenter provisions nodes faster than Cluster Autoscaler because it directly launches EC2 instances with right-sized specifications without going through Auto Scaling group operations. It also supports diverse instance types for faster capacity availability. Option B's warm pools work but aren't natively supported with EKS managed node groups. Option C reduces scan intervals but doesn't address the fundamental node provisioning time. Option D scales pods within existing capacity but doesn't help when nodes are needed.

stem: A company needs to implement a governance framework that prevents developers from deploying CloudFormation stacks that create publicly accessible resources (public S3 buckets, EC2 instances with public IPs, publicly accessible RDS instances). The governance must apply before stack creation. Which approach provides pre-deployment governance?

options.text: Implement an SCP that denies s3:PutBucketPolicy, ec2:RunInstances with public IP, and rds:CreateDBInstance with PubliclyAccessible. Apply the SCP across all accounts to prevent any principal from creating publicly accessible resources through any deployment method.

Create AWS Config conformance packs with rules checking for public S3 buckets, EC2 public IPs, and public RDS instances. Deploy the conformance packs across all accounts using AWS Organizations and configure auto-remediation to revoke public access on detected resources.

Deploy CloudFormation Hooks that run custom validation logic before resource provisioning. Register hooks that inspect CloudFormation resource configurations for public accessibility settings and reject stack operations containing publicly accessible resource configurations.

Configure AWS CloudFormation Guard rules in a CodeBuild stage that validates templates before deployment. Write Guard rules that check S3 PublicAccessBlockConfiguration, EC2 AssociatePublicIpAddress, and RDS PubliclyAccessible properties and fail the pipeline on violations.

explanation: CloudFormation Hooks run custom validation logic before CloudFormation provisions resources, providing true pre-deployment governance. Hooks evaluate the actual resource configuration in the template and reject non-compliant stacks. Option B detects after deployment which violates the pre-deployment requirement. Option C uses SCPs which can restrict some operations but don't inspect all CloudFormation resource properties at deployment time. Option D validates templates in CI/CD but doesn't protect against direct console or CLI CloudFormation deployments.

stem: A company wants to implement automated rollback for their ECS service deployments. If the new deployment's error rate exceeds 1% within the first 10 minutes, the service should automatically roll back to the previous version. The deployment uses a rolling update strategy with the ECS service. Which feature provides this automatic rollback?

options.text: Configure the ECS service with deployment circuit breaker enabled and rollback enabled. The circuit breaker automatically detects deployment failures when new tasks repeatedly fail to reach steady state and triggers a rollback to the last successful deployment configuration.

Switch from rolling update to blue/green deployment using CodeDeploy with the ECS deployment type. Configure a CloudWatch alarm for the error rate metric and attach it to the CodeDeploy deployment group's automatic rollback configuration for alarm-triggered rollback.

Configure the ECS service deployment configuration with minimumHealthyPercent set to 100% and maximumPercent set to 200%. Add an ALB health check with a 5-second interval that deregisters targets returning errors, causing the deployment to stall if too many targets fail.

Create a CloudWatch alarm on the ALB HTTP 5xx error rate with a 1% threshold and 10-minute evaluation period. Configure the alarm action to invoke a Lambda function that calls the UpdateService API with the previous task definition revision to trigger a manual rollback.

explanation: CodeDeploy blue/green deployment with CloudWatch alarm-based rollback provides automatic rollback when the error rate exceeds the threshold during the deployment window. This directly addresses the 1% error rate requirement. Option A's circuit breaker detects task startup failures, not application error rates after tasks are running. Option B requires custom Lambda logic when CodeDeploy provides this natively. Option D stalls the deployment but doesn't automatically roll back to the previous version.

stem: A company uses AWS CDK and needs to tag all resources created by their CDK stacks with mandatory tags including Application, Environment, and Owner. The tags must be applied consistently without requiring each construct to specify them individually. Which CDK feature applies tags to all resources?

options.text: Define tags in the CDK context (cdk.json) as context values. Reference the context tags in each construct definition using the node.tryGetContext() method and apply them as resource tags, maintaining tag definitions in configuration separate from the application code.

Create a CDK Aspect that visits all constructs implementing ITaggable in the construct tree. The Aspect adds the mandatory tags to each taggable resource during synthesis, providing a centralized tagging mechanism that works across all construct types.

Use the Tags.of(scope).add() method at the stack level to apply tags to all resources within the stack. CDK propagates stack-level tags to all child constructs automatically, ensuring consistent tagging without modifying individual resource definitions in the construct tree.

Create a custom L3 construct wrapper that extends each AWS resource construct and adds mandatory tags in the constructor. Require development teams to use these wrapper constructs instead of the standard L2 constructs, with a CDK Aspect that verifies tag compliance.

explanation: Tags.of(scope).add() at the stack level automatically propagates tags to all child resources in the construct tree. This is the CDK-native approach for consistent resource tagging without individual construct modification. Option B works but is more complex than the built-in Tags API. Option C requires explicit tag application in each construct. Option D requires wrapping every construct which adds significant development overhead.

stem: A company runs a WebSocket-based real-time application on Amazon API Gateway with a Lambda backend. During scaling events, existing WebSocket connections are dropped because the Lambda function reaches its concurrency limit. Users experience disconnections and data loss. Which approach maintains WebSocket connection stability during scaling?

options.text: Replace the Lambda backend with an ECS Fargate service running a WebSocket server behind a Network Load Balancer. Configure the NLB with sticky sessions and the ECS service with a gradual scaling policy that adds tasks before existing ones reach connection capacity limits.

Implement client-side reconnection logic with exponential backoff in the WebSocket client application. Store the connection state and pending messages in DynamoDB and restore the session state when the client reconnects after a transient disconnection during scaling events.

Configure Lambda provisioned concurrency matching the expected peak WebSocket connection count. Provisioned concurrency keeps function instances initialized and ready, preventing throttling of WebSocket message handler invocations during traffic spikes.

Configure API Gateway WebSocket API with throttling settings that match the Lambda function's concurrency limit. Set the route-level throttle rate to prevent message delivery attempts that would exceed Lambda capacity, buffering messages at the API Gateway level.

explanation: ECS Fargate with a WebSocket server maintains persistent connections without the stateless invocation model of Lambda. NLB with sticky sessions ensures connections persist on the same task. Gradual scaling prevents connection drops. Option A's provisioned concurrency helps Lambda cold starts but doesn't solve the fundamental issue of Lambda's stateless invocation model for persistent WebSocket connections. Option C handles reconnection but doesn't prevent the underlying disconnection. Option D throttles at the API level which still drops messages.

stem: A company runs a multi-tenant SaaS application and needs to provide each tenant with a dedicated CloudWatch dashboard showing their specific metrics including API call counts, error rates, and response latencies. The company has 200 tenants. Creating individual dashboards manually is not scalable. Which approach automates per-tenant dashboard creation?

options.text: Create a CloudFormation template for tenant dashboards with parameterized metric dimensions. Use CloudFormation StackSets or a Lambda function to deploy dashboard stacks for each tenant with tenant-specific dimension values, automating the creation of 200 identical dashboard layouts.

Create a single CloudWatch dashboard with metric math SEARCH expressions that dynamically query metrics across all tenants. Add dashboard variables (text widget filters) that allow users to type a tenant ID to filter the displayed metrics to a specific tenant's data.

Create an API Gateway endpoint backed by Lambda that generates CloudWatch dashboard JSON definitions dynamically based on the requested tenant ID. Serve the dashboard through a custom web application that embeds the CloudWatch dashboard using the GetDashboard API response.

Deploy Amazon Managed Grafana with CloudWatch as a data source. Create a Grafana dashboard template with tenant ID as a template variable. Grafana's variable feature allows selecting a tenant from a dropdown, dynamically filtering all dashboard panels to show that tenant's metrics.

explanation: Grafana with template variables provides a single dashboard that dynamically filters to any tenant's metrics via dropdown selection. This scales to 200+ tenants without creating individual dashboards. Option A creates 200 separate dashboards which are expensive and hard to maintain. Option B's text widget filters require manual text entry and don't provide a dropdown experience. Option D builds a custom application when Grafana provides this functionality natively.

stem: A company's application uses Amazon SQS with a visibility timeout of 30 seconds. The consumer Lambda function processes messages in 10-25 seconds. Occasionally, a message takes 35 seconds to process, causing it to become visible again and be processed by another consumer, resulting in duplicate processing. Which solution prevents duplicate processing from visibility timeout expiration?

options.text: Configure the Lambda event source mapping with a maximum batching window of 0 seconds to process messages immediately. Set the Lambda function timeout to 30 seconds matching the visibility timeout and add a dead-letter queue after 1 receive for failed processing attempts.

Implement the ChangeMessageVisibility API call within the Lambda function's processing logic. Extend the visibility timeout by an additional 30 seconds when the function detects that processing is taking longer than 20 seconds, preventing the message from becoming visible.

Increase the SQS queue visibility timeout to 60 seconds, which is at least double the maximum expected processing time. Configure the Lambda event source mapping's function timeout to 50 seconds to ensure the function completes before the visibility timeout expires.

Enable SQS FIFO queue deduplication with a content-based deduplication ID. Move from the standard queue to a FIFO queue which ensures exactly-once delivery within the deduplication window, preventing any message from being delivered to a second consumer while one is processing.

explanation: Setting the visibility timeout to at least 2x the maximum processing time ensures messages remain invisible throughout processing. The Lambda timeout should be less than the visibility timeout so the function completes before re-visibility. Option B adds ChangeMessageVisibility calls which increase code complexity when simply extending the timeout is simpler. Option C matches timeouts which still risks the same issue. Option D switches to FIFO which changes queue semantics and has lower throughput limits.

stem: A company needs to ensure that all outbound internet traffic from their VPC is inspected and filtered. The solution must block access to known malicious domains, prevent data exfiltration through DNS tunneling, and log all outbound connections for security audit. Which architecture provides comprehensive outbound traffic control?

options.text: Deploy AWS Network Firewall in the VPC with stateful rule groups that inspect outbound traffic. Configure domain filtering rules to block known malicious domains, enable DNS inspection to detect tunneling, and log all traffic to CloudWatch Logs and S3 for security auditing.

Deploy a Squid proxy on EC2 instances in the public subnet with URL filtering enabled. Configure all private subnet route tables to direct HTTP/HTTPS traffic through the proxy and log all proxy access to CloudWatch Logs. Use an NLB in front of the proxy for high availability.

Configure a NAT Gateway with VPC Flow Logs enabled for outbound traffic logging. Deploy Route 53 Resolver DNS Firewall with domain lists that block malicious domains and detect DNS tunneling patterns. Use Network ACLs to restrict outbound traffic to approved port ranges.

Configure AWS PrivateLink for all AWS service access to eliminate internet-bound traffic. Deploy VPC endpoints for S3, DynamoDB, and other services, and block all outbound internet access through the route table by removing the NAT Gateway route to enforce private-only connectivity.

explanation: AWS Network Firewall provides stateful packet inspection, domain filtering, DNS inspection for tunneling detection, and comprehensive logging to both CloudWatch and S3. It covers all protocols, not just HTTP/HTTPS. Option B combines multiple services but doesn't provide deep packet inspection. Option C deploys a proxy which only handles HTTP/HTTPS traffic and requires EC2 management. Option D eliminates internet access entirely which doesn't work for applications that need to reach external APIs.

stem: A company needs to manage environment-specific configuration for their application deployed across dev, staging, and production. Configurations include feature flags, connection strings, and timeouts. Changes to configuration must be deployable independently from code changes and should support gradual rollout with automatic rollback. Which service is purpose-built for this?

options.text: Use AWS AppConfig with configuration profiles for each environment. Define deployment strategies with gradual rollout percentages and bake times. Configure validators to check configuration syntax before deployment and enable automatic rollback when CloudWatch alarms indicate issues.

Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with hierarchical parameters organized by environment (/dev/app/timeout, /prod/app/timeout). Update parameters independently from code deployments and configure Lambda functions to detect parameter changes via EventBridge for cache invalidation.

Store configuration in a DynamoDB table with partition key by environment and sort key by configuration name. Build a configuration SDK that caches values locally with a 5-minute TTL and polls DynamoDB for changes, implementing circuit breaker logic for DynamoDB failures.

Store configuration in a Git repository alongside application code with environment-specific files (config.dev.json, config.prod.json). Deploy configuration changes through the same CodePipeline as code changes, using CloudFormation to update SSM parameters from the config files.

explanation: AWS AppConfig provides managed configuration deployment with gradual rollout, validation, bake times, and automatic rollback based on CloudWatch alarms. It's purpose-built for separating configuration from code deployments. Option B stores parameters but lacks built-in gradual rollout and automatic rollback capabilities. Option C builds custom configuration infrastructure on DynamoDB. Option D couples configuration with code deployment pipelines, violating the independent deployment requirement.

stem: A company uses Terraform with modules that reference specific provider versions. A module author updated a provider version that introduced breaking changes, causing downstream Terraform applies to fail for teams using the module. Which Terraform feature prevents unexpected provider version changes from breaking existing configurations?

options.text: Specify provider version constraints in the terraform required_providers block using pessimistic constraint operators (~>). For example, ~> 4.0 allows 4.x updates but prevents major version changes, ensuring compatibility while still receiving minor updates and patches.

Use the .terraform.lock.hcl dependency lock file committed to version control. The lock file records the exact provider versions and hashes used, ensuring all team members and CI/CD pipelines use identical provider versions regardless of available updates in the registry.

Pin all providers to exact versions in the module's required_providers block (version = "= 4.67.0"). This prevents any version changes, though it requires manual updates to receive security patches and new features from the provider maintainers.

Configure a private Terraform provider mirror in S3 that hosts approved provider versions. Set the provider_installation block in the CLI configuration to use the mirror exclusively, preventing teams from downloading unapproved provider versions from the public registry.

explanation: The .terraform.lock.hcl file locks provider versions and integrity hashes, ensuring consistent provider versions across all environments. It prevents unexpected updates while allowing explicit upgrades through terraform init -upgrade. Option B uses version constraints which allow updates within the constraint range, potentially introducing breaking changes in minor releases. Option C pins exact versions but requires manual updates and is inflexible. Option D adds infrastructure for mirroring when the lock file provides version consistency natively.

stem: A company wants to implement progressive delivery for Lambda functions deployed via SAM. The deployment should gradually increase traffic from 10% to 100% over 30 minutes, with CloudWatch alarms monitoring each increment. Which deployment preference achieves this gradual traffic shifting?

options.text: Configure the Lambda DeploymentPreference type to Linear10PercentEvery3Minutes. This shifts 10% of traffic every 3 minutes from the old version to the new version, completing the full migration in 30 minutes with alarm-based rollback at each increment.

Configure the Lambda DeploymentPreference type to AllAtOnce with a pre-traffic hook that runs a 30-minute load test. The hook gradually increases synthetic traffic from 10% to 100% against the new version, rolling back if alarms trigger during the test.

Configure a custom Lambda DeploymentPreference with a CodeDeploy deployment configuration specifying 10 linear increments of 10% at 3-minute intervals. Attach CloudWatch alarms for error rate and duration to the CodeDeploy deployment group for each step.

Configure the Lambda DeploymentPreference type to Canary10Percent30Minutes. This shifts 10% immediately and waits 30 minutes before shifting the remaining 90%, with alarm evaluation during the canary period to detect deployment issues before full migration.

explanation: Linear10PercentEvery3Minutes gradually shifts traffic in 10% increments every 3 minutes, reaching 100% in 30 minutes with alarm monitoring at each step. Option B is canary (two-step) not linear. Option C uses AllAtOnce which shifts all traffic immediately. Option D describes the same behavior as option A but as custom config when the built-in type exists.

stem: A company uses AWS CloudFormation and needs to create an Auto Scaling group that waits for a minimum of 3 instances to signal SUCCESS before the stack creation is marked complete. The instances run a 5-minute bootstrapping script. Which combination of CloudFormation features implements this?

options.text: Configure the Auto Scaling group with MinSize of 3 and a health check grace period of 600 seconds. Use ELB health checks on the target group that return healthy only after the bootstrapping script completes and starts the application health endpoint.

Add a DependsOn attribute on subsequent resources that references the Auto Scaling group. CloudFormation automatically waits for all instances to reach the InService state in the Auto Scaling group before proceeding to create dependent resources.

Add a CreationPolicy with ResourceSignal Count of 3 and Timeout of PT10M to the Auto Scaling group resource. Configure each instance's UserData script to run cfn-signal with --exit-code $? after bootstrapping completes to signal success or failure.

Add a WaitCondition resource with Count of 3 and Timeout of 600 seconds. Create a WaitConditionHandle and pass its URL to each instance via UserData. Configure instances to POST to the handle URL with success status after bootstrapping finishes.

explanation: CreationPolicy with ResourceSignal on ASG is the modern approach. cfn-signal reports bootstrapping completion, and CloudFormation waits for the specified count of signals. Option B uses WaitCondition which works but CreationPolicy is preferred for ASGs. Option C doesn't signal CloudFormation about bootstrapping completion. Option D only waits for the ASG resource itself, not for instance bootstrapping.

stem: A company operates a microservices application where each service has its own DynamoDB table. During peak load, Service A's DynamoDB table is throttled, causing a cascade of failures in Services B, C, and D that depend on Service A. Which architectural pattern prevents this cascading failure?

options.text: Implement the saga pattern with compensating transactions across all services. When Service A fails, Services B, C, and D execute compensating actions to reverse partial transactions and maintain data consistency without requiring Service A availability.

Deploy all services in separate VPCs with VPC peering for communication. Configure Network ACLs to rate-limit traffic between VPCs and implement health check endpoints in each service that other services check before sending requests.

Switch all DynamoDB tables to on-demand capacity mode to eliminate throttling. Configure DynamoDB Auto Scaling with aggressive target utilization of 40% and add DAX clusters for read-heavy services to reduce direct DynamoDB load during peak periods.

Implement the bulkhead pattern by isolating each service's dependencies. Configure Service A with an SQS queue that buffers incoming requests and implement circuit breakers in Services B, C, and D that return cached responses when Service A is degraded.

explanation: The bulkhead pattern isolates failures. SQS buffers requests to Service A, and circuit breakers in dependent services prevent cascading failures by returning cached responses. Option B addresses capacity but doesn't prevent cascading failures from any remaining throttling. Option C handles transaction consistency but not the cascading failure pattern. Option D uses network isolation which doesn't address application-level failure propagation.

stem: A company needs to implement centralized tracing for an application that spans API Gateway, Lambda, SQS, and Step Functions. The team wants to trace a request from the initial API call through all asynchronous processing steps. Some steps process messages hours after the original request. Which tracing configuration maintains trace context across async boundaries?

options.text: Instrument each service with the OpenTelemetry SDK and configure baggage propagation for trace context. Deploy the ADOT collector as a Lambda layer and configure it to export traces to X-Ray, manually extracting and injecting trace context from SQS message attributes.

Enable X-Ray active tracing on all services. X-Ray automatically propagates trace headers through API Gateway, Lambda, and Step Functions. For SQS, enable the AWSTraceHeader message system attribute to propagate trace context through the queue to downstream consumers.

Create a custom tracing solution using DynamoDB to store trace context by request ID. Each service writes its span data to a DynamoDB table and reads the parent trace context from the table, reconstructing the distributed trace from the stored spans in a post-processing Lambda.

Configure CloudWatch ServiceLens to correlate traces, metrics, and logs across all services. Enable X-Ray tracing on API Gateway and Lambda, and configure ServiceLens to link asynchronous processing steps through shared correlation IDs stored in CloudWatch Logs.

explanation: X-Ray propagates trace context natively across API Gateway, Lambda, and Step Functions. The AWSTraceHeader SQS message attribute carries trace context through queues to downstream consumers, maintaining the trace across async boundaries. Option B requires manual context injection/extraction. Option C uses ServiceLens but doesn't solve the async trace propagation. Option D builds custom tracing when X-Ray handles it natively.

stem: A company runs an EKS cluster with multiple microservices. A pod is experiencing intermittent failures, but the failures don't generate any application logs or errors. The pod occasionally restarts with a CrashLoopBackOff status. Which Kubernetes diagnostic approach identifies the root cause?

options.text: Deploy a Prometheus metrics exporter sidecar in the failing pod's deployment. Configure Prometheus to scrape container resource metrics and create Grafana dashboards showing CPU, memory, and network utilization patterns around the times when CrashLoopBackOff events occur.

Enable EKS control plane logging for the api-server and scheduler components. Analyze the control plane logs in CloudWatch Logs to identify scheduling failures, node affinity violations, or resource quota limitations that might cause intermittent pod restarts.

Run kubectl describe pod to examine the pod's events, restart reasons, and last termination state. Check the container's lastState.terminated.exitCode and reason fields which indicate whether the failure was due to OOMKilled, application error, or liveness probe failure.

Configure a PodPreset that adds debug logging environment variables to the failing pod. Redeploy the pod with verbose logging enabled and analyze the CloudWatch Logs output for error messages that were previously suppressed by the default log level setting.

explanation: kubectl describe pod shows the terminated state including exit codes and reasons. Exit code 137 indicates OOMKilled, exit code 1 indicates application error, and specific reasons like 'Liveness probe failed' identify the exact cause. Option B adds logging but won't help if the failure is an OOM kill or probe failure. Option C shows control plane events, not pod-level failure reasons. Option D requires deploying new infrastructure before diagnosis.

stem: A company needs to implement network-level encryption for all traffic between EC2 instances within their VPC, including traffic between instances in the same subnet. The encryption must be transparent to applications and not require code changes. Which solution provides transparent in-VPC encryption?

options.text: Enable VPC encryption in-transit by launching EC2 instances on Nitro-based instance types. AWS Nitro System automatically encrypts traffic between Nitro instances in the same VPC using AES-256-GCM without any application modifications or performance impact.
