Option B provides dedicated throughput but doesn't address failure recovery or checkpointing. Option C describes a DLQ pattern that Kinesis Data Streams doesn't natively support for consumer failures. Option D uses Lambda which works but the question asks about a processing application, and KCL provides the most control over checkpoint semantics.

stem: A company needs to implement comprehensive cost monitoring that alerts when any AWS service's daily spending exceeds the forecasted amount by more than 20%. The alerts must identify which service and account are responsible for the anomaly. Which TWO AWS services together provide automated cost anomaly detection and alerting? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Configure AWS Budgets with daily budget amounts for each AWS service. Set budget alerts at 120% of the budgeted amount to detect when any service exceeds its expected daily spending by more than 20%, sending notifications via SNS to the operations team.

Enable Cost Explorer's daily cost and usage reports and create a Lambda function that runs daily to compare current spending against the previous 30-day average for each service. The function sends SNS alerts when any service exceeds 120% of its historical average cost.

Enable AWS Cost Anomaly Detection and create a cost monitor scoped to AWS services. Cost Anomaly Detection uses machine learning to establish spending baselines per service and automatically detects when actual spending deviates significantly from the predicted forecast.

Configure SNS notifications on the Cost Anomaly Detection monitor with a threshold of 20% above expected spending. When an anomaly is detected, the SNS notification includes the affected service, account, usage type, and the magnitude of the spending anomaly for investigation.

Create CloudWatch billing alarms on the EstimatedCharges metric for each AWS service namespace. Set the alarm threshold at 120% of the average daily cost for the previous 30 days, with SNS notifications to alert the team when any service exceeds the threshold.

explanation: Cost Anomaly Detection (Option A) uses ML to establish service-level spending baselines and detect deviations. SNS notifications (Option C) deliver alerts with service, account, and anomaly details when spending exceeds the configured threshold. Option B requires manually setting budget amounts per service which doesn't adapt to changing usage patterns. Option D uses static CloudWatch billing alarms that don't provide service-level granularity for anomaly detection. Option E builds custom anomaly detection when AWS provides this natively.

stem: A development team needs to enforce code quality standards in their CI/CD pipeline. Pull requests must pass linting, unit tests, and code coverage thresholds before merging. The team uses CodeCommit and CodeBuild. Which configuration automates quality gate enforcement on pull requests?

options.text: Create a CodeCommit approval rule template that requires a successful CodeBuild execution. Configure EventBridge to trigger CodeBuild on pull request created and updated events. The build runs quality checks and the result determines if the approval rule condition is satisfied.

Configure CodePipeline with a source stage monitoring the CodeCommit repository for pull request branches. Add a CodeBuild stage that runs quality checks, and a manual approval stage where the build results are reviewed before the pull request branch is allowed to merge.

Set up a Lambda function triggered by CodeCommit pull request events that clones the repository, runs linting and unit tests locally in the Lambda environment, and posts approval or rejection comments on the pull request based on the quality check results.

Configure a CodeBuild project triggered by CodeCommit pull request events via EventBridge. The buildspec runs linting, unit tests, and code coverage checks. CodeBuild reports the build status back to the pull request as an approval rule that must pass before merging.

explanation: CodeCommit approval rule templates combined with CodeBuild execution create automated quality gates. EventBridge triggers CodeBuild on PR events, and the build result satisfies or fails the approval rule, blocking merge if quality checks fail. Option A describes status reporting but CodeBuild doesn't natively report back as an approval rule condition. Option C runs tests in Lambda which has execution time and environment limitations. Option D uses CodePipeline for PR validation which is designed for deployment pipelines, not PR checks.

stem: A company deploys infrastructure using AWS CDK and needs to test that their CDK constructs generate the expected CloudFormation resources with correct properties. The tests must run locally without deploying any resources to AWS. Which CDK testing approach validates construct output without deployment?

options.text: Use CDK snapshot testing to capture the synthesized CloudFormation template as a JSON snapshot. Compare subsequent test runs against the saved snapshot to detect unintended changes. Update snapshots intentionally when the construct's expected output changes legitimately.

Use CDK assertions library to write unit tests that synthesize the CDK stack and validate the generated CloudFormation template. Tests use Template.fromStack() to create a template object and hasResourceProperties() to verify resource configurations match expectations.

Deploy the CDK stack to a dedicated testing AWS account using cdk deploy. Run integration tests against the deployed resources to verify they match expected configurations. Destroy the stack after testing with cdk destroy to clean up the testing account resources.

Run cdk synth to generate the CloudFormation template and use cfn-lint to validate the template syntax and resource properties against CloudFormation resource specifications. Integrate cfn-lint into the CI/CD pipeline to catch template errors before deployment.

explanation: CDK assertions library provides fine-grained unit testing of synthesized templates without deployment. Template.fromStack() and hasResourceProperties() verify specific resource configurations. This runs locally and validates construct logic. Option B validates template syntax but doesn't verify construct-specific property expectations. Option C deploys resources which the question explicitly wants to avoid. Option D detects changes but doesn't validate that resource properties match specific expected values.

stem: A company runs a global application using Amazon CloudFront with origins in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. If the primary origin in us-east-1 becomes unavailable, CloudFront must automatically route requests to the eu-west-1 origin without manual intervention. Which CloudFront configuration enables automatic origin failover?

options.text: Configure a CloudFront origin group containing the us-east-1 origin as primary and eu-west-1 origin as secondary. CloudFront automatically routes requests to the secondary origin when the primary returns specific HTTP error status codes (500, 502, 503, 504) or times out.

Configure CloudFront with a Lambda@Edge function on the origin request event. The function checks the primary origin's health by making a HEAD request and, if unhealthy, modifies the origin to the eu-west-1 endpoint before CloudFront sends the actual origin request.

Set up an Application Load Balancer with cross-region targets pointing to both us-east-1 and eu-west-1 application servers. Configure CloudFront with the ALB as its single origin, and the ALB handles failover between regions using target group health checks.

Create two CloudFront distributions, one for each origin region. Configure Route 53 with a failover routing policy that health-checks both distributions and routes traffic to the eu-west-1 distribution when the us-east-1 distribution's health check fails.

explanation: CloudFront origin groups provide automatic failover between primary and secondary origins. When the primary returns configured error codes or times out, CloudFront transparently retries the request against the secondary origin. Option B uses Route 53 failover with separate distributions which adds DNS propagation delay. Option C adds Lambda@Edge complexity for built-in functionality. Option D requires a single-region ALB which can't have cross-region targets and doesn't solve the regional failure scenario.

stem: A company's application writes custom business metrics (order count, revenue, cart abandonment rate) that need to be available in CloudWatch for dashboarding and alarming. The metrics must have dimensions for region, product category, and customer tier. Which approach publishes custom business metrics to CloudWatch?

options.text: Write business metrics to application logs in CloudWatch Embedded Metric Format (EMF). EMF-formatted logs are automatically extracted by CloudWatch into custom metrics with the specified dimensions, without requiring explicit PutMetricData API calls from the application code.

Configure CloudWatch Logs metric filters on the application log group to extract business metrics. Create metric filters with filter patterns that match order, revenue, and cart abandonment log entries and publish the extracted values as custom CloudWatch metrics.

Use the CloudWatch PutMetricData API from the application code to publish custom metrics with the three dimensions (region, product category, customer tier). Batch multiple metric data points in each API call using the MetricData array to reduce API overhead.

Deploy a CloudWatch agent on the application hosts configured with a custom metrics collection configuration. Define StatsD or collectd metric definitions for order count, revenue, and cart abandonment in the agent configuration file with the required dimension mappings.

explanation: CloudWatch Embedded Metric Format (EMF) allows applications to write structured metric data to logs which CloudWatch automatically extracts as custom metrics with dimensions. This avoids direct PutMetricData API calls and associated throttling. Option A works but requires managing API calls and batching in application code. Option C uses metric filters which have limited pattern matching and can't handle complex multi-dimensional business metrics. Option D's StatsD/collectd metrics are for system metrics, not structured business metrics with multiple dimensions.

stem: A company needs to implement automated forensic data collection when a GuardDuty finding indicates a potentially compromised EC2 instance. The forensic process must capture a memory dump, create an EBS snapshot, and isolate the instance from the network. Which orchestration approach automates this forensic workflow?

options.text: Configure GuardDuty to send findings to Security Hub. Create a Security Hub custom action that triggers a Lambda function to perform all three forensic steps sequentially: capture memory via SSM, create EBS snapshots, and replace the instance security group with an isolation group.

Create an EventBridge rule matching GuardDuty EC2 instance compromise findings. The rule triggers a Step Functions state machine that orchestrates parallel Lambda functions: one creates EBS snapshots, another modifies security groups for isolation, and a third triggers SSM Run Command for memory capture.

Configure Systems Manager Incident Manager with a response plan for GuardDuty EC2 findings. The response plan includes a runbook that automates memory capture via SSM Run Command, EBS snapshot creation, and security group modification for instance isolation in the defined sequence.

Deploy a Lambda function triggered directly by GuardDuty findings via the GuardDuty notification configuration. The function captures memory using an SSM document, creates EBS volume snapshots, and modifies the instance's security group to a forensic isolation group sequentially.

explanation: EventBridge with Step Functions provides robust orchestration for multi-step forensic workflows. Step Functions handles parallel execution, error handling, and retry logic for the three forensic actions. Option B requires manual Security Hub custom action invocation, not automatic triggering. Option C uses a single Lambda which may timeout for complex forensic workflows and lacks orchestration capabilities. Option D works but Incident Manager runbooks are simpler than Step Functions for complex parallel orchestration.

stem: A company needs to prevent IAM users from creating access keys for themselves, while still allowing a designated security team to manage access keys for all users. Access key creation by non-security users must be blocked organization-wide. Which IAM policy approach enforces this access key restriction?

options.text: Configure AWS IAM Identity Center as the sole authentication method and disable IAM user access key creation at the account level. Identity Center uses temporary credentials that expire automatically, eliminating the need for long-lived access keys for any user including the security team.

Create an SCP that denies iam:CreateAccessKey for all principals except those with the SecurityTeam tag. Apply the SCP to all organizational units. The security team's IAM roles have an aws:PrincipalTag/Team value of SecurityTeam that matches the SCP condition exemption.

Create an IAM permission boundary for all non-security IAM users that excludes the iam:CreateAccessKey action. Attach the permission boundary to all user creation processes via SCP conditions, ensuring new users always receive the boundary that prevents access key self-service.

Attach an inline deny policy to every IAM user that explicitly denies iam:CreateAccessKey when the target user matches the calling user's ARN. The security team members have an additional allow policy that overrides the deny for cross-user access key management.

explanation: SCPs with tag-based conditions provide organization-wide enforcement. The SCP denies iam:CreateAccessKey for all principals except those tagged as SecurityTeam, enforcing the restriction across all accounts without per-user policy management. Option B uses permission boundaries which must be individually attached and don't provide organization-wide enforcement. Option C requires per-user inline policies and explicit deny cannot be overridden by allow policies. Option D eliminates access keys entirely which may break legitimate service account requirements.

stem: A company's CodePipeline deployment to production takes 45 minutes, and the team wants to enable rapid rollback within 2 minutes if issues are detected post-deployment. The application runs on ECS with Fargate. Which deployment configuration enables the fastest rollback?

options.text: Configure CodeDeploy blue/green deployment for ECS with an original revision termination wait time of 60 minutes. During the 60-minute window after deployment, trigger a manual rollback in CodeDeploy which redirects the ALB target group back to the original blue task set immediately.

Configure ECS rolling update deployment with a deployment circuit breaker enabled. When the circuit breaker detects task launch failures during deployment, it automatically triggers a rollback to the previous task definition, restoring the original container version within minutes.

Store the previous ECS task definition revision number in SSM Parameter Store before each deployment. Create a rollback Lambda function that retrieves the previous revision and calls UpdateService to revert. The Lambda deploys the old task definition which takes 5-10 minutes to stabilize.

Configure ECS deployment with a canary deployment controller that routes 10% of traffic to the new version for 5 minutes. If CloudWatch alarms trigger during the canary phase, CodeDeploy automatically stops the deployment and rolls back all traffic to the original task set.

explanation: CodeDeploy blue/green for ECS maintains the original (blue) task set running for the configured wait time. Rollback simply redirects the ALB listener back to the blue target group, which is nearly instantaneous since the original tasks are still running. Option A's circuit breaker only detects task launch failures, not post-deployment application issues. Option C describes a canary phase which helps but rollback is limited to the canary observation window. Option D requires launching new tasks which takes longer than redirecting existing traffic.

stem: A company uses CloudFormation nested stacks to manage a complex application with 15 child stacks. Updating the parent stack sometimes fails midway, leaving some child stacks updated and others in the previous version. The team needs reliable update rollback behavior. Which CloudFormation feature addresses partial nested stack update failures?

options.text: Enable the parent stack's automatic rollback on failure setting (DisableRollback: false). When a child stack update fails, CloudFormation automatically rolls back the entire parent stack including all child stacks to their previous known-good state as a single atomic operation.

Enable stack-level rollback configuration on the parent stack with RollbackConfiguration monitoring CloudWatch alarms. If any alarm triggers during the update, CloudFormation automatically rolls back all child stacks to their previous versions within the specified monitoring time.

Convert the nested stacks architecture to use CloudFormation StackSets instead. StackSets manage deployment across multiple stacks with configurable failure tolerance and automatic rollback, providing more reliable multi-stack update orchestration than nested stacks.

Implement a blue/green deployment strategy by maintaining two copies of the nested stack hierarchy. Update the inactive copy first, verify all 15 child stacks are healthy, then switch traffic using Route 53 weighted routing to the updated stack hierarchy after validation completes.

explanation: CloudFormation's automatic rollback on failure (default behavior when DisableRollback is false) treats the parent stack and all nested child stacks as a single unit. When any child stack fails to update, the entire hierarchy rolls back to the previous state. Option A monitors alarms for rollback triggers but the default rollback behavior already handles update failures. Option B changes the architecture unnecessarily; StackSets serve a different purpose (multi-account/region deployment). Option D creates infrastructure duplication for what rollback handles natively.

stem: A company needs their application to handle sudden traffic spikes of 10x normal load within 60 seconds. The application runs on EC2 instances behind an ALB with Auto Scaling. Current scaling policies take 5 minutes to launch and register new instances. Which approach achieves the 60-second scaling requirement?

options.text: Switch to predictive scaling policies that forecast traffic patterns based on historical data. Predictive scaling launches instances before the anticipated traffic spike, ensuring capacity is available when the spike occurs, meeting the 60-second response requirement.

Replace EC2 instances with Lambda functions behind an API Gateway to handle the traffic spikes. Lambda scales to thousands of concurrent executions within seconds, and API Gateway absorbs the traffic burst while Lambda provisions execution environments on demand.

Configure the Auto Scaling group with a step scaling policy that launches 10x the current capacity when CloudWatch CPU alarm breaches 70%. Set the health check grace period to 30 seconds and the instance warmup time to 60 seconds for faster scaling responsiveness.

Configure an Auto Scaling warm pool with pre-initialized instances in a stopped state. When the scaling policy triggers, warm pool instances transition from stopped to running in approximately 30 seconds since they skip the AMI boot and application initialization phases.

explanation: Auto Scaling warm pools keep pre-initialized instances in a stopped state, dramatically reducing launch time. When scaling triggers, stopped instances start in approximately 30 seconds with the application already installed, meeting the 60-second requirement. Option B forecasts based on patterns which doesn't handle unexpected spikes. Option C requires re-architecting the application for Lambda. Option D launches fresh instances which take 5 minutes regardless of policy aggressiveness.

stem: A company needs to implement Service Level Objective (SLO) monitoring for their API, targeting 99.9% availability measured over a 30-day rolling window. The team needs to track the remaining error budget and alert when the budget is being consumed too quickly. Which CloudWatch configuration implements SLO monitoring with error budget tracking?

options.text: Configure CloudWatch composite alarms combining 5xx error rate and request count metrics using metric math to calculate availability. Set alarm thresholds at the 0.1% error rate (inverse of 99.9% SLO) and configure the evaluation period to cover the 30-day rolling window.

Create CloudWatch Synthetics canaries that call the API endpoints every minute from multiple regions. Calculate availability as the percentage of successful canary runs over 30 days and create CloudWatch metric math expressions to derive error budget remaining from the canary success rate.

Deploy a Lambda function on a 1-minute schedule that queries the API Gateway 5xx error rate metric and calculates the rolling 30-day availability percentage. The function publishes a custom metric for remaining error budget and creates CloudWatch alarms at 50% and 80% budget consumption.

Create a CloudWatch Application Signals SLO with a 99.9% availability target over a 30-day period. Application Signals automatically tracks the error budget consumption rate and creates alarms when the burn rate exceeds configurable thresholds indicating the SLO is at risk.

explanation: CloudWatch Application Signals provides native SLO monitoring with automatic error budget calculation and burn rate alerting. It tracks availability against the defined target over the specified window and alerts when budget consumption accelerates. Option B builds custom SLO tracking when Application Signals provides this natively. Option C measures synthetic availability, not actual API availability. Option D uses composite alarms which can't natively track rolling 30-day error budgets or burn rates.

stem: A company needs to implement feature flags in their application to enable trunk-based development with dark launches. New features must be deployable to production in a disabled state and gradually enabled for specific user segments without redeploying the application. Which AWS service provides feature flag management?

options.text: Store feature flags in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as JSON documents. The application reads parameter values at startup to determine which features are enabled. Update parameter values to toggle features on or off for different user segments without redeployment.

Deploy feature flags using Amazon DynamoDB with a table storing flag names, enabled status, and user segment targeting rules. The application queries DynamoDB on each request to check feature flag status, with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) caching for low-latency flag reads.

Use AWS AppConfig with feature flags. Define feature flag configurations that specify which user segments see each feature. AppConfig deploys flag changes independently from application code deployments, with built-in rollback if the flag change causes increased error rates.

Implement feature flags using AWS Lambda environment variables that control feature enablement. Create a deployment pipeline that updates Lambda environment variables to toggle features. The Lambda function restarts automatically when environment variables change, applying new flag values.

explanation: AWS AppConfig provides native feature flag management with user segment targeting, gradual rollout, and automatic rollback capabilities. Flag changes deploy independently from application code through AppConfig's deployment strategies. Option B uses Parameter Store which lacks feature flag-specific capabilities like targeting rules and rollback. Option C builds custom feature flag infrastructure in DynamoDB. Option D uses environment variables which require function restarts and don't support user segment targeting.

stem: A company needs to automatically scale their DynamoDB table's read capacity in response to a sudden spike in read throttling events. The current Auto Scaling configuration takes 5-10 minutes to respond to throttling. The team needs faster capacity adjustment when throttling is detected. Which approach provides faster DynamoDB capacity scaling during throttle events?

options.text: Create a CloudWatch alarm on the DynamoDB ReadThrottleEvents metric with a 1-minute evaluation period. The alarm triggers a Lambda function that calls UpdateTable to increase provisioned read capacity by 50% immediately, bypassing the Auto Scaling gradual adjustment period.

Enable DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) as a read cache layer in front of the table. DAX serves read requests from its in-memory cache with microsecond latency, absorbing read traffic spikes without increasing the underlying DynamoDB table's provisioned read capacity.

Switch the DynamoDB table to on-demand capacity mode which automatically handles any read traffic volume without capacity planning. On-demand mode scales instantly to accommodate read spikes without throttling and requires no Auto Scaling configuration or manual intervention.

Configure DynamoDB Auto Scaling with a lower target utilization percentage (40% instead of 70%) to maintain more headroom above normal traffic levels. The lower utilization target provisions more capacity proactively, reducing the likelihood of throttling during traffic spikes.

explanation: A CloudWatch alarm on ReadThrottleEvents with Lambda-triggered capacity increase provides near-immediate response to throttling. The Lambda directly increases provisioned capacity, bypassing Auto Scaling's gradual adjustment. Option B switches to on-demand which eliminates throttling but may significantly increase costs for predictable workloads. Option C adds DAX caching which helps reads but doesn't solve the capacity scaling speed requirement. Option D reduces throttling likelihood but doesn't address the response time when throttling does occur.

stem: A company needs to implement centralized certificate management for their microservices running on ECS. All inter-service communication must use mutual TLS (mTLS) with certificates rotated every 90 days. Managing individual certificates per service is operationally complex. Which service simplifies mTLS certificate management for ECS services?

options.text: Use AWS Certificate Manager to issue public TLS certificates for each service endpoint. Configure the ECS task definitions to mount certificates from ACM and enable mTLS in the application's HTTP client and server configurations for inter-service authentication.

Deploy HashiCorp Vault on ECS as a centralized certificate authority. Configure each microservice to request short-lived TLS certificates from Vault at startup, with Vault managing certificate issuance, rotation, and revocation for all inter-service mTLS connections.

Deploy AWS App Mesh with mTLS enabled between virtual services. App Mesh integrates with AWS Certificate Manager Private CA to automatically provision, distribute, and rotate certificates for each service's Envoy proxy sidecar, handling the complete mTLS certificate lifecycle.

Create a private certificate authority using AWS Certificate Manager Private CA. Issue individual certificates for each ECS service and store them in Secrets Manager. Configure Secrets Manager rotation Lambda functions to renew certificates from Private CA every 90 days automatically.

explanation: App Mesh with ACM Private CA integration provides automated mTLS certificate lifecycle management for ECS services. The Envoy sidecar proxies handle TLS termination and certificate rotation transparently, removing certificate management from application code. Option B uses public ACM certificates which can't be used for mTLS client authentication. Option C deploys third-party infrastructure when AWS services provide this natively. Option D requires per-service certificate management and custom rotation logic.

stem: A company uses Terraform with a remote S3 backend for state storage. Multiple developers occasionally run terraform apply simultaneously, causing state file corruption. The team needs to prevent concurrent state modifications while allowing concurrent terraform plan operations. Which Terraform backend configuration prevents state corruption?

options.text: Implement a CI/CD pipeline that serializes all Terraform operations through a single CodeBuild project with a concurrency limit of 1. All developers submit apply requests through the pipeline, and CodeBuild's queue ensures only one apply runs at a time for the workspace.

Configure the S3 bucket with object locking in governance mode to prevent concurrent writes to the state file. S3 object locking ensures only one write operation can modify the state file at a time, blocking concurrent terraform apply operations at the storage level.

Enable S3 bucket versioning and configure the Terraform backend with the skip_metadata_check flag. Versioning allows recovery from concurrent write corruption by restoring previous state versions, and metadata check skipping improves concurrent access performance.

Enable state locking by adding a DynamoDB table for lock management in the S3 backend configuration. Terraform acquires a lock in DynamoDB before any state-modifying operation and releases it after completion, preventing concurrent applies while allowing concurrent plan operations.

explanation: DynamoDB state locking is the standard Terraform mechanism for preventing concurrent state modifications. It acquires an exclusive lock during apply operations while plan operations only need read access. Option B's S3 object locking prevents deletion/overwrite but doesn't provide application-level locking for Terraform operations. Option C serializes all operations including plans which is unnecessarily restrictive. Option D enables versioning for recovery but doesn't prevent corruption from concurrent writes.

stem: A company's application uses SQS as a message buffer between producers and consumers. During peak periods, the consumer fleet cannot keep up with message production, causing messages to approach the 14-day retention limit. The team needs to prevent message loss while managing the processing backlog. Which approach prevents message loss during sustained high-throughput periods?

options.text: Configure an SQS dead-letter queue with a maximum receive count of 5. Messages that fail processing 5 times move to the DLQ where they are retained separately. Create a CloudWatch alarm on ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage to trigger additional consumer scaling before messages expire.

Enable SQS long polling with a wait time of 20 seconds to reduce empty receive calls and improve consumer efficiency. Configure the visibility timeout to match the maximum processing time to prevent duplicate processing that wastes consumer capacity during high-throughput periods.

Implement Auto Scaling for the consumer fleet based on the SQS ApproximateNumberOfMessages metric. Configure target tracking scaling to maintain the backlog-per-instance metric at a level where consumers can process all messages within the retention period, scaling up during peak periods.

Switch from standard SQS to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams which supports configurable retention up to 365 days. The extended retention provides more time for consumers to process the backlog during sustained high-throughput periods without risk of message loss.

explanation: Auto Scaling consumers based on the SQS backlog metric dynamically adjusts processing capacity to match production rate. Target tracking on backlog-per-instance ensures consumers scale to process messages before they expire. Option A sets up DLQ for processing failures but doesn't address the throughput backlog. Option C changes the messaging service which may require application changes. Option D improves efficiency marginally but doesn't address insufficient consumer capacity during sustained peaks.

stem: A company runs a distributed application and needs to identify which downstream service is causing increased latency in their API responses. The application calls 5 downstream services for each request, and the team needs to pinpoint which service is the bottleneck. Which observability tool provides this downstream latency breakdown?

options.text: Enable VPC Flow Logs and analyze network-level latency between the application and each downstream service. Flow logs capture packet timing information that reveals network-level delays to each downstream endpoint, identifying network bottlenecks in the service communication path.

Configure CloudWatch Synthetics canaries that individually call each of the 5 downstream services from the application's VPC. Compare canary latency measurements across all downstream services to identify which service has the highest response time during the observed period.

Deploy AWS X-Ray with the X-Ray SDK integrated into the application and all downstream service clients. X-Ray trace maps visualize the latency contribution of each downstream service call, and the service map highlights services with elevated response times as potential bottlenecks.

Create CloudWatch dashboards with latency metrics for each downstream service using CloudWatch Contributor Insights. Contributor Insights analyzes log patterns to identify the highest-latency downstream calls and ranks them by their impact on overall API response time.

explanation: X-Ray provides distributed tracing that visualizes the latency breakdown across all downstream service calls within each request. The service map and trace timeline show exactly which service contributes the most latency. Option B uses Contributor Insights which analyzes log patterns, not distributed traces. Option C's VPC Flow Logs capture network flows but not application-level service call latency. Option D tests downstream services in isolation which doesn't reflect actual request path latency.

stem: A company wants to implement a multi-stage deployment pipeline for a Lambda-based application that deploys to dev, staging, and production environments sequentially. Each stage must use a different AWS account. Which TWO configurations are needed for this cross-account CodePipeline deployment? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Configure the CodePipeline artifact store S3 bucket with a bucket policy that grants read access to the target account roles. Encrypt artifacts with a KMS key that has key policy grants allowing the cross-account roles to decrypt, enabling artifact sharing across accounts.

Create a single CodePipeline in the production account that deploys to all three environments. Configure the pipeline to use the production account's IAM service role for all deployment actions, with resource-based policies on dev and staging resources granting the production role access.

Deploy separate CodePipeline instances in each target account (dev, staging, prod). Configure the source stage in each pipeline to trigger on successful completion of the previous environment's pipeline using cross-account EventBridge event forwarding between accounts.

Create a cross-account IAM role in each target account (dev, staging, prod) that trusts the pipeline account. The roles grant permissions for CloudFormation and Lambda operations. CodePipeline assumes these roles when executing deployment actions in each target account.

Deploy AWS CodeArtifact repositories in each target account to store deployment packages. Configure the pipeline to publish artifacts to each account's CodeArtifact repository, and each account's deployment action pulls artifacts from its local CodeArtifact repository for deployment.

explanation: Cross-account CodePipeline requires IAM roles in target accounts (Option A) for CodePipeline to assume when deploying, and artifact store access (Option C) with KMS key sharing for encrypted artifact decryption. Option B uses separate pipelines per account which isn't a single multi-stage pipeline. Option D tries to use a single role across accounts which doesn't work for cross-account deployment. Option E uses CodeArtifact for package management, not pipeline artifact sharing.

stem: A company needs to implement chaos engineering practices on their AWS infrastructure to test resilience. The team wants to inject faults like network latency, CPU stress, and service unavailability into their ECS Fargate tasks in a controlled manner. Which AWS service provides managed fault injection for ECS?

options.text: Deploy a custom chaos engineering sidecar container in each ECS task definition. The sidecar container runs a chaos agent that can inject network latency using tc commands, CPU stress using stress-ng, and randomly terminate the main application container based on configured schedules.

Implement Netflix Chaos Monkey adapted for AWS ECS. Deploy Chaos Monkey as an ECS service that randomly terminates other ECS tasks in the cluster during business hours. Configure termination probability and target service filters to control the scope of chaos experiments.

Configure Systems Manager Automation documents that simulate faults by modifying ECS service configurations. Create automation runbooks that reduce desired count, modify task CPU limits, and update security groups to simulate service unavailability, network issues, and resource constraints.

Use AWS Fault Injection Service (FIS) with experiment templates targeting ECS tasks. FIS supports actions like injecting network latency, CPU stress, and task termination on Fargate tasks. Stop conditions using CloudWatch alarms automatically halt experiments if safety thresholds are breached.

explanation: AWS Fault Injection Service provides managed chaos engineering with native ECS Fargate support. FIS experiment templates define fault types, targets, and stop conditions for safe, controlled experiments. Option B requires building custom chaos tooling when FIS provides this natively. Option C modifies service configurations rather than injecting real faults at the task level. Option D implements a third-party approach limited to task termination without network or CPU fault injection.

stem: A company uses AWS Organizations and needs to restrict which AWS regions member accounts can create resources in. Only us-east-1, us-west-2, and eu-west-1 should be allowed for workloads. Global services like IAM and CloudFront must remain accessible. Which policy mechanism enforces regional restrictions?

options.text: Create IAM permission boundaries that restrict the aws:RequestedRegion condition to the three allowed regions. Attach the permission boundary to all IAM roles and users in member accounts, preventing them from making API calls to non-approved regional service endpoints.

Configure VPC endpoints in only the three approved regions. Without VPC endpoints in other regions, applications cannot reach regional AWS service endpoints, effectively preventing resource creation in non-approved regions through network-level access restriction.

Create an SCP that denies all actions with a StringNotEquals condition on aws:RequestedRegion for the three allowed regions. Include a NotAction list for global services (iam:*, sts:*, cloudfront:*, route53:*, organizations:*) that are exempt from the regional restriction.

Configure AWS Control Tower with Region deny guardrails that block resource creation in non-approved regions. Control Tower's built-in guardrails automatically exempt global services and only restrict regional service API calls to the three approved regions.

explanation: An SCP with aws:RequestedRegion condition and NotAction for global services is the standard approach for organizational region restriction. The SCP denies actions in unapproved regions while exempting global services that don't operate in specific regions. Option B uses Control Tower guardrails which work but SCPs provide more flexible configuration. Option C uses permission boundaries which must be individually managed. Option D relies on network restrictions which don't prevent API calls made from outside VPCs.

stem: A company needs to detect configuration changes to their AWS resources in real-time and automatically evaluate compliance against custom rules. When a security group rule allows SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0, the system must automatically remove the offending rule within 1 minute. Which approach provides real-time detection and remediation?

options.text: Create an EventBridge rule that matches the AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress CloudTrail API event. Configure the rule with an input transformer that extracts the security group ID and rule details, triggering a Lambda function that immediately revokes the SSH 0.0.0.0/0 ingress rule.

Deploy an AWS Config custom rule using a Lambda function that evaluates security group configurations. Enable auto-remediation with a custom SSM Automation document that calls RevokeSecurityGroupIngress to remove the offending SSH rule when the Config rule marks it non-compliant.

Configure VPC Network Access Analyzer to detect security group rules allowing unrestricted SSH access. Set up a scheduled analysis every minute and trigger a Lambda function to remediate non-compliant security groups identified in the analysis findings.

Enable AWS Firewall Manager with a security group audit policy that detects security groups allowing SSH from 0.0.0.0/0. Configure the audit policy with auto-remediation enabled to automatically remove non-compliant inbound rules from managed security groups across all accounts.

explanation: EventBridge with CloudTrail API event matching provides near-real-time detection when a security group rule is created. The Lambda function immediately revokes the offending rule, achieving sub-minute remediation. Option A uses Config which evaluates periodically (not real-time) and auto-remediation adds additional latency. Option C's Firewall Manager evaluates compliance on a schedule, not in real-time. Option D's Network Access Analyzer is designed for network path analysis, not real-time security group monitoring.

stem: A company needs to implement a multi-region active-active architecture for their DynamoDB-based application. Both regions must serve read and write requests simultaneously, with writes in one region appearing in the other within 1 second. Which DynamoDB feature supports this multi-region active-active pattern?

options.text: Deploy DynamoDB tables in both regions with DynamoDB Streams enabled. Create Lambda functions triggered by streams that write changes to the other region's table using cross-region API calls. Configure conflict resolution logic in the Lambda function for concurrent writes.

Use DynamoDB with DAX clusters in both regions for read performance. Configure application-level write routing that sends all writes to a primary region, which are then replicated via DynamoDB Streams to the secondary region for eventual consistency across both regions.

Implement Amazon ElastiCache Global Datastore as a caching layer in front of DynamoDB in both regions. Writes go to DynamoDB in the primary region and are cached in both ElastiCache regions, providing sub-second read consistency for cached items across both geographic locations.

Configure DynamoDB Global Tables with replication across both regions. Global Tables provide active-active replication where each replica accepts read and write operations. Changes are replicated asynchronously between regions with sub-second replication latency for most items.

explanation: DynamoDB Global Tables provide managed active-active multi-region replication. Both replicas accept reads and writes with built-in conflict resolution (last writer wins) and sub-second cross-region replication. Option B builds custom replication with Lambda which Global Tables provides natively with better conflict handling. Option C routes all writes to a single region which is active-passive, not active-active. Option D adds ElastiCache caching but doesn't address multi-region write capability for DynamoDB.

stem: A company needs to implement centralized logging for applications running across 30 AWS accounts. All logs must be stored in a central logging account with a 7-year retention period for compliance, and the solution must prevent any account from tampering with their own logs. Which architecture ensures tamper-proof centralized logging?

options.text: Deploy Kinesis Data Firehose in each account to stream logs to a central S3 bucket in the logging account. Enable S3 Object Lock in compliance mode on the bucket with a 7-year retention period. The S3 bucket policy allows PutObject from member accounts but denies all delete and modify operations.

Configure CloudWatch Logs cross-account log delivery from each source account to the central logging account. Enable CloudWatch Logs resource policies in the central account that accept logs from organization member accounts, with log group retention set to 7 years.

Configure AWS CloudTrail organization trail that delivers logs from all member accounts to a central S3 bucket in the logging account. Enable S3 bucket versioning and MFA delete to prevent unauthorized log modification or deletion during the 7-year retention period.

Deploy a centralized Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster in the logging account. Configure FluentBit on all application hosts to send logs directly to the OpenSearch cluster using cross-account IAM roles. Apply OpenSearch index lifecycle policies with a 7-year retention for compliance.

explanation: Kinesis Firehose to S3 with Object Lock in compliance mode provides tamper-proof storage. Compliance mode prevents anyone, including root users, from deleting or modifying objects during the retention period. Option A uses CloudWatch Logs which supports cross-account delivery but doesn't provide tamper-proof storage guarantees. Option C configures CloudTrail which is for API audit logs, not application logs. Option D uses OpenSearch which has storage costs and operational overhead for long-term log retention.

stem: A company needs to implement automated rollback for CloudFormation stack deployments when post-deployment health checks fail. After a stack update completes successfully, the application health check must pass within 10 minutes, or the stack should automatically roll back to the previous version. Which CloudFormation feature enables health-check-based automatic rollback?

options.text: Create a Lambda-backed custom resource that runs health checks against the application endpoint for 10 minutes after stack update. If the health checks fail, the custom resource signals failure to CloudFormation, causing the stack update to fail and trigger automatic rollback.

Configure CloudFormation rollback triggers with a CloudWatch alarm that monitors the application health check endpoint. Set the monitoring time to 10 minutes. If the alarm enters ALARM state during the monitoring period, CloudFormation automatically rolls back the stack to its previous state.

Configure an EventBridge rule that triggers on CloudFormation stack update completion events. The rule invokes a Step Functions workflow that runs health checks for 10 minutes and calls the CloudFormation RollbackStack API if the health checks fail during the monitoring window.

Add a CloudFormation WaitCondition resource with a timeout of 10 minutes that depends on the application's health check signal. If the WaitCondition doesn't receive a success signal from the application within the timeout, the stack update fails and triggers automatic rollback.

explanation: CloudFormation rollback triggers monitor CloudWatch alarms after stack operations complete. If the specified alarm enters ALARM state during the monitoring time, CloudFormation automatically rolls back the stack. This is the native mechanism for post-deployment health-based rollback. Option B uses WaitCondition which blocks the stack update during creation, not after completion. Option C runs during stack creation not after successful completion. Option D builds custom rollback logic when rollback triggers provide this natively.

stem: A company experiences intermittent database connection timeouts from their ECS application to an RDS Aurora cluster. The issue occurs randomly 2-3 times per week and resolves within 5 minutes. The team needs to capture diagnostic data at the moment the timeout occurs. Which approach captures real-time diagnostic data during intermittent failures?

options.text: Deploy a custom health check Lambda function that runs every 30 seconds, attempting to connect to the Aurora cluster and measuring connection time. Log connection attempts to CloudWatch Logs and create metric filters that track connection failures and latency over time for trend analysis.

Configure CloudWatch Contributor Insights rules on VPC Flow Logs to identify network-level connection patterns. Analyze the top contributors (source IPs, ports, bytes transferred) during the timeout window to determine if network congestion or packet loss causes the connection failures.

Enable RDS Enhanced Monitoring with 1-second granularity on the Aurora cluster. Review the Enhanced Monitoring dashboard after each incident to analyze OS-level metrics (CPU, memory, network, processes) during the timeout window to identify the root cause pattern.

Create a CloudWatch alarm on the RDS DatabaseConnections metric with anomaly detection. When the alarm triggers, it invokes a Lambda function that captures RDS Performance Insights data, ECS task metrics, VPC Flow Logs summary, and DNS resolution logs for the Aurora endpoint.

explanation: A CloudWatch alarm with automated diagnostic collection captures comprehensive data at the moment of failure. The Lambda function gathers RDS Performance Insights, ECS metrics, and network data simultaneously, providing a complete diagnostic snapshot. Option B provides OS-level monitoring data but requires manual review after the fact. Option C analyzes network patterns but doesn't capture application and database-level diagnostics. Option D monitors connectivity but doesn't capture comprehensive diagnostic data when failures occur.

stem: A company needs to implement a defense-in-depth strategy for their public-facing web application running on ECS behind an ALB. The application must be protected against SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and DDoS attacks. Which TWO services should be deployed together for comprehensive web application protection? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Deploy AWS WAF with managed rule groups including the SQL injection rule set and cross-site scripting rule set on the ALB. Configure rate-based rules to limit requests per IP address, providing application-layer protection against common web exploits and basic DDoS mitigation.

Configure Amazon GuardDuty with ECS Runtime Monitoring to detect suspicious runtime behavior in containers. GuardDuty identifies compromised containers, malware execution, and unauthorized network connections, alerting the security team to application-layer attacks from within the container environment.

Deploy Amazon Inspector on the ECS tasks to continuously scan container images for known vulnerabilities. Inspector identifies software vulnerabilities and network exposure in container configurations, providing findings that help remediate potential attack vectors before they are exploited.

Enable AWS Firewall Manager to centrally manage WAF rules and Shield Advanced protections across all accounts. Firewall Manager deploys consistent security policies to all ALBs and CloudFront distributions, ensuring uniform web application protection standards across the organization.

Enable AWS Shield Advanced on the ALB resource. Shield Advanced provides enhanced DDoS protection with real-time attack visibility, automatic application-layer DDoS mitigation, cost protection for DDoS-related scaling, and 24/7 access to the AWS DDoS Response Team for support.

explanation: AWS WAF (Option A) protects against SQL injection, XSS, and provides rate-based rules for basic DDoS mitigation at the application layer. Shield Advanced (Option B) provides comprehensive DDoS protection with automatic mitigation, cost protection, and DRT access. Option C detects runtime anomalies but doesn't prevent web exploits or DDoS. Option D scans for vulnerabilities but doesn't provide runtime protection. Option E manages policies centrally but is a management tool, not a protection mechanism itself.

stem: A company uses CodeBuild to compile a large C++ application. Build times exceed 30 minutes because the compilation doesn't parallelize across source files. The team wants to reduce build times by distributing compilation across multiple build workers. Which CodeBuild feature enables distributed builds?

options.text: Switch to a CodeBuild compute type with more vCPUs (e.g., BUILD_GENERAL1_2XLARGE with 72 vCPUs). Configure the build command to use make -j72 for parallel compilation on a single high-CPU build instance, utilizing all available processor cores for simultaneous file compilation.

Deploy a distributed build system using ccache and distcc on EC2 instances. Configure the CodeBuild project to connect to the distcc cluster for distributed compilation, spreading the C++ compilation workload across multiple worker instances in the build cluster.

Configure CodeBuild batch builds with build graph mode to split the compilation into multiple parallel build tasks. Each task compiles a subset of source files independently, and a final task links all compiled objects together into the final application binary.

Enable CodeBuild local caching with source cache mode to cache the compilation output between builds. Subsequent builds only recompile changed source files while reusing cached object files for unchanged files, reducing the effective compilation time significantly.

explanation: CodeBuild batch builds with build graph mode distribute work across multiple parallel build tasks. This effectively distributes compilation across workers, with a final linking step. Option B increases parallelism on a single instance which helps but doesn't distribute across multiple workers. Option C caches outputs but doesn't parallelize the initial full build. Option D deploys third-party distributed build infrastructure when CodeBuild provides native distributed build capabilities.

stem: A company needs to enforce infrastructure compliance policies before CloudFormation templates are deployed. Policies must check that S3 buckets have encryption enabled, RDS instances use encrypted storage, and all resources are tagged with mandatory tags. Which approach validates templates against policies before deployment?

options.text: Configure AWS Config with managed rules for S3 encryption, RDS encryption, and required tags. Enable auto-remediation on each rule to automatically fix non-compliant resources after they are created by CloudFormation, ensuring all deployed resources meet compliance requirements.

Create OPA (Open Policy Agent) policies using Rego language to evaluate CloudFormation templates for encryption and tagging requirements. Integrate OPA evaluation into the CI/CD pipeline using conftest to validate templates against the policy bundle before CloudFormation deployment.

Write CloudFormation Guard rules that validate template properties: S3 bucket encryption configuration, RDS storage encryption, and mandatory tag presence on all resources. Run cfn-guard validate in the CI/CD pipeline to block deployments with non-compliant templates.

Deploy CloudFormation Hooks that evaluate each resource in a template before provisioning. Register hooks for S3, RDS, and all taggable resource types with validation logic that checks encryption settings and mandatory tags, failing stack creation if any resource is non-compliant.

explanation: CloudFormation Guard is AWS's native policy-as-code tool for validating CloudFormation templates. Guard rules evaluate template properties against defined policies, and cfn-guard validate in the pipeline blocks non-compliant deployments before resources are created. Option B uses Hooks which evaluate at deployment time adding latency; Guard validates in the pipeline for faster feedback. Option C remediates after deployment rather than preventing non-compliant creation. Option D uses third-party OPA when Guard provides native CloudFormation validation.

stem: A company runs a critical API on ECS Fargate that must maintain 99.99% availability. The current architecture uses a single ALB in one region. The team needs to add multi-region redundancy with automatic failover in under 30 seconds. Which architecture provides sub-30-second regional failover?

options.text: Deploy the API in two regions and use AWS Global Accelerator with endpoint groups in both regions. Global Accelerator continuously monitors endpoint health and reroutes traffic to the healthy region within seconds of detecting an endpoint failure, using anycast IP routing.

Deploy the API in two regions with an ALB in each region. Use Route 53 failover routing with health checks on both ALBs. Route 53 detects the primary region failure via health check and routes traffic to the secondary region within 30 seconds of failure detection.

Deploy the API in two regions and use an NLB with cross-region load balancing enabled. The NLB distributes traffic across ECS tasks in both regions simultaneously, and when one region's tasks fail health checks, the NLB stops sending traffic to that region automatically.

Deploy the API in two regions with CloudFront as the global entry point. Configure CloudFront origin groups with the primary origin in one region and failover origin in the other. CloudFront retries failed requests on the secondary origin for automatic regional failover.

explanation: Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses with continuous health monitoring and instant traffic rerouting. Failover occurs within seconds at the network layer without DNS propagation delays. Option A uses Route 53 which has DNS TTL propagation delays that may exceed 30 seconds. Option C's CloudFront origin groups handle individual request failures but don't provide active health-based regional failover. Option D's NLB doesn't support cross-region load balancing natively.

stem: A company's application generates 10 TB of logs daily across 500 microservices. The team needs to query logs across all services for troubleshooting but CloudWatch Logs Insights queries are timing out due to data volume. Which approach enables efficient querying of high-volume log data?

options.text: Deploy a self-managed Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster sized for 10 TB daily ingestion. Configure CloudWatch Logs subscription filters to stream logs to OpenSearch via Lambda. Use OpenSearch dashboards and query DSL for full-text search across all microservice logs simultaneously.

Archive logs older than 24 hours to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval and only keep recent logs in CloudWatch Logs. This reduces the CloudWatch Logs data volume enabling faster Insights queries for recent data, while archived logs remain accessible within milliseconds for historical analysis.

Enable CloudWatch Logs Insights query result caching and increase the query timeout to the maximum allowed value. Narrow queries by specifying precise time ranges and specific log groups rather than querying all 500 log groups simultaneously to reduce data scanned per query.

Configure CloudWatch Logs subscription filters to stream logs to Amazon S3 via Kinesis Data Firehose. Use Amazon Athena with partitioned tables to query the S3 log data using standard SQL. Partition by date, service, and log level for efficient query performance on the 10 TB daily volume.

explanation: Streaming logs to S3 via Firehose and querying with Athena handles high-volume log data efficiently. Athena's partitioned tables and columnar scanning process only relevant data, enabling fast queries across 10 TB daily logs. Option B works for smaller datasets but doesn't solve the fundamental volume problem at 10 TB per day. Option C adds significant OpenSearch infrastructure cost and operational overhead. Option D moves logs to Glacier which is for archival, not active querying.

stem: A company's ECS application experiences a memory leak that gradually increases container memory usage until the container is OOM-killed and replaced. The team needs to detect the memory leak pattern before the container crashes and proactively restart the affected task. Which monitoring approach detects the gradual memory leak?

options.text: Deploy a sidecar container in each ECS task that monitors the main container's memory usage via the /proc filesystem. The sidecar reports memory metrics to CloudWatch and initiates a graceful container restart when memory usage exceeds 85% of the allocated memory limit.

Create a CloudWatch anomaly detection alarm on the ECS MemoryUtilization metric for each service. Anomaly detection identifies the unusual upward trend in memory consumption that deviates from the normal usage pattern, alerting before the memory reaches the OOM threshold.

Enable Container Insights for the ECS cluster and monitor the pod_memory_utilization_over_pod_limit metric. Set a CloudWatch alarm at 80% memory utilization that triggers an SNS notification to the operations team for manual investigation and task restart if confirmed.

Configure a CloudWatch metric math expression that calculates the rate of change of ECS MemoryUtilization over a 30-minute window. Create an alarm when the rate of memory increase exceeds a threshold, indicating a leak pattern, and trigger an ECS task stop via Lambda function.

explanation: Metric math calculating the rate of memory increase over time detects the gradual leak pattern regardless of the absolute memory level. Alarming on the rate of change triggers proactive task restart before OOM occurs. Option A's anomaly detection may not flag a gradual consistent increase if it becomes the new baseline. Option C sets a static threshold which only triggers near the limit, not when the leak pattern starts. Option D uses a sidecar which adds complexity and a static threshold approach.

stem: A company needs to automate the creation of AMIs that include the latest security patches, application runtime, and monitoring agents. The AMIs must be validated through automated tests before being promoted for use by Auto Scaling groups. Which service provides an automated AMI build and test pipeline?

options.text: Configure AWS Systems Manager Automation to run a multi-step document that patches an existing EC2 instance, installs required software, stops the instance, and creates an AMI. Schedule the automation monthly and use the resulting AMI ID as the Auto Scaling launch template image.

Deploy HashiCorp Packer as a CodeBuild project that builds AMIs using Packer templates with provisioners for patching, runtime installation, and agent deployment. Add a post-processor that launches the AMI and runs Goss tests for validation before marking the AMI as production-ready.

Create a CodePipeline that launches an EC2 instance from a base AMI, runs Ansible playbooks via SSM Run Command for configuration, creates an AMI using the CreateImage API, then runs InSpec tests against a test instance launched from the new AMI to validate functionality.

Use EC2 Image Builder with a pipeline that includes build components for OS patching, runtime installation, and agent deployment. Add test components that validate the AMI by launching a test instance and running verification scripts. Schedule the pipeline to run weekly for updated AMIs.

explanation: EC2 Image Builder provides a managed pipeline for building, testing, and distributing AMIs. Build components handle software installation, test components validate the image, and distribution settings control AMI sharing. Option B builds custom pipeline logic when Image Builder provides this natively. Option C uses third-party Packer when Image Builder is the native AWS solution. Option D uses SSM Automation which creates AMIs but lacks built-in test component orchestration.

stem: A company deploys CloudFormation stacks that create Lambda functions with inline code. The inline code frequently exceeds CloudFormation's 4096-character template body limit, causing deployment failures. The team needs to deploy Lambda functions with larger code packages through CloudFormation. Which approach handles Lambda code deployment beyond the inline limit?

options.text: Split the Lambda function into multiple smaller functions, each within the 4096-character inline limit. Use Step Functions to orchestrate the smaller functions in sequence, with each function performing part of the original function's logic and passing state between executions.

Create a Lambda Layer containing the majority of the function code and reference the layer in the CloudFormation template. Keep only the handler entry point code inline within the 4096-character limit, while the layer contains all the supporting modules and dependencies.

Package the Lambda function code as a ZIP file and upload it to an S3 bucket. Reference the S3 bucket and key in the CloudFormation template's AWS::Lambda::Function resource using the Code property with S3Bucket and S3Key sub-properties instead of ZipFile inline code.

Convert the CloudFormation template to use AWS SAM which has a higher inline code limit of 65536 characters. SAM's AWS::Serverless::Function resource type supports larger inline code blocks and automatically packages the function during sam build before deployment.

explanation: Referencing Lambda code from an S3 bucket removes the inline code size limitation. The ZIP file in S3 can be up to 50 MB compressed (250 MB uncompressed). CloudFormation's Code property with S3Bucket/S3Key is the standard pattern for deploying larger Lambda functions. Option B unnecessarily splits function logic. Option C incorrectly states SAM has a higher inline limit; SAM uses the same CloudFormation limits. Option D adds layer complexity when S3 packaging solves the issue directly.

stem: A company's application uses Amazon ElastiCache Redis as a session store. When the primary Redis node fails, the application experiences 30 seconds of errors before the failover completes. The team needs to reduce the failover impact to under 5 seconds. Which ElastiCache configuration minimizes failover impact?

options.text: Configure the ElastiCache Redis cluster in cluster mode enabled with multiple shards and replicas. Use the cluster's configuration endpoint which automatically redirects clients to the new primary after failover, reducing the application's awareness of node failures to under 5 seconds.

Enable ElastiCache Global Datastore with a secondary cluster in another region. Global Datastore provides cross-region replication with sub-second failover capabilities. During a primary node failure, the application redirects to the secondary cluster for continued session access.

Switch from ElastiCache Redis to ElastiCache Memcached with multiple nodes in an Auto Discovery cluster. Memcached distributes sessions across multiple nodes, so a single node failure only affects a fraction of sessions while the remaining nodes continue serving requests.

Implement application-level retry logic with exponential backoff for Redis connection failures. Configure the Redis client library with a 1-second connection timeout and 3 retry attempts. The application automatically reconnects to the new primary node after the failover completes.

explanation: Cluster mode enabled with the configuration endpoint handles failover transparently. The configuration endpoint maintains the cluster topology map, so clients automatically discover the new primary within seconds. Option A uses Global Datastore for cross-region DR, not for faster local failover. Option C adds retry logic but doesn't speed up the actual failover process. Option D switches to Memcached which doesn't have replication and loses all data on a node failure.

stem: A company needs to monitor the health and performance of 200 on-premises servers alongside their AWS resources in a single CloudWatch dashboard. The on-premises servers run various Linux distributions and need to report CPU, memory, disk, and custom application metrics. Which approach collects on-premises server metrics in CloudWatch?

options.text: Configure each on-premises server to send metrics via StatsD protocol to a centralized CloudWatch agent running on a single relay server. The relay agent aggregates StatsD metrics from all 200 servers and publishes them as custom CloudWatch metrics using a single IAM credential.

Install the CloudWatch agent on each on-premises server. Configure the agent with an IAM user access key (stored in the agent configuration) to authenticate API calls. The agent collects system metrics (CPU, memory, disk) and custom application metrics, publishing them to CloudWatch.

Deploy a Prometheus server on-premises to scrape metrics from all 200 servers. Configure the CloudWatch agent on the Prometheus server with Prometheus metrics collection to forward the scraped metrics to CloudWatch using the Prometheus remote write endpoint integration.

Deploy AWS Systems Manager Agent on each on-premises server and register them as managed instances. Use SSM Run Command to execute a script every minute that collects system metrics and publishes them to CloudWatch using the aws cloudwatch put-metric-data CLI command.

explanation: The CloudWatch agent runs natively on Linux servers and collects system and custom metrics. For on-premises servers, IAM user credentials authenticate the agent's API calls to publish metrics to CloudWatch. This provides direct per-server metric collection and reporting. Option B adds Prometheus infrastructure complexity when the CloudWatch agent handles this directly. Option C centralizes through a relay which creates a single point of failure for 200 servers. Option D uses SSM with scripted metric collection which is fragile compared to the purpose-built CloudWatch agent.

stem: A company uses CodePipeline to deploy containerized applications to Amazon EKS. The pipeline must build the container image, scan it for vulnerabilities, push it to ECR, and update the Kubernetes deployment. Which TWO pipeline stages are required for secure container deployment to EKS? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Add a manual approval stage between the build and deploy stages. The approval notification includes the ECR image scan results so a security reviewer can verify no critical vulnerabilities exist before approving the deployment to the production EKS cluster.

Add a Lambda invoke stage that calls the EKS API directly to update the deployment's container image. The Lambda function uses the Kubernetes Python client with IAM authentication to patch the deployment resource with the new ECR image URI and tag.

Add a CodeDeploy stage configured with an EKS deployment group. CodeDeploy manages the Kubernetes deployment using a blue/green strategy, creating a new ReplicaSet with the updated container image and gradually shifting traffic from the old to the new pods.

Add a CodeBuild stage that authenticates to the EKS cluster using aws eks update-kubeconfig, then runs kubectl set image to update the Kubernetes deployment with the new container image tag from ECR. The build verifies the rollout completes using kubectl rollout status.

Add a CodeBuild stage that builds the container image, runs Amazon ECR image scanning (enhanced scanning with Inspector) on the built image, and fails the build if any critical or high-severity vulnerabilities are found in the container image scan results.

explanation: A CodeBuild stage for building and scanning images (Option A) ensures only secure images are deployed. A CodeBuild stage for kubectl-based EKS deployment (Option B) updates the Kubernetes deployment with the scanned image. Option C's CodeDeploy doesn't natively integrate with EKS Kubernetes deployments. Option D adds manual approval which slows automation and is not required for the described workflow. Option E uses Lambda for kubectl operations which is less maintainable than CodeBuild.

stem: A company discovered that an EC2 instance in their production VPC is making unexpected outbound connections to unknown IP addresses. The security team suspects the instance may be compromised. They need to isolate the instance for investigation while preserving all forensic evidence. Which isolation procedure preserves evidence while stopping malicious activity?

options.text: Stop the EC2 instance immediately to halt all network activity and preserve the current disk state. Create an AMI from the stopped instance to capture the complete machine state. Launch a new instance from the AMI in an isolated VPC for forensic analysis without network access.

Replace the instance's security group with a forensic isolation security group that allows no inbound or outbound traffic. Detach the instance from any Auto Scaling group to prevent termination. Create EBS snapshots of all attached volumes for forensic analysis of the disk contents.

Terminate the EC2 instance to immediately stop all malicious outbound connections. Before termination, create EBS snapshots of all volumes. Launch a new forensic instance from the snapshots in an isolated VPC to analyze the disk contents without the compromised operating system running.

Modify the VPC's network ACL to deny all outbound traffic from the compromised instance's subnet. This blocks the malicious connections at the network level while keeping the instance running for live memory analysis. Create EBS snapshots after the NACL change for disk forensics.

explanation: Replacing the security group with a no-traffic forensic group immediately stops all network communication while keeping the instance running for potential memory forensics. Detaching from ASG prevents automatic termination. EBS snapshots preserve disk evidence. Option B stops the instance which loses volatile memory evidence. Option C terminates the instance destroying all volatile state. Option D modifies the subnet NACL which affects all instances in the subnet, not just the compromised one.

stem: A company needs to ensure that all API calls made in their AWS accounts are logged and that the log files cannot be tampered with after creation. The logs must be stored for 5 years and must be verifiable for integrity at any point during the retention period. Which CloudTrail configuration provides tamper-proof logging?

options.text: Create a CloudTrail organization trail that delivers logs to CloudWatch Logs in a logging account. Configure CloudWatch Logs retention to 5 years. CloudWatch Logs provides built-in immutability since log events cannot be modified or deleted after ingestion into the log group.

Create a CloudTrail organization trail that delivers logs to an S3 bucket in a dedicated logging account. Enable CloudTrail log file integrity validation and S3 Object Lock in compliance mode with a 5-year retention period to prevent any modification or deletion of log files.

Create a CloudTrail organization trail with log file encryption using a customer-managed KMS key. Enable S3 bucket versioning and MFA delete on the log bucket. The KMS encryption and versioning together prevent unauthorized modification while preserving all log file versions.

Create a CloudTrail trail in each account that delivers logs to a centralized S3 bucket. Enable S3 server-side encryption with SSE-S3 and configure a bucket lifecycle policy to transition logs to S3 Glacier after 90 days. Glacier's immutable archive provides tamper-proof storage.

explanation: CloudTrail log file integrity validation creates digest files that enable verification of log file integrity. S3 Object Lock in compliance mode prevents deletion or modification by anyone, including root users, during the retention period. Together they provide verifiable, tamper-proof logging. Option B uses versioning and MFA delete which can be disabled by a root user. Option C's Glacier doesn't provide built-in integrity validation. Option D stores in CloudWatch Logs which has retention limits and doesn't provide cryptographic integrity validation like CloudTrail digest files.

stem: A company uses Terraform to manage an Aurora PostgreSQL cluster. They need to perform a major version upgrade from PostgreSQL 13 to PostgreSQL 15. Terraform's plan shows the cluster will be destroyed and recreated, which would cause data loss. How should the team perform the upgrade safely with Terraform?

options.text: Create a manual snapshot of the Aurora cluster before running terraform apply. Let Terraform destroy and recreate the cluster with PostgreSQL 15. After the new cluster is created, restore the data from the manual snapshot using a separate restore operation outside of Terraform management.

Use terraform state rm to remove the Aurora cluster from Terraform state. Perform the upgrade through the AWS console. Then use terraform import to reimport the upgraded cluster back into Terraform state and update the configuration to match the upgraded cluster's attributes.

Perform the major version upgrade manually through the RDS console or CLI first. Then update the engine_version in Terraform configuration to match the new version and run terraform plan to verify Terraform detects no differences. Run terraform apply to align the state with the actual configuration.

Add lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true } to the Aurora cluster resource to block Terraform from destroying it. Update the engine_version to 15 and run terraform apply. Terraform will attempt an in-place update instead of replacement when destruction is prevented by the lifecycle rule.

explanation: Removing from state, upgrading outside Terraform, and reimporting is the safest approach for destructive Terraform changes. This avoids any risk of Terraform destroying the cluster while allowing the major version upgrade to proceed through the proper RDS upgrade mechanism. Option A assumes Terraform won't detect differences, but other attributes may change during upgrade. Option B's prevent_destroy blocks the apply entirely rather than converting it to an in-place update. Option C involves actual data loss during the destroy-recreate cycle.

stem: A company runs a batch processing system that processes files uploaded to S3. Each file takes 10-60 minutes to process. If a processing instance fails mid-job, the file must not be lost or processed twice. Which architecture ensures exactly-once processing with fault tolerance?

options.text: Deploy an S3 Batch Operations job that periodically scans for unprocessed files based on object tags. The batch job processes each file and applies a 'processed' tag upon completion. Files without the 'processed' tag are reprocessed in the next batch job execution cycle.

Create an S3 event notification that triggers a Step Functions workflow for each uploaded file. The workflow manages the processing state machine with retry logic and error handling. Step Functions' exactly-once execution guarantee prevents duplicate file processing across failures.
