stem: A company needs to implement cross-account access for their central security team to investigate incidents in workload accounts. The security team must be able to assume a role in any workload account to review CloudTrail logs, inspect VPC configurations, and analyze GuardDuty findings. Which approach implements secure cross-account investigation access?

options.text: Configure AWS IAM Identity Center with a permission set that grants read-only access to CloudTrail, VPC, and GuardDuty. Assign the security team group to this permission set across all workload accounts. Security team members access workload accounts through the Identity Center portal.

Create a centralized security dashboard in the security account using CloudWatch cross-account observability. Workload accounts share CloudTrail logs and GuardDuty findings to the security account's CloudWatch. The security team investigates incidents using CloudWatch Logs Insights in the central account.

Create an IAM role in each workload account with a trust policy allowing the security account's IAM roles to assume it. Attach a read-only policy granting access to CloudTrail, VPC, and GuardDuty resources. Deploy the role using CloudFormation StackSets across all organizational units.

Share CloudTrail logs, VPC configurations, and GuardDuty findings from workload accounts to the security account using AWS Resource Access Manager. The security team reviews all findings and configurations in the central security account without needing to access workload accounts directly.

explanation: IAM Identity Center provides centralized access management with permission sets that can be assigned across multiple accounts. The security team uses a single portal to access any workload account with consistent read-only permissions. Option A creates per-account IAM roles which works but is harder to manage than Identity Center. Option C can't share all required resources through RAM (VPC configurations aren't RAM-shareable). Option D provides log access but not interactive VPC configuration inspection or GuardDuty investigation capabilities.

stem: A company needs to implement a canary deployment for their CloudFormation stack updates. Before updating the production stack, the same template changes should be deployed to a canary stack with a small percentage of traffic. If the canary is healthy for 30 minutes, the production stack is updated. Which approach implements canary stack testing for CloudFormation?

options.text: Create two CloudFormation stacks: a canary stack receiving 10% of traffic via Route 53 weighted routing, and the production stack receiving 90%. Update the canary stack first with the new template. After 30 minutes of monitoring with CloudWatch alarms, update the production stack with the same template.

Enable CloudFormation rollback triggers with a 30-minute monitoring period. Deploy the template update to the production stack directly. If CloudWatch alarms trigger within 30 minutes, CloudFormation automatically rolls back the production stack to its previous state, effectively using production as the canary.

Configure CodePipeline with a canary deployment stage that creates a CloudFormation change set for a test stack. Execute the change set and run integration tests. If tests pass within 30 minutes, the pipeline proceeds to create and execute a change set for the production stack.

Use CloudFormation StackSets to deploy the template to a canary account first. Monitor the canary deployment for 30 minutes using CloudWatch cross-account metrics. If healthy, deploy the same template to the production account using the StackSet's sequential deployment ordering.

explanation: Separate canary and production stacks with weighted routing provides true canary testing. The canary receives a small percentage of real production traffic for validation. After 30 minutes of healthy operation, the same template is applied to the production stack. Option B uses separate accounts which doesn't test with production traffic. Option C uses a test stack without production traffic routing. Option D uses production as the canary which risks affecting all users.

stem: A company runs a stateless web application on EC2 instances with Auto Scaling. During peak traffic, new instances take 8 minutes to fully initialize (install dependencies, warm caches). This initialization time causes degraded performance during scale-out events. Which approach reduces the effective initialization time during scaling?

options.text: Switch to an AWS Graviton-based instance type that provides faster boot times compared to x86 instances. Graviton instances initialize faster due to the ARM architecture's efficient startup sequence, reducing the overall instance initialization time from 8 minutes to under 2 minutes.

Enable Auto Scaling instance warm-up period set to 8 minutes. During warm-up, Auto Scaling excludes the new instance from the target tracking metric calculation. This prevents Auto Scaling from launching more instances while the initializing instances are still below target utilization.

Create a golden AMI with all dependencies pre-installed and caches pre-warmed using EC2 Image Builder. Update the Auto Scaling launch template to use the golden AMI. New instances launch with all software ready, reducing initialization from 8 minutes to approximately 1 minute for boot.

Configure predictive scaling policies that use machine learning to forecast traffic patterns and launch instances before peak traffic arrives. Predictive scaling analyzes 14 days of historical metrics to anticipate scaling needs, ensuring capacity is pre-provisioned before demand spikes occur.

Configure an Auto Scaling lifecycle hook on EC2_INSTANCE_LAUNCHING that pauses the instance registration with the load balancer. During the hook, a user data script installs dependencies and warms caches. The script signals completion to proceed with load balancer registration.

explanation: A golden AMI with pre-installed dependencies and pre-warmed caches eliminates the majority of initialization time. Instances boot from the AMI ready to serve traffic in approximately 1 minute. Option B pre-provisions capacity but doesn't reduce initialization time for unexpected spikes. Option C manages metric calculation during warm-up but doesn't reduce the actual initialization time. Option D delays registration but doesn't speed up initialization. Option E's Graviton doesn't significantly reduce application-level initialization time.

stem: A company needs to implement distributed tracing for their application that uses both synchronous (HTTP) and asynchronous (SQS) communication between services. The team needs end-to-end trace visibility even when messages pass through SQS queues, connecting the producing and consuming service traces. Which X-Ray configuration enables tracing through SQS?

options.text: Enable X-Ray active tracing on the SQS queue resource. X-Ray automatically propagates the trace context through the queue, linking the producer's trace segment to the consumer's trace segment without requiring application code changes for trace header propagation.

Configure the X-Ray daemon on both producer and consumer hosts. The daemon automatically detects SQS API calls and propagates trace IDs through the queue metadata. The consumer daemon reads the trace ID from the SQS message metadata and continues the trace from the producer.

Instrument both the producer and consumer services with the X-Ray SDK. The producer adds the X-Ray trace header to SQS message attributes when sending messages. The consumer extracts the trace header from the received message and creates a linked subsegment, connecting both service traces.

Deploy AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT) on both services. ADOT's SQS instrumentation automatically extracts and injects trace context into SQS messages using the W3C Trace Context standard. Configure ADOT to export traces to X-Ray for unified visualization of async communication paths.

explanation: The X-Ray SDK propagates trace context through SQS message attributes. The producer adds the trace header, and the consumer extracts it to create linked trace segments. This connects synchronous and asynchronous communication in a single trace view. Option B describes automatic SQS tracing which doesn't exist as a native SQS feature. Option C's daemon doesn't handle SQS message-level trace propagation automatically. Option D uses ADOT which works but the standard X-Ray SDK provides this capability directly.

stem: A company needs to implement a secure CI/CD pipeline for a containerized application. The pipeline must scan for secrets in the source code, scan container images for vulnerabilities, and sign images before deployment. Which TWO pipeline stages address these security requirements? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Add a manual approval stage where a security engineer reviews the container image scan results and secret scan findings. The engineer approves the deployment only after confirming no critical vulnerabilities or exposed secrets exist, providing human verification of automated scan results.

Add a CodeBuild stage that builds the image, pushes to ECR, runs enhanced scanning to check for vulnerabilities, and upon clean results, signs the image with AWS Signer using a signing profile. Signed images are verified by ECS before deployment, ensuring only approved images run.

Add a CodeBuild stage that runs OWASP Dependency Check against the application's dependency files. The stage identifies known vulnerabilities in third-party libraries referenced in package.json, pom.xml, or requirements.txt, failing the build if high-severity dependency vulnerabilities are detected.

Add a CodeBuild stage that runs git-secrets or truffleHog to scan the repository for hardcoded secrets, API keys, and credentials. The stage fails the pipeline if any secrets are detected in the source code, preventing sensitive data from being included in the built container image.

Add a CodeBuild stage that builds the container image, pushes it to ECR, triggers ECR enhanced scanning, and evaluates scan results. If critical vulnerabilities are found, the stage signs the image using AWS Signer to mark it as scanned. If clean, it signs with a production-approved signature.

explanation: Secret scanning (Option A) prevents credentials from being included in images. Image scanning with signing (Option E) ensures only vulnerability-free, cryptographically signed images are deployed. Option B incorrectly signs vulnerable images. Option C scans dependencies but not container images. Option D adds manual approval which slows automation and isn't a pipeline stage addressing the specific security requirements.

stem: A company needs to implement a mechanism to detect and respond to AWS account compromise. If the root user logs in, if new IAM users are created outside of the CI/CD pipeline, or if CloudTrail is disabled, the security team must be alerted within 1 minute. Which detection approach provides near-real-time compromise indicators?

options.text: Configure AWS Config rules that evaluate root login activity, IAM user count changes, and CloudTrail enabled status. When Config detects non-compliance (root login, new IAM users, CloudTrail disabled), it triggers auto-remediation actions and sends notifications via SNS to the security team.

Enable GuardDuty which monitors CloudTrail management events for suspicious activity including root user logins, unauthorized IAM user creation, and CloudTrail tampering. GuardDuty generates findings for these compromise indicators with configurable severity-based notification thresholds.

Deploy a Lambda function on a 1-minute schedule that queries CloudTrail LookupEvents for root logins, checks IAM ListUsers for new users, and verifies CloudTrail status via GetTrailStatus. The function sends SNS alerts when any compromise indicator is detected during its scheduled evaluation.

Create EventBridge rules matching CloudTrail events for ConsoleLogin with root user identity, CreateUser API calls, and StopLogging/DeleteTrail API calls. Each rule triggers an SNS notification to the security team and a Lambda function that can take immediate containment actions.

explanation: EventBridge with CloudTrail event matching provides near-real-time detection (seconds) for specific API calls. Rules trigger immediately when the matching API event is recorded, enabling sub-minute alerting. Option B's GuardDuty provides threat detection but has finding generation latency that may exceed 1 minute. Option C's Config rules evaluate periodically, not in near-real-time. Option D polls every minute which meets the SLA but EventBridge's event-driven approach is more reliable and faster.

stem: A company needs to implement data classification for their S3 data lake. The classification system must automatically identify and tag objects containing PII, financial data, and healthcare information across 500 S3 buckets. Which service provides automated S3 data classification?

options.text: Enable Amazon Macie with automated sensitive data discovery across all 500 S3 buckets. Macie uses managed data identifiers and machine learning to automatically classify objects containing PII, financial data (credit cards, bank accounts), and healthcare information (PHI), generating classification findings.

Create custom AWS Config rules that evaluate S3 object metadata and tags for classification compliance. Deploy a Lambda function that samples objects from each bucket, runs regex patterns for PII/financial/healthcare data, and tags objects with classification labels based on pattern matches.

Configure AWS Glue Data Catalog with crawlers that scan S3 data and classify schemas. Enable the built-in PII detection classifier in Glue that identifies columns containing personal information. Use Glue's data classification results to tag S3 objects with appropriate sensitivity labels.

Deploy Amazon Comprehend with entity recognition to analyze S3 object contents. Create a Lambda function triggered by S3 PutObject events that sends object content to Comprehend for PII detection. Tag objects with classification labels based on Comprehend's detected entity types.

explanation: Macie provides purpose-built S3 data classification with managed data identifiers for PII, financial, and healthcare data patterns. It scales to hundreds of buckets with automated discovery and classification findings. Option B uses Comprehend for NLP analysis which is not optimized for structured data pattern detection like credit card numbers. Option C's Glue classifies schema structures, not content-level PII detection. Option D builds custom regex-based classification which doesn't match Macie's ML-based detection accuracy.

stem: A company uses CloudFormation with nested stacks. The parent stack references child stack templates stored in S3. When a child template is updated in S3, the parent stack does not automatically detect the change. The team needs parent stack updates to pick up child template changes. Which approach ensures parent stacks use the latest child templates?

options.text: Use S3 versioning on the template bucket and reference child templates using the specific S3 object version URL in the parent stack's TemplateURL property. Update the parent stack's TemplateURL to the new version URL when child templates change, triggering a nested stack update.

Reference child templates using S3 URLs without version specifiers. When child templates change in S3, run aws cloudformation update-stack on the parent stack with the same template. CloudFormation re-fetches child templates from S3 and applies any changes found in the updated child templates.

Create a Lambda-backed custom resource in the parent stack that checks S3 for child template modifications. When the custom resource detects a child template change, it triggers an update on the corresponding nested stack using the UpdateStack API with the new template URL.

Store child templates in a CodeCommit repository and use CloudFormation template packaging (aws cloudformation package) to upload templates to S3 with unique names. Each package operation creates new S3 keys, ensuring the parent template always references the latest child template version.

explanation: CloudFormation package command uploads templates to S3 with content-based unique keys (hashes). When child templates change, packaging produces new S3 keys that are automatically referenced in the parent template. This ensures updates always pick up the latest child templates. Option A requires manually tracking version URLs. Option B re-fetches templates but may not detect changes if the URL hasn't changed. Option D adds custom resource complexity for what packaging handles natively.

stem: A company runs an API on Lambda behind API Gateway. During a regional outage in us-east-1, the API must failover to us-west-2 within 60 seconds. The Lambda functions are deployed in both regions. Which multi-region architecture provides sub-60-second API failover?

options.text: Deploy API Gateway in both regions with custom domain names using Route 53 failover routing. Health checks monitor the primary API Gateway endpoint in us-east-1. When the health check fails, Route 53 routes traffic to the us-west-2 API Gateway within the health check detection interval.

Deploy API Gateway in both regions behind AWS Global Accelerator. Configure endpoint groups in both regions with health checks. Global Accelerator detects the us-east-1 endpoint failure and reroutes traffic to us-west-2 within seconds using its anycast IP routing without DNS propagation delays.

Deploy API Gateway in both regions behind a CloudFront distribution with origin groups. Configure the us-east-1 API Gateway as primary origin and us-west-2 as failover origin. CloudFront automatically retries failed requests on the failover origin, providing transparent regional failover.

Deploy a single API Gateway with Lambda@Edge functions instead of regional Lambda. Lambda@Edge runs at CloudFront edge locations globally, so a regional outage in us-east-1 doesn't affect API processing since the functions execute at the nearest edge location to each client.

explanation: Global Accelerator provides static anycast IPs with continuous health monitoring and instant traffic rerouting. Regional failover occurs within seconds at the network layer, well within the 60-second requirement. Option A uses Route 53 which has DNS TTL propagation delays that may approach or exceed 60 seconds. Option B's CloudFront origin failover retries individual requests but doesn't provide health-based regional failover. Option D's Lambda@Edge has limitations (no VPC access, limited runtime) that may not suit all API workloads.

stem: A company needs to detect when their application's behavior changes after a deployment. They want to automatically compare key metrics (latency p50, p95, p99, error rate, throughput) from the 1-hour window before deployment against the 1-hour window after deployment. Which approach automates post-deployment metric comparison?

options.text: Configure CloudWatch dashboards with annotation markers for each deployment. Add metric math expressions that calculate the difference between pre and post-deployment metric averages. The dashboard automatically shows the impact of each deployment on key metrics for manual review.

Enable X-Ray analytics for the application. X-Ray compares trace data between time windows, identifying latency distribution changes and error pattern differences. After each deployment, query X-Ray analytics to compare the pre and post-deployment trace statistics for behavioral changes.

Create CloudWatch anomaly detection models for each metric. After deployment, the anomaly detection bands represent expected behavior based on historical data. If post-deployment metrics fall outside the bands, CloudWatch alarms alert the team to behavioral changes caused by the deployment.

Deploy a Lambda function triggered by CodeDeploy deployment lifecycle events. The function queries CloudWatch GetMetricData for the pre-deployment and post-deployment windows, calculates statistical differences for each metric, and publishes a deployment impact report to SNS with comparison results.

explanation: A Lambda function triggered by deployment events provides automated metric comparison. It queries CloudWatch for specific pre/post time windows, calculates statistical differences, and reports results. Option B detects anomalies but doesn't compare specific pre/post deployment windows. Option C requires manual dashboard review. Option D provides trace-level analysis but doesn't automate the comparison or reporting workflow.

stem: A company needs to implement a pipeline that deploys infrastructure changes and application code in the correct order. The infrastructure (VPC, ALB, ECS cluster) must be deployed before the application (ECS service, task definition). Both are managed in separate CloudFormation stacks. Which CodePipeline configuration enforces deployment ordering?

options.text: Create a single CodePipeline with sequential stages: infrastructure deploy stage followed by application deploy stage. The infrastructure stage deploys the VPC/ALB/ECS cluster stack. The application stage deploys the ECS service stack only after the infrastructure stage succeeds.

Create a CodePipeline with a CodeBuild stage that deploys both stacks sequentially using the AWS CLI. The buildspec runs aws cloudformation deploy for the infrastructure stack first, waits for completion, then runs aws cloudformation deploy for the application stack.

Create a single CodePipeline with both stacks deployed in the same stage as parallel CloudFormation actions. Use CloudFormation cross-stack references (Fn::ImportValue) to create implicit ordering. CloudFormation resolves the dependencies and deploys the infrastructure stack before the application stack.

Create two separate CodePipelines: one for infrastructure and one for application. Configure the application pipeline's source stage to trigger only when the infrastructure pipeline completes successfully, using EventBridge to forward the infrastructure pipeline's success event to the application pipeline.

explanation: Sequential CodePipeline stages enforce strict ordering. The application stage only executes after the infrastructure stage completes successfully. This is the standard CodePipeline pattern for ordered multi-stack deployments. Option B adds complexity with two pipelines and EventBridge coupling. Option C deploys in parallel which doesn't guarantee ordering. Option D uses CodeBuild for CloudFormation deployment which loses CodePipeline's native CloudFormation integration and status tracking.

stem: A company needs to implement automated remediation for EC2 instances that are not sending logs to CloudWatch. When an instance stops sending logs for more than 10 minutes, the system must restart the CloudWatch agent on the instance and alert the operations team if the restart fails. Which approach detects and remediates silent log sources?

options.text: Deploy a Lambda function on a 5-minute schedule that queries CloudWatch Logs FilterLogEvents for each instance's log group. If no log events are found in the last 10 minutes, the function triggers SSM Run Command to restart the CloudWatch agent and sends an SNS notification about the silent instance.

Enable CloudWatch agent health monitoring using SSM State Manager with a compliance association. State Manager checks the CloudWatch agent status every 5 minutes. When the agent is detected as stopped, State Manager automatically restarts it and reports the compliance status for operations tracking.

Configure CloudWatch Logs subscription filters that forward log events to a Kinesis Data Stream. Deploy a Lambda consumer that tracks the last log event timestamp per instance. If no events are received for 10 minutes, the consumer triggers SSM Run Command to restart the CloudWatch agent.

Create a CloudWatch alarm using metric math that evaluates the IncomingLogEvents metric per log group. When the metric drops to zero for 10 minutes, the alarm triggers SSM Run Command to restart the CloudWatch agent on the associated instance. If the agent restart fails, SNS alerts the operations team.

explanation: CloudWatch alarm on IncomingLogEvents metric detects when log ingestion stops. SSM Run Command restarts the agent remotely, and alarm notification handles failure alerting. This is event-driven and uses native CloudWatch metrics. Option B polls which is less efficient than alarm-based detection. Option C adds Kinesis streaming infrastructure for what CloudWatch metrics handle natively. Option D checks agent process status but doesn't detect scenarios where the agent is running but not sending logs.

stem: A company needs to implement network isolation for their production ECS tasks so that they can only communicate with specific approved endpoints (RDS database, ElastiCache, S3 VPC endpoint). All other outbound network access must be blocked. Which networking configuration provides ECS task-level network isolation?

options.text: Configure Network ACLs on the ECS task subnets to deny all outbound traffic except to the specific IP ranges of the RDS, ElastiCache, and S3 VPC endpoint. NACLs provide stateless filtering at the subnet level, controlling which destinations ECS tasks can communicate with.

Deploy AWS Network Firewall in the VPC with stateful rules that allow ECS task traffic only to approved endpoints. Network Firewall inspects all outbound traffic and blocks connections to non-approved destinations, providing deep packet inspection for ECS task network isolation.

Deploy ECS tasks in private subnets with no NAT Gateway. Configure VPC endpoints for S3, RDS, and ElastiCache. Without a NAT Gateway or internet gateway, tasks can only reach services through VPC endpoints and private network connections, blocking all public internet access.

Deploy ECS tasks in awsvpc network mode with dedicated security groups per service. Configure the security group outbound rules to allow traffic only to the RDS, ElastiCache, and S3 VPC endpoint security groups on their specific ports. Remove the default allow-all outbound rule.

explanation: awsvpc network mode gives each ECS task its own ENI with a dedicated security group. Outbound rules restricting traffic to specific security groups on specific ports provide precise network isolation. Removing the default allow-all rule blocks unapproved destinations. Option B blocks internet access but allows all private network communication. Option C's NACLs operate at subnet level affecting all resources, not per-task. Option D adds Network Firewall infrastructure when security groups provide sufficient isolation.

stem: A company uses Terraform to manage their infrastructure and needs to refactor a monolithic Terraform configuration into multiple smaller modules without destroying and recreating existing resources. How should the team move resources between Terraform state files safely?

options.text: Create the new module configurations referencing the same resources. Run terraform apply in the new modules which will detect existing resources and adopt them. Then remove the resources from the monolithic configuration and run terraform apply to release them from the old state.

Use terraform import in the new module configurations to import existing resources. Then use terraform state rm in the monolithic configuration to remove the migrated resources. Run terraform plan in both configurations to verify no unexpected changes are planned.

Export the monolithic state file using terraform state pull, manually edit the JSON to reorganize resources into separate state files for each module, then push the edited state files using terraform state push to the respective module backends after validation.

Use terraform state mv to move resources from the monolithic state to the new module states. The state mv command updates the resource address in the state file without modifying the actual AWS resource. After moving, verify with terraform plan that no changes are detected in either state.

explanation: terraform state mv moves resource addresses between states without affecting the actual AWS resources. This is the safe, recommended approach for Terraform refactoring. Verifying with terraform plan confirms no changes are detected after the move. Option B uses import and remove which works but is more steps and riskier. Option C's terraform apply in new modules may attempt to create duplicate resources. Option D manually edits state files which is error-prone and not recommended.

stem: A company needs to implement a deployment pipeline for their AWS Lambda functions that uses container images instead of ZIP packages. The pipeline must build the container image, test it locally, push to ECR, and update the Lambda function. Which pipeline configuration deploys Lambda container images?

options.text: Configure CodePipeline with a CodeBuild stage that builds the container image and publishes it to ECR. Add a CodeDeploy action that deploys the new container image to Lambda using a blue/green deployment configuration with traffic shifting and CloudWatch alarm-based rollback.

Configure CodePipeline with a CodeBuild stage that builds and pushes the container image to ECR. Add a CloudFormation deploy action that updates the AWS::Lambda::Function resource's Code.ImageUri property with the new ECR image URI, triggering a Lambda function update.

Configure CodePipeline with a CodeBuild stage that builds the container image locally, tests it using SAM local invoke with the container image, and deploys using sam deploy which packages and pushes the image to ECR and updates the Lambda function through CloudFormation.

Configure CodePipeline with a CodeBuild stage that builds the Docker image using the Dockerfile, runs local tests using docker run, pushes the image to ECR, and updates the Lambda function using aws lambda update-function-code with the ECR image URI as the image parameter.

explanation: CodeBuild builds the container image, runs tests locally, pushes to ECR, and updates Lambda with the ECR image URI. This is the direct approach for Lambda container image deployment. Option B uses CloudFormation which works but adds template management overhead for a simple function update. Option C's CodeDeploy with Lambda requires SAM/CloudFormation for traffic shifting, not standalone CodeDeploy actions. Option D uses SAM which works but isn't required for container image Lambda deployment.

stem: A company needs to implement a mechanism that detects and responds to API Gateway throttling events. When API Gateway starts returning 429 responses to clients, the system must automatically increase the API's throttle limits and notify the operations team. Which approach detects API Gateway throttling in real-time?

options.text: Configure API Gateway access logging to CloudWatch Logs. Create a metric filter matching log entries with status code 429. Create a CloudWatch alarm on the extracted metric that triggers Lambda to increase throttle limits and SNS to notify the operations team about throttling events.

Enable API Gateway execution logging with detailed CloudWatch metrics. Create a composite alarm combining the Count metric (total requests) and IntegrationLatency metric. When both metrics indicate high load, proactively increase throttle limits before 429 responses start occurring.

Create a CloudWatch alarm on the API Gateway ThrottleCount metric which specifically tracks 429 responses. When the alarm breaches the threshold, it triggers a Lambda function that increases the stage-level throttle limits and sends an SNS notification to the operations team.

Create a CloudWatch alarm on the API Gateway 4XXError metric filtered by the 429 status code. When the alarm triggers, a Lambda function calls UpdateStage to increase the API's throttle rate and burst limits. An SNS notification alerts the operations team about the throttling event.

explanation: The API Gateway 4XXError metric can be filtered by status code to detect 429 throttling responses. A CloudWatch alarm on this metric triggers automated limit increases and notifications. Option B describes a ThrottleCount metric which doesn't exist as a standard API Gateway metric name. Option C adds log-based metric extraction when native metrics are available. Option D proactively scales before throttling but doesn't detect actual 429 responses.

stem: A company needs to implement encryption for data at rest across their entire AWS environment. All EBS volumes, S3 buckets, RDS databases, and DynamoDB tables must use encryption. Which TWO preventive controls ensure encryption is enforced for new resources? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Enable default EBS encryption at the account level in each AWS account. This automatically encrypts all new EBS volumes and snapshots without requiring users to specify encryption parameters when creating volumes, ensuring complete EBS encryption coverage.

Configure AWS Config rules (encrypted-volumes, s3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled, rds-storage-encrypted, dynamodb-table-encrypted-kms) to detect unencrypted resources. Enable auto-remediation to encrypt non-compliant resources immediately after they are created.

Deploy CloudFormation Hooks that validate encryption configuration on all resource types before provisioning. The hooks check for encryption properties on EBS, S3, RDS, and DynamoDB resources and block stack creation if any resource lacks encryption configuration.

Create IAM policies attached to all user and role principals that include condition keys requiring encryption parameters on resource creation actions. The IAM conditions enforce encryption at the identity level, preventing unencrypted resource creation regardless of the creation method.

Create SCPs that deny resource creation API calls (ec2:CreateVolume, s3:CreateBucket, rds:CreateDBInstance, dynamodb:CreateTable) unless encryption-related condition keys are present. The SCPs enforce encryption parameters on all resource creation across the organization.

explanation: SCPs (Option A) enforce encryption across the organization for all resource types, blocking unencrypted resource creation at the API level. Default EBS encryption (Option B) automatically encrypts all new EBS resources without user action. Option C detects and remediates after creation, not preventively. Option D only covers CloudFormation deployments, not console or CLI resource creation. Option E requires managing IAM policies for every principal.

stem: A company uses AWS CDK with TypeScript and needs to deploy the same application stack to multiple environments (dev, staging, prod) with different configurations. Each environment has different instance sizes, domain names, and feature flags. Which CDK pattern manages multi-environment configuration?

options.text: Define an interface for environment configuration and create configuration objects for each environment. Instantiate the stack multiple times in the CDK app with different environment configurations. Use cdk deploy StackName-dev or cdk deploy StackName-prod to deploy specific environments.

Create separate CDK apps for each environment, each importing the shared stack from a published npm package. Each app instantiates the stack with environment-specific props. Deploy each app independently using its own cdk.json configuration and deployment pipeline.

Create a CDK context file (cdk.json) with environment-specific configuration blocks. Use node.tryGetContext() in the CDK code to retrieve environment-specific values based on a context variable passed during cdk deploy. Each environment is deployed with -c env=dev, -c env=staging, or -c env=prod.

Use environment variables in the CDK code to select configuration values. Set ENVIRONMENT=dev before running cdk deploy. The CDK code reads process.env.ENVIRONMENT and selects the corresponding configuration from a configuration map for instance sizes, domains, and feature flags.

explanation: Defining typed configuration interfaces and instantiating the stack multiple times with different configs is the recommended CDK pattern. Each environment gets its own named stack instance with explicit configuration. Deploying by stack name targets specific environments. Option A uses context which works but lacks type safety. Option B creates separate apps which adds unnecessary project management overhead. Option D uses environment variables which are less explicit and harder to version control than typed configurations.

stem: A company's application uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster with one writer and two reader instances. Read traffic is distributed across readers using the Aurora reader endpoint. When one reader instance fails, some read requests fail until the DNS endpoint updates. How should the team minimize read failure impact during reader instance failures?

options.text: Deploy RDS Proxy with a read-only endpoint pointing to the Aurora cluster's reader instances. RDS Proxy multiplexes connections and handles instance failover transparently, redirecting read traffic away from failed readers without DNS propagation delays or application-level retry logic.

Configure the application to use the Aurora reader endpoint with a short DNS TTL and implement connection retry logic with exponential backoff. When a reader fails, the retry logic handles the brief DNS propagation period while the endpoint updates to exclude the failed reader.

Create individual instance endpoints for each reader and implement application-level load balancing with health checks. The application maintains a list of reader endpoints, distributes reads using round-robin, and removes unhealthy readers from the rotation based on connection test results.

Add a third reader instance to the Aurora cluster for additional redundancy. With three readers, the loss of one reader only reduces read capacity by one-third while the reader endpoint DNS updates. The remaining two readers handle the read traffic during the brief failover period.

explanation: RDS Proxy provides connection-level failover handling, transparently routing read traffic away from failed reader instances without DNS propagation delays. Applications maintain their existing connections through the proxy. Option A relies on DNS updates and retry logic which still causes brief failures. Option C builds custom load balancing when RDS Proxy provides this natively. Option D adds capacity but doesn't prevent read failures during the DNS update window.

stem: A company needs to implement alerting that detects when their Lambda function's cold start percentage increases above 15% of total invocations. Cold starts are identified by the INIT_START log entry in CloudWatch Logs. Which monitoring approach calculates cold start percentage?

options.text: Deploy Lambda Powertools with the Metrics utility configured to emit a custom cold_start metric. Powertools automatically detects cold starts and publishes a boolean metric. Use CloudWatch metric math to calculate the percentage of cold starts from the custom metric data for alarming.

Enable Lambda Insights which automatically tracks cold start metrics. Lambda Insights publishes the init_duration metric for cold starts and the total invocation count. Create a CloudWatch alarm on the cold start percentage derived from these Lambda Insights metrics.

Configure X-Ray active tracing on the Lambda function. X-Ray captures initialization segments for cold starts. Query X-Ray analytics to calculate the cold start percentage and create a CloudWatch custom metric from the X-Ray data for alarming when the percentage exceeds 15%.

Create two CloudWatch Logs metric filters: one matching INIT_START entries (cold starts) and one matching START entries (all invocations). Use CloudWatch metric math to calculate the ratio of cold starts to total invocations as a percentage. Create an alarm when the ratio exceeds 15%.

explanation: Two metric filters (INIT_START for cold starts, START for all invocations) combined with metric math provide a calculated cold start percentage. An alarm on the ratio detects when cold starts exceed 15%. Option B's Lambda Insights tracks init_duration but doesn't directly publish a cold start percentage metric. Option C uses X-Ray which captures initialization data but doesn't provide ongoing percentage-based monitoring. Option D requires code changes when log-based metric filters work without modification.

stem: A company needs to implement a deployment strategy that enables instant rollback for their CloudFront-distributed static website. The current deployment replaces files in the S3 origin bucket, making rollback slow because files must be re-uploaded and the CloudFront cache must be invalidated. Which deployment approach enables instant rollback?

options.text: Enable S3 versioning and deploy by overwriting existing files. For rollback, restore previous object versions for all files using S3 batch operations. Create a CloudFront cache invalidation after restoring previous versions so CloudFront serves the restored content from the origin.

Maintain two S3 buckets (blue and green) as CloudFront origins in an origin group. Deploy new versions to the inactive bucket. Switch the CloudFront origin group's primary origin to the newly deployed bucket. For rollback, switch back to the previous bucket as the primary origin.

Deploy each version to a uniquely named S3 prefix (e.g., /v1.2.3/). Update the CloudFront origin path to point to the new version's prefix. For rollback, change the CloudFront origin path back to the previous version's prefix. The previous files are still in S3 under the old prefix.

Deploy new versions to a separate S3 bucket and use CloudFront Lambda@Edge to route requests to the appropriate bucket based on a version header or cookie. For rollback, update the Lambda@Edge function to route all requests back to the previous version's bucket.

explanation: Versioned S3 prefixes with CloudFront origin path switching provides instant rollback. Each version's files remain in S3 under their prefix. Changing the origin path immediately serves the previous version since CloudFront fetches from the new path on cache miss. Option B requires file restoration and cache invalidation which is slow. Option C requires two full S3 buckets and origin group reconfiguration. Option D adds Lambda@Edge complexity for request routing.

stem: A company experienced a cascading failure where a single database connection pool exhaustion in one microservice caused timeouts that propagated to all upstream services. The team needs to prevent future cascading failures from connection pool issues. Which resilience pattern addresses connection pool exhaustion?

options.text: Increase the maximum connection pool size to handle peak load with a 2x safety margin. Larger connection pools accommodate traffic bursts without exhaustion. Configure connection pool idle timeout to release unused connections back to the pool quickly during low-traffic periods.

Deploy RDS Proxy to manage database connections. RDS Proxy maintains a shared connection pool that multiplexes application connections to a smaller set of database connections. This prevents individual microservice pool exhaustion from consuming all available database connections.

Implement the bulkhead pattern by creating separate connection pools for each downstream dependency. If one dependency's pool is exhausted, other dependencies maintain their own independent pools. This prevents connection pool exhaustion for one service from blocking connections to other services.

Implement connection pool monitoring with CloudWatch custom metrics that track pool utilization, active connections, and waiting threads. Create alarms when pool utilization exceeds 80% to alert operators before exhaustion occurs. Operators scale the database to handle additional connections.

explanation: The bulkhead pattern isolates connection pools per dependency, preventing one dependency's exhaustion from cascading to others. Each pool has its own limits, so a slow database doesn't consume connections meant for other services. Option B monitors but doesn't prevent cascading failures. Option C increases pool size but still uses a single shared pool that can be exhausted. Option D manages database connections but doesn't address application-side connection pool isolation between dependencies.

stem: A company needs to implement continuous compliance monitoring for PCI DSS requirements across their AWS environment. The monitoring must evaluate network segmentation, encryption configuration, access controls, and logging requirements. Which service provides PCI DSS compliance evaluation?

options.text: Configure AWS Config with PCI DSS conformance packs that include rules evaluating encryption, network segmentation, access controls, and logging. The conformance pack provides a compliance dashboard showing per-rule compliance status across all evaluated resources for PCI DSS controls.

Enable AWS Security Hub with the PCI DSS security standard enabled across all accounts. Security Hub continuously evaluates resources against PCI DSS controls and provides a compliance dashboard showing the overall compliance score and per-control pass/fail status with remediation guidance.

Deploy AWS Audit Manager with the PCI DSS assessment framework. Audit Manager collects evidence from multiple AWS services to demonstrate compliance with PCI DSS requirements. It generates assessment reports with evidence attachments for auditor review during PCI DSS certification.

Run Amazon Inspector assessments using the PCI DSS scanning template. Inspector evaluates EC2 instances and container images against PCI DSS technical requirements including patch management, vulnerability scanning, and configuration hardening for cardholder data environment instances.

explanation: Security Hub's PCI DSS standard provides continuous automated compliance evaluation against PCI DSS controls. It evaluates resources for encryption, access controls, logging, and network configuration with per-control compliance scoring. Option B collects evidence for audits but doesn't provide continuous automated evaluation. Option C evaluates individual Config rules but doesn't provide the integrated PCI DSS compliance scoring. Option D evaluates instance-level vulnerabilities, not the full breadth of PCI DSS controls.

stem: A company has a microservices application with 20 services, each with its own CodePipeline. When a shared library is updated, all 20 service pipelines must be triggered to rebuild with the new library version. Which approach triggers multiple pipelines from a single event?

options.text: Publish the shared library to CodeArtifact with a new version. Create an EventBridge rule matching CodeArtifact package version publish events. The rule triggers a Lambda function that starts all 20 CodePipeline executions using the StartPipelineExecution API for each pipeline.

Publish the shared library to an S3 bucket. Configure an S3 event notification that triggers an SNS topic. Each of the 20 CodePipelines has a source action configured with the same S3 bucket and object key, triggering all pipelines when the library artifact is uploaded.

Deploy the shared library as a Lambda Layer. When the layer is updated, configure an EventBridge rule matching Lambda Layer version creation events. The rule triggers a Step Functions workflow that starts all 20 pipelines sequentially, waiting for each to complete before starting the next.

Store the shared library in a CodeCommit repository. Configure each of the 20 service pipelines with a source action that monitors the shared library repository in addition to their own service repository. Any change to the library triggers all 20 pipelines automatically.

explanation: CodeArtifact with EventBridge provides event-driven pipeline triggering when the shared library version is published. The Lambda function starts all 20 pipelines in parallel. Option B adds a source dependency to each pipeline which triggers on any library repository change, not just version publishes. Option C uses Lambda Layers which isn't applicable to all service types and sequential execution is slow for 20 services. Option D uses S3 triggers which can be fragile for multi-pipeline coordination.

stem: A company runs a critical payment processing system that must maintain exactly-once processing semantics. The system uses SQS FIFO queues with Lambda consumers. During a Lambda function timeout, the message becomes visible again and is processed a second time, causing duplicate payments. How should the team prevent duplicate payment processing?

options.text: Configure the Lambda event source mapping with a maximum concurrency of 1 for the FIFO queue. Single-threaded processing ensures only one message is processed at a time, preventing concurrent processing that could lead to duplicate payments when messages are redelivered.

Enable content-based deduplication on the SQS FIFO queue. Content-based deduplication automatically rejects messages with identical content within the 5-minute deduplication window, preventing the same payment message from being processed twice by the Lambda consumer.

Implement idempotency in the Lambda function using a DynamoDB table as an idempotency store. Before processing each payment, check DynamoDB for the message's deduplication ID. If found, skip processing. If not found, process the payment and record the ID in DynamoDB atomically.

Increase the SQS FIFO queue visibility timeout to be longer than the Lambda function's maximum execution time. This prevents the message from becoming visible again while the Lambda function is still processing, eliminating the redelivery that causes duplicate processing.

explanation: Idempotency with DynamoDB ensures each payment is processed exactly once regardless of redelivery. Checking the deduplication ID before processing prevents duplicate payments even when Lambda times out and the message is redelivered. Option B reduces redelivery likelihood but doesn't prevent it if Lambda crashes or is throttled. Option C deduplicates at send time, not at processing time; a message already in the queue will be redelivered after visibility timeout. Option D limits concurrency but doesn't prevent reprocessing of the same message.

stem: A company needs to implement health checking for their multi-tier application that detects failures at each tier (load balancer, application server, database). The health check must distinguish between tier-specific failures to enable targeted remediation. Which health check architecture provides tier-specific failure detection?

options.text: Implement a deep health check endpoint on the application that verifies connectivity to the database (SELECT 1 query) and returns a JSON response indicating the health status of each tier. Create CloudWatch Synthetics canaries that call this endpoint and parse the response for per-tier health.

Deploy AWS Health checks using Amazon EventBridge to monitor each tier's AWS service health. EventBridge routes AWS Health events for ELB, ECS, and RDS to Lambda functions that correlate service health events with application-level impact for targeted remediation decisions.

Create separate Route 53 health checks for each tier: an HTTP health check on the ALB endpoint, a TCP health check on the application server port, and a TCP health check on the database port. Create a calculated health check that combines all three for overall health assessment.

Configure CloudWatch alarms for each tier: ALB HealthyHostCount for the load balancer, ECS RunningTaskCount for the application, and RDS DatabaseConnections for the database. Create a composite alarm that evaluates all three tiers and identifies which specific tier is experiencing the failure.

explanation: A deep health check endpoint that verifies each tier and returns structured per-tier status provides the most detailed failure information. Synthetics canaries continuously test the endpoint and parse responses for tier-specific health. Option B uses network-level checks that can't distinguish application-level failures. Option C monitors metrics which indicate symptoms but don't directly test tier connectivity from the application's perspective. Option D monitors AWS service health, not application-tier health.

stem: A company needs to implement a mechanism that automatically creates a detailed timeline of events during an outage for post-incident review. The timeline must include CloudWatch alarm state changes, deployment events, configuration changes, and scaling events that occurred during the incident window. Which service creates an automated incident timeline?

options.text: Configure Amazon DevOps Guru to monitor the application resources. DevOps Guru automatically correlates related operational events including deployments, configuration changes, and metric anomalies into proactive insights with timelines that help identify the root cause of operational issues.

Configure AWS Systems Manager Incident Manager with response plans. Incident Manager automatically creates an incident timeline that includes related CloudWatch alarm changes, SSM automation executions, and manual actions taken by responders during the incident for post-incident review.

Create a CloudWatch dashboard that displays all relevant metrics, alarms, and events on a single time-synchronized view. During post-incident review, operators manually annotate the dashboard with deployment and configuration change timestamps to construct the incident timeline.

Deploy a Lambda function triggered by incident creation events that queries CloudTrail for API calls, CloudWatch for alarm state changes, CodePipeline for deployment events, and Auto Scaling for scaling activities during the incident window. The function compiles a timeline in DynamoDB.

explanation: Incident Manager automatically creates and maintains an incident timeline that includes alarm changes, automation actions, and responder activities. The timeline is built as the incident progresses, providing a ready-made record for post-incident review. Option B builds a custom timeline generator. Option C provides proactive insights but doesn't create incident-specific timelines. Option D requires manual dashboard analysis and annotation.

stem: A company needs to detect when sensitive data is being exfiltrated from their S3 buckets. The detection must identify unusual data access patterns such as large downloads from unfamiliar IP addresses or bulk GetObject requests outside normal business hours. Which service detects S3 data exfiltration patterns?

options.text: Enable Amazon Macie with automated sensitive data discovery. Macie monitors S3 bucket access patterns and generates policy findings when unusual data access is detected. Macie's ML models identify anomalous access volumes and access from unfamiliar principals for exfiltration detection.

Configure CloudTrail S3 data event logging and create CloudWatch Logs metric filters matching GetObject events. Create alarms for unusual download volumes based on static thresholds. Deploy a Lambda function that analyzes source IP addresses against known company IP ranges for anomaly detection.

Enable Amazon GuardDuty with S3 protection. GuardDuty analyzes S3 data events from CloudTrail to detect unusual access patterns including anomalous data downloads, access from suspicious IP addresses, and data retrieval from Tor exit nodes, generating findings for potential exfiltration.

Deploy VPC Flow Logs on the VPC endpoints used for S3 access. Analyze flow logs for unusual data transfer volumes to S3 endpoints during off-hours. Create CloudWatch alarms on flow log metrics when outbound data transfer exceeds normal baseline thresholds for S3 traffic.

explanation: GuardDuty S3 protection uses ML to analyze CloudTrail S3 data events and detect anomalous access patterns including data exfiltration indicators. It identifies unusual download volumes, access from suspicious IPs, and Tor exit node access without custom rule creation. Option B's Macie classifies data sensitivity but doesn't focus on access pattern anomaly detection. Option C builds custom monitoring with static thresholds that don't adapt to normal patterns. Option D monitors network-level flows which can't identify specific S3 access patterns.

stem: A company uses CloudFormation and needs to deploy resources that have circular dependencies. Resource A needs the ID of Resource B, and Resource B needs the ID of Resource A. CloudFormation cannot resolve this circular reference. Which approach breaks the circular dependency?

options.text: Use CloudFormation conditions to create Resources A and B in a specific order. Add a Condition that checks if Resource B exists before creating the reference from A to B. On the first deployment, Resource A is created without the reference, then a second update adds the reference.

Split the deployment into two CloudFormation stacks. Stack 1 creates Resource A with a placeholder configuration. Stack 2 creates Resource B referencing Resource A's output. Then update Stack 1 to configure Resource A with Resource B's ID from Stack 2's output using cross-stack references.

Use the DependsOn attribute to force Resource A to be created before Resource B. Reference Resource A from Resource B using Ref. For the reverse reference, use a CloudFormation parameter with a default value that represents Resource B's expected ID based on the naming convention.

Define both resources without cross-references in the same stack. Add a Lambda-backed custom resource that runs after both resources are created. The custom resource updates Resource A with Resource B's ID and Resource B with Resource A's ID using the AWS SDK to complete the circular configuration.

explanation: A Lambda custom resource runs after both resources exist and can update their configurations to reference each other. This breaks the circular dependency by separating creation from cross-referencing. Option A requires two stacks and a stack update which adds complexity. Option B's conditions can't conditionally create references within a single deployment. Option D uses predicted IDs which is fragile and unreliable.

stem: A company is implementing a CI/CD pipeline for a serverless application using AWS SAM. The pipeline must validate the SAM template, run unit tests, deploy to a staging environment, run integration tests, and deploy to production with canary traffic shifting. Which TWO SAM-specific features should be used in this pipeline? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Use sam validate to check the SAM template for syntax errors and valid resource definitions in the CI stage. sam validate catches template errors before any build or deployment occurs, providing fast feedback on template issues without consuming build resources.

Use sam local invoke and sam local start-api in the CodeBuild stage to run integration tests against locally emulated Lambda functions and API Gateway endpoints. SAM local testing validates function behavior without deploying to AWS, reducing testing costs and feedback time.

Use sam sync for the staging deployment stage instead of sam deploy. sam sync provides faster deployment by only uploading and updating resources that have changed, using the AWS API directly instead of creating CloudFormation change sets for each deployment.

Configure DeploymentPreference with Type: Canary10Percent10Minutes in the SAM template's Globals section. This tells SAM to use CodeDeploy for canary traffic shifting on all Lambda functions, gradually shifting traffic to the new version with automatic rollback on alarm triggers.

Configure sam pipeline init to generate the CI/CD pipeline configuration files. SAM pipeline bootstrap creates the required infrastructure (S3 buckets, IAM roles, CodePipeline) for the deployment pipeline, automating the pipeline setup without manual resource configuration.

explanation: sam validate (Option A) catches template errors early in the pipeline without deployment. DeploymentPreference with canary configuration (Option B) provides SAM-native canary deployment with automatic rollback. Option C's sam local testing is useful but the question asks about SAM-specific pipeline features, and local testing is a development tool, not a pipeline-specific feature. Option D is for pipeline setup, not pipeline stages. Option E's sam sync is for development, not production deployment pipelines.

stem: A company runs a real-time data pipeline using Kinesis Data Streams with 10 shards. During peak traffic, the producers receive ProvisionedThroughputExceededException errors because the traffic exceeds the stream's write capacity. The team needs to handle traffic spikes without manual shard management. Which Kinesis configuration handles variable traffic volumes?

options.text: Implement producer-side retry with exponential backoff and jitter when ProvisionedThroughputExceededException is received. The retry logic distributes writes more evenly across shards by adding random jitter to the partition key, reducing hot shard scenarios that cause localized throttling.

Configure Auto Scaling for the Kinesis Data Stream using a CloudWatch alarm on the WriteProvisionedThroughputExceeded metric. When throttling is detected, a Lambda function calls UpdateShardCount to increase the shard count. A separate alarm triggers scale-down when utilization decreases.

Enable Kinesis Data Streams on-demand capacity mode. On-demand mode automatically scales the number of shards to accommodate write throughput up to 200 MB/s without requiring capacity planning or manual shard splitting. The stream adapts to traffic patterns within seconds.

Increase the number of shards from 10 to 50 to provide 5x headroom above normal traffic levels. Pre-provisioning excess capacity eliminates throttling during peak periods. Configure enhanced fan-out for consumers to maintain read throughput at the higher shard count.

explanation: On-demand capacity mode eliminates the need for manual shard management. The stream automatically scales write and read capacity to match traffic volume, handling spikes without ProvisionedThroughputExceededException errors. Option B builds custom auto-scaling when on-demand provides this natively. Option C handles throttling at the producer level but doesn't increase stream capacity. Option D over-provisions which increases cost and doesn't adapt to unexpected traffic patterns.

stem: A company needs to implement a cost-effective log archival strategy. Current CloudWatch Logs retention is set to indefinite, costing $50,000/month. The team needs to retain logs for 7 years for compliance while reducing costs. Logs older than 30 days are rarely accessed but must be searchable when needed. Which archival strategy reduces costs while maintaining searchability?

options.text: Set CloudWatch Logs retention to 30 days. Configure a subscription filter to stream all logs to S3 via Kinesis Data Firehose with Parquet format conversion. Store logs in S3 with lifecycle policies transitioning to S3 Glacier after 90 days. Use Athena to query archived logs when needed.

Keep all logs in CloudWatch Logs but change the log class to CloudWatch Logs Infrequent Access for log groups older than 30 days. Infrequent Access class provides the same retention and query capabilities at 50% lower cost compared to standard CloudWatch Logs storage pricing.

Set CloudWatch Logs retention to 7 days and stream all logs to Amazon OpenSearch Service with UltraWarm and cold storage tiers. OpenSearch provides full-text search on warm data and cost-effective cold storage for older data. Configure index lifecycle management for automatic tiering.

Set CloudWatch Logs retention to 30 days. Use CloudWatch Logs export tasks on a daily schedule to export logs to S3 in gzip format. Configure S3 lifecycle policies to transition logs to S3 Intelligent-Tiering after 30 days and S3 Glacier after 1 year for the 7-year retention.

explanation: Streaming to S3 via Firehose with Parquet format provides compact storage with Athena queryability. S3 lifecycle policies transition to Glacier for long-term archival at minimal cost. This dramatically reduces storage costs from CloudWatch Logs pricing while maintaining 7-year searchable retention. Option B uses export tasks which are less efficient than streaming for continuous archival. Option C's Infrequent Access class has limitations on Logs Insights queries. Option D's OpenSearch adds significant infrastructure cost for long-term storage.

stem: A company needs to implement a service-level objective (SLO) burn rate alert. When the error budget for their 99.9% availability SLO is being consumed at a rate that would exhaust the monthly budget within 6 hours, the team must be paged immediately. Which monitoring approach implements burn rate alerting?

options.text: Configure CloudWatch Application Signals with an SLO targeting 99.9% availability over a 30-day window. Application Signals automatically calculates burn rates and supports configurable burn rate alerting thresholds. Set the alert to trigger when the 6-hour burn rate exceeds the budget consumption rate.

Deploy a Lambda function every 5 minutes that calculates the remaining error budget by querying the total errors and requests for the current month. The function calculates the current burn rate (budget consumed / time elapsed) and pages the team when the projected exhaustion time falls below 6 hours.

Create a CloudWatch metric math expression that calculates the current error rate over a sliding 6-hour window. Compare this rate against the maximum allowable error rate (0.1% for 99.9% SLO). Create an alarm when the 6-hour error rate would exhaust the monthly budget if sustained for the remaining period.

Configure CloudWatch anomaly detection on the error rate metric. When the error rate exceeds the anomaly detection band for more than 1 hour, page the team. The anomaly detection model adapts to normal error patterns and alerts when errors deviate significantly from the expected baseline.

explanation: Application Signals provides native SLO monitoring with automatic burn rate calculation and alerting. It tracks error budget consumption rates and can alert when the burn rate would exhaust the budget within configurable time windows. Option B builds custom burn rate calculation with metric math which is complex. Option C deploys custom Lambda-based burn rate tracking. Option D detects anomalies but doesn't calculate burn rates against specific SLO targets.

stem: A company needs to implement a mechanism that prevents accidental or malicious deletion of critical CloudFormation stacks in production. Even administrators should not be able to delete stacks without going through an approval process. Which protection mechanism prevents unauthorized stack deletion?

options.text: Enable CloudFormation stack termination protection on all production stacks. Termination protection must be explicitly disabled before a stack can be deleted. Combine with an SCP that denies cloudformation:UpdateTerminationProtection to prevent administrators from disabling the protection.

Enable AWS Backup with backup plans for all production CloudFormation stack resources. If a stack is accidentally deleted, AWS Backup retains the resource configurations and can restore all stack resources to their pre-deletion state within the defined recovery point objective.

Configure CloudWatch alarms that trigger on CloudFormation DeleteStack API calls via CloudTrail. The alarm sends an SNS notification to the security team and triggers a Lambda function that creates a new stack from the most recent template to immediately restore deleted stacks.

Create an IAM policy that denies cloudformation:DeleteStack for all production stacks identified by a naming convention or tag. Attach the policy to all IAM roles and users. Only a break-glass IAM role with MFA requirement can delete production stacks in emergency situations.

explanation: Termination protection prevents stack deletion until explicitly disabled. Combining with an SCP that denies UpdateTerminationProtection creates a two-layer defense where even administrators cannot bypass the protection without SCP modification. Option B uses IAM denial which administrators could modify. Option C detects deletion after the fact. Option D provides backup-based recovery which doesn't prevent deletion.

stem: A company uses GitHub as their source code repository and needs to trigger AWS CodePipeline when changes are pushed to specific branches. The connection must be secure and use webhook-based triggering for near-instant pipeline starts. Which integration connects GitHub to CodePipeline?

options.text: Configure a GitHub Action workflow that runs on push events to the target branch. The workflow uses the AWS CLI to call aws codepipeline start-pipeline-execution to trigger the CodePipeline. Store AWS credentials as GitHub Secrets for authentication in the GitHub Actions workflow.

Create a CodePipeline source stage using the GitHub (Version 2) action provider with an OAuth token stored in Secrets Manager. The OAuth token authenticates CodePipeline's polling of the GitHub repository for changes, triggering the pipeline when new commits are detected.

Create an AWS CodeConnections (formerly CodeStar Connections) connection to the GitHub repository. Configure the CodePipeline source stage with the CodeConnections source action type, specifying the repository, branch, and connection ARN. CodeConnections handles authentication and webhook setup automatically.

Create a GitHub webhook that sends push events to an API Gateway endpoint. The API Gateway triggers a Lambda function that validates the webhook payload and calls StartPipelineExecution to trigger the CodePipeline. The Lambda function filters events by branch name before triggering.

explanation: CodeConnections provides the native, secure integration between GitHub and CodePipeline with automatic webhook management. It handles authentication using an app installation model rather than personal tokens, and webhooks provide near-instant triggering. Option B builds custom webhook handling when CodeConnections provides this natively. Option C uses GitHub Actions to trigger CodePipeline which adds unnecessary intermediary steps. Option D describes OAuth-based polling which is the older integration method.

stem: A company's multi-AZ RDS MySQL database experienced a failover during a maintenance window. After failover, the application reported a high number of broken database connections and took 5 minutes to recover. How should the team reduce application recovery time after RDS failover?

options.text: Configure the application's connection pool with connection validation that detects broken connections before use. Enable test-on-borrow with a lightweight validation query. The pool automatically replaces broken connections with new connections to the current primary instance.

Switch to Amazon Aurora MySQL which provides faster failover than standard RDS MySQL. Aurora's writer endpoint DNS updates within 30 seconds after failover. Configure the application's JDBC connection string with the Aurora cluster endpoint for automatic primary instance discovery.

Increase the application's connection pool size and configure aggressive connection refresh intervals. The pool pre-creates connections and replaces them frequently, ensuring fresh connections are available. During failover, the pool quickly establishes new connections to the promoted standby.

Deploy Amazon RDS Proxy between the application and the RDS database. RDS Proxy maintains a pool of database connections and transparently handles failover by redirecting connections to the new primary instance. Applications experience minimal disruption during failover events.

explanation: RDS Proxy handles failover transparency by maintaining its own connection pool to the database. During failover, the proxy redirects application connections to the new primary without breaking application-side connections. This dramatically reduces recovery time from minutes to seconds. Option B improves connection validation but still requires the application to detect and recreate broken connections. Option C pre-creates connections but doesn't prevent breakage during failover. Option D improves failover speed but still breaks existing connections.

stem: A company needs to implement a dashboard that shows the current deployment status of all 30 microservices across development, staging, and production environments. The dashboard must show which version is deployed in each environment and when the last deployment occurred. Which approach provides a deployment status dashboard?

options.text: Create a CloudWatch dashboard with custom widgets powered by Lambda functions. Each Lambda function queries CodeDeploy and CodePipeline APIs to retrieve current deployment information for each service and environment. The widgets display version numbers, deployment timestamps, and status.

Configure CodePipeline notifications for each service pipeline to send deployment events to CloudWatch Logs. Create CloudWatch Logs Insights queries that extract service names, versions, and environments from deployment events. Display the query results on a CloudWatch dashboard.

Store deployment metadata in a DynamoDB table updated by CodePipeline event notifications. Each deployment record includes service name, environment, version, timestamp, and status. Build a custom web dashboard that queries DynamoDB to display the current deployment matrix across all services.

Use AWS Systems Manager Application Manager to create an application definition for each microservice. Application Manager provides a unified view of application resources, deployments, and operational data across environments, showing current deployment versions and health status.

explanation: CloudWatch dashboard with Lambda-backed custom widgets provides a real-time deployment status view. Lambda functions query CodeDeploy and CodePipeline APIs for current deployment information across all services and environments. Option B builds a custom web application which is more development effort. Option C uses log-based queries which are less reliable for real-time status than API queries. Option D provides application-level views but may not consolidate all 30 services in a single deployment matrix view.

stem: A company needs to implement automated rollback for their Kubernetes deployments on EKS. If a deployment causes the pod error rate to exceed 5% within the first 10 minutes, the deployment must automatically roll back to the previous version. Which Kubernetes-native approach implements automated rollback?

options.text: Deploy Argo Rollouts with a canary strategy that monitors a Prometheus metric for pod error rate. Configure the analysis template to query the error rate metric every minute for 10 minutes. If the error rate exceeds 5%, Argo Rollouts automatically aborts the rollout and reverts to the previous version.

Create a CloudWatch alarm on the EKS Container Insights pod error metric with a 5% threshold and 10-minute evaluation period. The alarm triggers a Lambda function that executes kubectl rollout undo against the EKS cluster to revert the deployment to the previous version.

Implement a Flagger canary release controller that integrates with the EKS service mesh. Flagger gradually shifts traffic to the new version while monitoring pod error rates. If the error rate exceeds the 5% threshold during the analysis period, Flagger automatically rolls back the release.

Configure the Kubernetes deployment with progressDeadlineSeconds set to 600 and minReadySeconds set to 60. If pods fail readiness probes within the progress deadline, Kubernetes automatically rolls back the deployment to the previous ReplicaSet revision using the built-in rollback mechanism.

explanation: Argo Rollouts provides advanced deployment strategies with automated analysis and rollback. The canary strategy with metric-based analysis templates monitors error rates and automatically aborts rollouts when thresholds are breached. Option B uses native Kubernetes rollback which only detects pod startup failures, not application-level error rates. Option C builds external monitoring with Lambda which is less integrated than Kubernetes-native tools. Option D uses Flagger which works but requires a service mesh; Argo Rollouts works without one.

stem: A company needs to implement a solution that automatically generates IAM policies based on actual service usage. The team wants to replace overly permissive wildcard policies with least-privilege policies that only include the permissions actually used by each role. Which service generates usage-based IAM policies?

options.text: Configure AWS Config with the iam-policy-no-statements-with-full-access rule. Config identifies IAM policies with wildcard actions. For each flagged policy, manually review the associated role's CloudTrail activity to determine which specific permissions are needed and create a replacement policy.

Enable IAM Access Analyzer policy generation. Access Analyzer reviews CloudTrail logs for the last 90 days to identify the actual AWS service actions and resources used by each IAM role. It generates a least-privilege policy based on observed activity that can replace the existing overly permissive policy.

Enable AWS CloudTrail and query the trail logs to manually identify which API actions each IAM role has called. Create custom IAM policies that include only the observed API actions and resource ARNs. Replace the wildcard policies with the custom least-privilege policies.

Use IAM Access Analyzer to review existing IAM policies for findings about overly permissive access. Access Analyzer identifies policies that grant access to external principals or unused permissions. Use the findings to manually reduce policy permissions to the minimum required.

explanation: IAM Access Analyzer policy generation automatically analyzes CloudTrail logs to determine which API actions and resources each role actually uses, then generates a recommended least-privilege policy. This automates the process of creating minimum-permission policies. Option B manually analyzes CloudTrail which Access Analyzer automates. Option C identifies overly permissive policies but doesn't generate replacement policies based on usage. Option D identifies wildcard policies but requires manual CloudTrail analysis.

stem: A company uses CloudFormation to deploy EKS clusters and needs to run kubectl commands as part of the stack deployment to create Kubernetes resources (namespaces, RBAC roles, ConfigMaps). CloudFormation doesn't natively support Kubernetes resource creation. Which approach deploys Kubernetes resources through CloudFormation?

options.text: Deploy Helm charts containing the Kubernetes resources using a CloudFormation custom resource that invokes the Helm CLI. The custom resource Lambda installs Helm, authenticates to the EKS cluster, and runs helm install to create the namespaces, RBAC roles, and ConfigMaps from the chart.

Add a CodeBuild project as a CloudFormation resource that runs kubectl commands after the EKS cluster is created. The CodeBuild buildspec configures kubeconfig and creates Kubernetes resources. Use DependsOn to ensure the CodeBuild project runs after the cluster is fully provisioned.
